title: PENGARUH PENGUNGKAPAN ESG, PROFITABILITAS, DAN LEVERAGE TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN DENGAN KUALITAS LABA SEBAGAI VARIABEL MEDIASI
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh Pengungkapan Lingkungan, Sosial, dan Tata Kelola (ESG), Profitabilitas, dan Leverage terhadap Nilai Perusahaan dengan Kualitas Laba sebagai variabel mediasi pada perusahaan non-keuangan yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) selama periode 2023–2025. Meningkatnya penerapan praktik bisnis berkelanjutan dan perhatian investor terhadap kinerja ESG telah mendorong perusahaan untuk meningkatkan transparansi dan akuntabilitas dalam pelaporan keuangan maupun non-keuangan. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kuantitatif dengan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan tahunan, laporan keberlanjutan, dan laporan keuangan perusahaan-perusahaan terpilih. Sampel ditentukan melalui purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria tertentu, sehingga menghasilkan perusahaan-perusahaan yang secara konsisten mempublikasikan informasi ESG dan keuangan secara lengkap selama periode pengamatan. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) untuk menguji hubungan langsung maupun tidak langsung di antara variabel-variabel tersebut. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa Pengungkapan ESG dan Profitabilitas memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan, sedangkan Leverage memiliki pengaruh negatif dan signifikan terhadap Nilai Perusahaan. Selain itu, Kualitas Laba ditemukan berperan sebagai mediator parsial dalam hubungan antara Pengungkapan ESG dan Nilai Perusahaan, yang menunjukkan bahwa perusahaan dengan praktik ESG yang lebih baik cenderung menghasilkan informasi laba berkualitas lebih tinggi, yang meningkatkan kepercayaan investor dan menaikkan valuasi pasar. Hasil ini mendukung teori sinyal dan teori pemangku kepentingan, yang menekankan bahwa praktik bisnis berkelanjutan dan pelaporan keuangan yang transparan berkontribusi pada penciptaan nilai perusahaan dalam jangka panjang. Studi ini memberikan implikasi praktis bagi manajemen, investor, dan regulator dalam mendorong implementasi ESG serta meningkatkan kualitas laba guna memperkuat nilai perusahaan di pasar modal Indonesia.

title: Effects of Institutional Ownership, Independent Commissioners, and CSR Disclosure on ROA: the Moderating Role of Green Credit in Indonesian Conventional Banks
summary: Increasing commitment to sustainable finance has encouraged banks to strengthen corporate governance, improve the transparency of corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure, and expand environmentally responsible lending practices. Although previous studies have examined the associations of institutional ownership, independent commissioners, and CSR disclosure with financial performance, their findings remain mixed. Moreover, empirical evidence on the moderating role of green credit in these relationships remains limited, particularly among Indonesian conventional commercial banks. This study examines the associations of institutional ownership, independent commissioners, and CSR disclosure with bank financial performance and investigates the moderating role of green credit. Using a balanced panel dataset of 176 firm-year observations from 16 conventional commercial banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2014–2024, the study employs the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) to examine the direct associations and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) to assess the moderating role of green credit. The findings show that institutional ownership (β = 0.028, p = 0.022), independent commissioners (β = 0.019, p = 0.037), and CSR disclosure (β = 0.022, p = 0.033) are positively and significantly associated with return on assets (ROA). Green credit also significantly moderates the associations of institutional ownership (β = 0.047, p = 0.019), independent commissioners (β = 0.039, p = 0.027), and CSR disclosure (β = 0.062, p = 0.008) with ROA. The inclusion of green credit and its interaction terms increases the model's explanatory power from R² = 0.45 to R² = 0.61. These findings provide empirical evidence that governance mechanisms, CSR disclosure, and green credit are associated with bank financial performance and extend the application of Agency Theory and Stakeholder Theory within the sustainable finance context. The findings also offer practical considerations for regulators, policymakers, and bank managers regarding governance quality, CSR disclosure, and the development of green financing practices.

title: The Impact of Green Banking, Corporate Governance, and CSR on Financial Performance: Evidence from KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 Banks in Indonesia
summary: Financial performance reflects a bank's operational efficiency and systemic stability. Following regulatory shifts under POJK No. 12/POJK.03/2021, KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 banks face pressures to integrate sustainability and governance into their business models. This study investigates the impact of Green Banking, Corporate Governance, and Corporate Social Responsibility on banking financial performance. Using a quantitative causal approach, secondary data were gathered from annual and sustainability reports of KBMI 3 and KBMI 4 banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange from 2020 to 2024. The population comprised 16 banking firms, and a full sampling method yielded 80 observations. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model via EViews 14. The results demonstrate that Green Banking, measured by the Green Banking Disclosure Index, has a positive and significant effect on Return on Assets. Corporate Governance, proxied by Board Gender Diversity, shows no significant effect on financial performance. Conversely, Corporate Social Responsibility, measured by the CSR expenditure ratio, has a negative and significant effect on Return on Assets. These findings highlight that green disclosure enhances efficiency and stakeholder trust, whereas short-term CSR expenses act as direct operational costs

title: The role of fintech and digital transformation in enhancing customer satisfaction: Mediating evidence from service quality in online transportation
summary: This study examines the influence of digital transformation and financial technology (fintech) on customer satisfaction in online transportation services in Indonesia, with service quality as a mediating variable. The study focuses on explaining how technological capabilities are translated into customer satisfaction through perceived service quality. The findings indicate that both digital transformation and fintech have positive and significant effects on customer satisfaction and service quality. Service quality also has a positive and significant effect on customer satisfaction and mediates the relationships between digital transformation, fintech, and customer satisfaction. These findings suggest that technological innovation creates greater customer value when it is translated into reliable, responsive, and customer-oriented service experiences. The novelty of this study lies in integrating digital transformation and fintech within a single mediation framework, positioning service quality as the mechanism linking technological capabilities to customer satisfaction. The study highlights the importance of complementing technological investment with improvements in service reliability, system responsiveness, transaction security, and overall customer experience to support sustainable customer satisfaction in online transportation services.

title: THE ROLE OF DIGITAL TRANSFORMATION IN IMPROVING MANAGEMENT EFFICIENCY IN UZBEKISTAN
summary: Digital transformation has become an important factor influencing the development of modern management systems. The rapid development of information technologies, digital platforms, artificial intelligence and electronic services is changing the way organizations plan, communicate, make decisions and evaluate performance. For Uzbekistan, digital transformation is particularly significant because the country is implementing large-scale reforms aimed at modernizing public administration, supporting entrepreneurship and developing a digital economy. This study examines the role of digital transformation in improving management efficiency in Uzbekistan. It focuses on the relationship between digital technologies, decision-making, organizational processes, employee skills and performance management. The study also identifies major challenges, including insufficient digital skills, uneven adoption of technologies and the need for better coordination between institutions. The research concludes that successful digital transformation requires not only technological infrastructure but also effective management, qualified human resources, organizational readiness and continuous evaluation of results.

title: Catering to climate-conscious investors: Does investor climate concern induce corporate greenwashing?
summary: Purpose As climate risks intensify, investors increasingly incorporate climate considerations into capital market decisions, making investor climate concern an important external governance force. However, prior research offers conflicting views on whether such concern disciplines firms toward substantive environmental action or incentivizes symbolic responses such as greenwashing. Existing studies mainly emphasize regulatory pressure or media scrutiny and pay limited attention to investor-driven governance in interactive disclosure settings. Our study aims to examine whether and how investor climate concern induces corporate greenwashing, and to clarify the governance mechanisms and boundary conditions through which investor scrutiny shapes firms' environmental disclosure strategies. Design/methodology/approach Using a sample of Chinese A-share listed firms from 2008 to 2022, we investigate the impact of investor climate concern on corporate greenwashing. The primary dataset is drawn from the textual content of question-and-answer sessions at earnings communication conferences, which include discussions on climate change, green development, and environmental disclosure strategies. Findings The results show that firms are more likely to engage in greenwashing when the level of investor climate concern is higher, particularly when such concern focuses on pollution control, ecological protection, energy efficiency and low-carbon development. Executive green awareness serves as a mediating factor in this relationship. Further analysis shows that the structural content of investor climate concern, the frequency of investor–management interactions, and the tone of investor questions all significantly influence corporate behavior. Specifically, broader investor concern, more detailed managerial responses, and a more negative tone in investor questioning are each associated with a lower likelihood of greenwashing. The effect of investor climate concern on corporate greenwashing is particularly pronounced among firms in non-heavy-polluting industries, non-asset-intensive firms, firms with higher-quality environmental disclosure, and firms with lower levels of earnings management. Moreover, stronger internal governance mechanisms can effectively suppress greenwashing behavior under the pressure of investor climate concern. Originality/value Our study extends the greenwashing literature by introducing investor climate concern as a distinct external governance force shaping firms' environmental disclosure strategies, complementing the existing focus on regulation, media scrutiny, and market discipline. It broadens the investor attention literature by moving beyond asset pricing and market reactions to examine micro-level behavioral consequences for corporate environmental conduct. By leveraging interactive question-and-answer texts from earnings communication conferences, the study offers a novel, real-time measure of investor climate concern, providing a sharper lens through which to capture investor pressure and its governance implications.

title: Does Market Competition Reduce Corporate Environmental Investment? Evidence From China's Anti‐Monopoly Law
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines whether stronger competition supports or constrains corporate environmental responsibility, using China's 2008 Anti‐Monopoly Law as a quasi‐natural experiment. Applying a difference‐in‐differences design to Chinese A‐share listed firms in heavily polluting industries from 2006 to 2019, we find that firms with high preexisting monopoly power significantly reduced environmental investment after the law's implementation. The evidence is consistent with three mechanisms: intensified competition redirected resources toward market defence, reduced monopoly rents weakened the financial slack available for environmental initiatives and greater antitrust scrutiny discouraged interfirm environmental cooperation. The negative effect is stronger in weaker institutional environments and among more vulnerable firms, and the law is also associated with reduced environmental disclosure. These findings reveal an unintended sustainability consequence of antitrust enforcement and suggest that competition policy should be coordinated with clearer environmental exemptions, targeted green finance and institutional safeguards that help firms maintain environmental commitments under competitive pressure.

title: Transformasi Digital dalam Akuntansi Keuangan: Systematic Literature Review Menggunakan Pendekatan PRISMA
summary: Aim: This study aims to analyze the development of digital transformation in financial accounting, identify dominant technologies and research themes, and explore research gaps in the field of digital transformation in financial accounting. Method: This study employs a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach guided by the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 framework. The data consist of scientific articles obtained from Scopus, ScienceDirect, SpringerLink, Emerald Insight, Google Scholar, and other scholarly sources. A total of 18 articles published between 2017 and 2026 met the inclusion criteria and were analyzed using content analysis with a thematic analysis approach. Results: The findings indicate that blockchain is the most dominant technology in the transformation of financial accounting due to its contribution to transparency, accountability, financial reporting quality, and fraud mitigation. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and automation also play important roles in improving the efficiency of accounting and auditing processes and supporting data-driven decision-making. However, existing research remains largely dominated by conceptual and literature-based studies, while empirical research examining the implementation of digital technologies in accounting practices remains relatively limited. Conclusion/Novelty/Implications: The novelty of this study lies in systematically mapping dominant technologies and research themes while identifying empirical research gaps. The findings imply that future research should integrate technology, governance, regulation, cybersecurity, and human resource competencies to support effective and sustainable digital transformation in financial accounting.

title: Pengaruh Transformasi Digital dan Proporsi Komisaris Independen terhadap Kualitas Pelaporan ESG pada Perusahaan ESG Quality 45 IDX KEHATI
summary: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) reporting in Indonesia continues to grow significantly in quantity, but this increase has not been fully accompanied by adequate sustainability information quality. Many companies have disclosed ESG information, yet the disclosures remain general and do not fully reflect transparency and substantive sustainability information. This study aims to analyze the effect of digital transformation and the proportion of independent commissioners on ESG reporting quality in companies included in the ESG Quality 45 IDX KEHATI during 2021–2024. The population consisted of all companies listed in the ESG Quality 45 IDX KEHATI index during the observation period. The sampling technique used purposive sampling, resulting in 88 observations. The study employed secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports. A quantitative approach with panel data regression analysis was applied. The results indicate that digital transformation and the proportion of independent commissioners have a significant positive effect on ESG reporting quality. These findings suggest that digital technology improves the effectiveness of sustainability data management and corporate information transparency, while independent commissioners strengthen the oversight function in ESG reporting practices. The study concludes that digital transformation and the proportion of independent commissioners are important factors in improving corporate ESG reporting quality and provides practical implications for companies and regulators in strengthening ESG implementation and reporting standards in Indonesia.

title: Moral hyperactivity in corporations: is corporate governance the solution?
summary: Until recently, moral hyperactivity in US corporate settings has primarily gone unnoticed in academic research. This is in large part due to the closed-door secrecy of the inner workings of corporate governance. Currently, when examining moral hyperactivity, academic literature primarily does so in the context of moralism’s impact on society. Additionally, corporate governance academic literature focuses on corporate theory, case law, and measurable data, largely ignoring the impact corporate managers personal ideologies’ can have on their employees. The purpose of this dissertation is to define moral hyperactivity in corporations and to determine the mitigating factors within corporate governance that allow employers to impose their moral ideology on employees. The research will address five key aims: (1) To determine why moral hyperactivity occurs in corporations and how it impacts employees. (2) To examine the literature on corporate policies that qualify as moral hyperactivity and examine how corporate governance leads to abuses of power by managers. (3) To identify the impact corporate personhood has had on corporate governance and discuss why personhood is often identified as the cause for expanding corporations’ ability to claim Constitutional protections and allow religious beliefs to influence corporate policies. (4) To discuss how existing corporate governance and shareholder primacy facilitates moral hyperactivity and how anti-discrimination laws and labor laws have failed to effectively protect employees. (5) To outline changes that could address this phenomenon in corporations. Currently, corporate managers’ moral imposition on employees goes unchecked due to a lack of effective monitoring and oversight from corporate boards. This allows managers to implement policies and practices on employees with the goal of forcing employees to conform to a specific moral ideology. Employees have little recourse due to a lack of representation in the corporation and a gap within existing laws that fails to account for moral hyperactivity from employers. This dissertation will recommend corporations begin to shift away from shareholder primacy and towards stakeholder primacy. Additionally, it will recommend the board become more active in its monitoring of managerial interactions with employees and utilize non-financial key performance indicators, such as employee satisfaction, to assess managers’ performance within the corporation. Finally, it will suggest different models of codetermination as a blueprint for the US to implement codetermination into its current corporate structures.

title: Coordinating Technological Change, Ener-gy-System Transformation and Inclusive De-velopment in the Transition to a Low-Carbon Economy
summary: The transition toward low-carbon development requires simultaneous transformation of energy supply, energy demand and the institutional structures that govern technological and economic change. This paper examines the relationships among renewable-energy deployment, energy efficiency and economy-wide decarbonization through a structured review of recent literature. The first dimension highlights technological learning, declining renewable costs, policy credibility, financing conditions, grid integration and storage as major determinants of renewable-energy expansion. The second focuses on energy efficiency, rebound effects, electrification, behavioral responses, digitalization and demand-side flexibility, showing that technical improvements do not automatically translate into proportional reductions in energy consumption or emissions. The third considers the broader development implications of energy transition through economic growth, green innovation, climate finance, corporate transformation and energy justice. The literature indicates that renewable energy and efficiency can reinforce economic and environmental performance when they are supported by stable policies, adequate infrastructure, technological innovation and appropriate financial mechanisms. However, successful decarbonization also depends on structural changes in industry, transport, buildings and consumption patterns. Moreover, distributional consequences must be integrated into transition strategies to ensure that environmental gains are accompanied by employment opportunities, affordability and social inclusion. Low-carbon development should therefore be approached as a coordinated technological, economic and institutional transformation rather than as the simple substitution of fossil fuels by renewable energy.

title: Research transitions in sustainable agricultural finance during the voluntary sustainability period
summary: Abstract Sustainable agricultural finance (SAF) supports the achievement of SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 13 (Climate Action), and SDG 1 (No Poverty) by promoting inclusive, resilient, and sustainable farming systems. Although SAF has gained growing attention, the literature remains fragmented and focused only on specific themes such as climate finance, rural credit, green investment, financial inclusion, and risk management in agriculture. There is a lack of comprehensive studies examining its overall intellectual structure, publication trends, key contributors, thematic evolution, bibliometric performance, and global collaboration patterns as a unified research field. Therefore, we performed a bibliometric analysis of literature in the field in Scopus database. Articles were searched using a TITLE-ABS-KEY search. The time period selected was Jan 2015 to february 2026. We included 155 documents in the analysis using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer. The selection was in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines and pre-defined inclusion and exclusion criteria for subject area, language, and document type. The most popular affiliation was Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST), Ghana. Core journals such as Sustainability (Switzerland) had significant reach. Author productivity was highly dispersed, indicating that SAF remains an emerging research field. The pattern of coupling pointed to China as the leading knowledge centre, and there is a strong global intellectual connectivity that dictates the advancement of SAF research. The thematic map indicates blockchain, ESG, and credit risk as possible directions for future studies, but these aspects are still developing. In brief, the findings indicate a growing scholarly focus on financing for climate resilience, resource efficiency, environmental sustainability and sustainable agricultural transformation.

title: From digital transformation to humanitarian supply chain resilience: A capability-based model of adaptive control and entrepreneurial action
summary: Digital systems can give humanitarian organizations faster and more detailed information about needs, inventory, transport, suppliers, and delivery. That information is useful, but it does not by itself make an operation resilient. Someone must decide what the information means, which priorities should change, and who may act when an established plan no longer fits conditions on the ground. This article develops a conceptual explanation of that problem. It brings together research on dynamic capabilities, enabling management control, organizational support, corporate entrepreneurship, and humanitarian supply-chain resilience. The argument has two parts. Adaptive management control links digital information to decisions, resource commitments, and review. Entrepreneurial action allows employees and local partners to develop workable alternatives when normal routines fail. The two capabilities are expected to reinforce each other. Control that leaves no room for judgement can slow a response, whereas local initiative without shared priorities can create duplication and weaken accountability. Seven propositions describe the proposed relationships, their limits, and conditions under which they may reverse. The article also sets out measures and research designs that could disconfirm the propositions. Its main contribution is to explain why similar digital investments may produce different operational results across humanitarian organizations. Keywords: Digital Transformation Capability, Humanitarian Supply Chains, Adaptive Management Control, Enabling Control, Corporate Entrepreneurship, Organizational Support, Resilience, Humanitarian Operational Performance.

title: Peran Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) terhadap Tax Avoidance dengan Board Gender Diversity sebagai Variabel Pemoderasi
summary: This study is intended to investigate and evaluate the influence of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) principles on tax avoidance practices among companies operating in the coal production sub-industry within the energy sector that are listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, covering the observation period from 2022 to 2024, while also taking into account the role of board-level gender diversity as a moderating variable in that relationship. This study is driven by the critical role that tax revenues play in supporting government financing, alongside the persistent indications of tax avoidance behavior, particularly within sectors that make substantial contributions to corporate income tax receipts. Simultaneously, the growing emphasis on ESG principles has encouraged corporations to operate with greater transparency and accountability across all aspects of their business conduct, including matters related to taxation. Furthermore, the presence of gender diversity within a company's board of directors is regarded as a factor capable of elevating the quality of both decision-making processes and supervisory functions, which in turn may have a meaningful bearing on a company's inclination to engage in tax avoidance practices. Panel data regression analysis was employed in this study with support from Stata to evaluate the association among variables, including the influence of the moderating variable on the proposed relationship under study. Overall, the results indicate that although ESG does not directly affect tax avoidance, the presence of women on the board of directors significantly alters the relationship by weakening the effect of ESG on tax avoidance practices

title: CEO Behavioral Traits and Firm Value During Market Uncertainty: A Structured Literature Review
summary: CEO behavioral characteristics have attracted increasing attention in the corporate governance literature because they influence strategic decision-making and firm value, particularly under conditions of market uncertainty. However, prior studies on CEO overconfidence and CEO narcissism have produced inconsistent findings and provide limited understanding of the mechanisms linking these traits to firm value. This study aims to synthesize how CEO overconfidence and CEO narcissism influence firm value under market uncertainty from the perspective of the Behavioral Theory of the Firm (BTOF). A Structured Literature Review (SLR) was conducted following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Articles were identified through systematic searches of the Scopus and ScienceDirect databases. After identification, screening, eligibility assessment, and quality appraisal, 71 articles were included in the final review. The findings indicate that the influence of CEO behavioral traits on firm value operates indirectly through five strategic mechanisms: (1) risk taking and strategic change; (2) financial policy and resource allocation; (3) governance, disclosure, and monitoring; (4) ESG and stakeholder management; and (5) innovation and strategic renewal. Risk taking and strategic change emerged as the most dominant mechanism. Furthermore, the effects of CEO overconfidence and CEO narcissism on firm value are highly contextual and may generate either positive or negative outcomes depending on organizational and environmental conditions. This study develops an integrated framework explaining the pathways through which CEO behavioral traits affect firm value and extends the Behavioral Theory of the Firm by clarifying strategic decision-making processes under uncertainty.

title: Transmission of green pressure: customer digitisation and supplier green innovation from the perspective of supply chain spillover
summary: Understanding the green enabling role of digitalisation in supply chains holds important theoretical and practical significance for promoting corporate green transformation. Using data from Chinese A-share listed companies spanning 2010–2023, this study examines the impact of customer digitalisation on supplier green innovation. The results show that customer digitalisation significantly improves both the quantity and quality of supplier green innovation, and this spillover effect is asymmetric. Mechanism analyses reveal that this effect operates through three pathways – psychological empowerment, structural empowerment, and resource empowerment. Heterogeneity analyses show that the effect is more pronounced when customer and supplier firms share the same ownership type or operate in industries with similar pollution characteristics, while heterogeneity in customers’ own digitalisation levels does not significantly affect the transmission. In addition, customer digitalisation drives supplier green innovation primarily through increased factor inputs rather than efficiency improvements. Further analyses indicate that customer digitalisation significantly stimulates suppliers’ independent innovation, but its effect on collaborative innovation is insignificant. By uncovering the underlying mechanisms, boundary conditions, and organisational modes through which digitalisation fosters green innovation, this study extends the literature on supply chain digitalisation and green innovation governance.

title: ESG and Financial Risk: Does AI Innovation Strengthen the Relationship?
summary: This study aims to examine the impact of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance on a firm’s financial risk and to explore the moderating role of Artificial intelligence (AI) innovation. This research uses a quantitative approach with secondary data from Indonesia companies listed on Indonesia Stock Exchange for the period 2018 – 2024, resulting in 340 observations. The firm financial risk is measured using Altman Z-Score and Zmijewski X-Score, while the analysis is conducted using panel regression with fixed effects. The results show that ESG performance does not have a significant effect on financial stability as measured by Z-Score, suggesting that the financial benefits of implementing ESG might not be immediately visible in the short-term. However, ESG significantly reduces financial distress risk as measured by the X-Score, indicating that stronger ESG practices increase financial resilience. AI innovation contributes to improving financial outcomes, but does not consistently strengthen them. Overall, this study concludes that ESG performance supported by AI innovation has the potential to lower financial distress. This study contributes to the growing sustainability finance literature by providing empirical evidence from an emerging market on how ESG performance and AI innovation jointly influence firm financial risk.

title: Impacts of Emergency Trust on Branders’ Corporate Social Responsibility Information Disclosure Decisions Under Emergency Context
summary: In emergency procurement, information asymmetry over suppliers’ CSR levels intertwines with governmental emergency-trust behavior, profoundly shaping branders’ CSR investment and signaling decisions. We construct a signaling game between government and brander: the brander privately observes the supplier’s true CSR type, while the government updates beliefs from CSR investment and wholesale price to set procurement price, exhibiting emergency trust toward high-CSR chains. Characterizing pooling, downward-distorted separating, and undistorted separating equilibria, and refining overlapping multiple equilibria via the LMSE criterion, we find that equilibrium strategies are driven by CSR supply uncertainty. Under low uncertainty, branders pool to conceal true types; at moderate levels, low-type branders distort CSR downward to deter imitation and separate; under high uncertainty, both types reach undistorted separating equilibria, where CSR investment becomes an effective signal for accurate identification. The emergency-trust coefficient positively incentivizes CSR investment, wholesale price, and governmental utility price, fostering a virtuous cycle enhancing emergency capacity. Information sharing significantly raises CSR investment and bilateral payoffs. Decisions under undistorted separating equilibria coincide exactly with those under information sharing, indicating that voluntary truthful disclosure eliminates signal costs and achieves win-win outcomes. This research offers theoretical foundations and managerial implications for CSR disclosure design and governmental procurement policy.

title: Enterprise Supply Chain Resilience Through SAP-Integrated Production Scheduling and Procurement Optimization
summary: Enterprise supply chains increasingly require integrated mechanisms for coordinating production scheduling, procurement decisions, and disruption response. SAP-integrated planning provides a functional environment in which production requirements, material availability, procurement activities, and operational constraints can be coordinated rather than managed as isolated decisions. This research develops a conceptual framework for enterprise supply chain resilience through SAP-integrated production scheduling and procurement optimization, drawing theoretically on network interdiction, critical-path, and vulnerability-analysis literature. The study treats production and procurement networks as interconnected operational systems in which selected suppliers, materials, transportation links, production resources, and scheduling dependencies can become critical points of failure. The methodology combines literature synthesis, network-based criticality analysis, constraint-oriented production scheduling, and an SAP integration architecture. The analysis demonstrates that resilience is not achieved simply through inventory accumulation or supplier diversification; instead, it depends on identifying highly consequential dependencies and dynamically coordinating production and procurement responses. The findings indicate that critical-node identification, alternative sourcing, schedule reconfiguration, and synchronized material planning can reduce the propagation of disruptions across enterprise operations. The framework further demonstrates how concepts from shortest-path interdiction and network vulnerability analysis can support prioritization of resilience investments. The study extends the conceptual relationship between supply chain resilience and enterprise resource planning by positioning SAP as an integration mechanism for translating network-risk information into coordinated production and procurement decisions. Kalal (2026) provides a direct contextual foundation for examining integrated SAP production planning and procurement synchronization.

title: The Role of Digitalized Accounting Information Systems in Preparing Financial Reports of Pontianak MSMES
summary: This study aims to analyze the role of digital Accounting Information Systems (AIS) in the preparation of financial statements for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Pontianak City, identify the challenges encountered during implementation, and examine the efforts undertaken by MSME actors to overcome these challenges. This research employs a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collected through interviews, observations, and documentation involving MSME owners in Pontianak City. The findings indicate that the implementation of digital AIS, including Microsoft Excel and web-based accounting applications, contributes to improving the accuracy, effectiveness, and efficiency of financial recording processes. Digital AIS also supports MSME actors in preparing more structured financial reports and making better business decisions. However, the adoption of digital AIS remains limited due to several obstacles, such as low levels of digital literacy, insufficient accounting knowledge, difficulties in adapting to technological changes, and the continued preference for manual recording systems. To address these challenges, MSME actors make efforts through independent learning, exploring digital accounting tools, and gradually adapting to technology-based financial management systems. This study highlights the importance of strengthening digital and accounting competencies to encourage more effective financial management among MSMEs.

title: Pengaruh Board Size, Board Tenure, Independent Commissioners dan Audit Committee terhadap ESG Score LQ45
summary: This study examines the effect of board size, board tenure, independent commissioners, and audit committee on ESG Score among LQ45 companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020-2024. The research is motivated by the increasing relevance of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) information in capital-market decision making and the wide variation of ESG Score among highly liquid and large-capitalization firms. The population consists of 71 LQ45 constituent companies observed during the study period. Using purposive sampling, 24 companies met the criteria of consistently publishing annual reports and having complete ESG Score data from Refinitiv/LSEG, producing 120 firm-year observations. This study applies a quantitative causal-associative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports, sustainability reports, and Refinitiv/LSEG. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 12 after model selection and classical assumption testing. The Chow and Hausman tests indicate that the Fixed Effect Model is the most appropriate model. The results show that board size, board tenure, independent commissioners, and audit committee simultaneously have a significant effect on ESG Score. Partially, board tenure has a positive and significant effect on ESG Score, while board size, independent commissioners, and audit committee have no significant effect. The adjusted R-squared value of 0.882250 indicates that 88.23% of ESG Score variation is explained by the model. The findings imply that accumulated board experience is more relevant than the mere number of governance organs in strengthening corporate ESG score.

title: Managerial Discretion and Corporate Social Responsibility among Manufacturing Firms in Uganda: A Relative Importance Analysis
summary: Corporate social responsibility is key for firm sustainability since. The currenmt study seeks to establish the influence of managerial discretion on corporate social responsibility. Specific dimensions of managerial discretion that most powerfully drive Corporate social responsibility are not empirically tested. Prior studies treat managerial discretion as a composite, unidimensional construct, thereby obscuring which specific dimension of decision-making autonomy or internal organizational factors exerts the greatest influence on CSR. Using Relative Weights Analysis, this study examined the dimension-specific effects of managerial discretion on corporate social responsibility. A cross-sectional quantitative survey design was adopted. Data were collected from 314 medium and large manufacturing firms in Uganda using a structured self-administered questionnaire. Hierarchical regression analysis tested the dimension-specific hypotheses, and Relative Weights Analysis (RWA) was subsequently employed to determine the precise proportional contribution of each managerial discretion dimension to total CSR variance. Both dimensions of managerial discretion positively and significantly predicted CSR. Hierarchical regression results established decision-making autonomy as the stronger predictor (β = .583, p < .001) relative to internal organizational factors (β = .354, p < .001). RWA results corroborated and refined these findings: decision-making autonomy accounted for the larger proportion of explained CSR variance (RW = 58.2%, rescaled), while internal organizational factors contributed 41.8%. This study makes a dual methodological and substantive contribution. Methodologically, it is among the first studies in the managerial discretion-CSR literature to apply RWA. The study also generates dimension-specific empirical evidence from manufacturing firms in a developing-country African context where evidence on the differential importance of managerial discretion dimensions for CSR is not yet tested.

title: Spatial Assessment of Digital Transformation in the Baltic Countries
summary: This paper presents an applied study of the level and dynamics of digital transformation in the Baltic countries (Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania) based on the proposed mposite indicator, the Baltic Digital Regional Transformation Index (BDRTI). The relevance of the study is motivated by the need for a comprehensive assessment of digital transformations in national economies, identification of structural imbalances, and determination of prospects for digital development. The aim of the study is to develop a methodological approach to the spatial assessment of digital transformation in the Baltic countries, determine their comparative positions, and identify promising trends. The methodological framework combines systemic and comparative approaches, methods of indicator normalization and aggregation, expert assessment, and trend forecasting. For a comprehensive assessment, four sub-indices were constructed: Business Digitalization, Digital Human Capital, Digital Infrastructure, and Innovation Capacity. The weights were derived from an expert survey of specialists in the digital economy, digital transformation, innovation development, and economic research, using the Saaty method and checking the consistency of expert judgments. The BDRTI was calculated for 2015, 2017, 2019, 2021, 2023, and 2025, which enabled assessment of the dynamics of digital development and comparison of the countries under study. The results demonstrated a steady increase in the BDRTI in all three countries. In 2025, the highest index value was recorded in Lithuania (0.516), followed by Estonia (0.490) and Latvia (0.429). Meanwhile, Latvia recorded the largest increase over the period 2015–2025, at 106.2%, identifying it as the country with the most pronounced catching-up dynamics. Estonia retains leading positions in Digital Infrastructure and Human Capital, whereas Lithuania’s key advantage is Business Digitalization. A shared structural weakness for all three countries remains the low level of Innovation Capacity, which indicates a gap between the existing digital potential and its transformation into innovation outcomes. Trend forecasting confirms the continuation of the positive BDRTI dynamics. For 2027, the forecast values are 0.501 for Estonia, 0.479 for Latvia, and 0.606 for Lithuania. The findings confirm that the BDRTI is a suitable tool for the comprehensive assessment of digital transformation. The practical significance of the study lies in the applicability of the proposed index to monitoring digital development, identify structural imbalances, determine digital policy priorities, and support strategic directions for the innovative development of the Baltic countries.

title: Upstream patent contestability and downstream digital transformation
summary: Digital transformation increasingly depends on firms’ positions and relationships within production networks. This study examines whether upstream innovation competition promotes downstream firms’ digital transformation by exploiting supplier patent invalidation as a quasi-experimental shock to suppliers’ technological market power. Combining supplier–customer links, patent invalidation events, and financial data for Chinese A-share listed firms, we estimate staggered difference-in-differences models. The results show that supplier patent invalidation significantly increases downstream firms’ digital transformation, with larger effects when more patents, particularly invention patents, are invalidated. Channel analyses provide evidence consistent with two pathways. First, patent invalidation weakens supplier bargaining power, reduces downstream prepayments, expands trade credit, and increases downstream markups, thereby releasing resources for digital investment. Second, downstream firms restructure their supply chains by maintaining fewer supplier relationships and shifting toward suppliers with stronger digital capabilities. The effect is stronger for firms facing tighter financing constraints, greater supplier concentration, and higher asset specificity. These findings identify upstream innovation competition as a supply-side driver of corporate digital transformation and extend evidence on the economic consequences of patent institutions to interfirm production networks.

title: CSR, CEO Characteristics, Prudence, And Earnings Management: The Moderating Role of GCG
summary: This study aims to examine the moderating role of Good Corporate Governance (GCG) in the relationship between Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), CEO characteristics, prudence, and earnings management in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2020–2023 period. This research employs a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports. A total of 31 companies were selected as samples through purposive sampling. Data analysis was conducted using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS version 3. The findings indicate that CSR and prudence are negatively associated with earnings management, whereas CEO characteristics do not exhibit a statistically significant direct association. Furthermore, the findings indicate a statistically significant moderating association between GCG and the relationship between CEO characteristics and earnings management (β = –0.219, p = 0.039). In contrast, the moderating effects of GCG on the relationships between CSR and earnings management and between prudence and earnings management are not statistically significant. The originality of this study lies in the integration of CSR, CEO characteristics, prudence, and GCG into a comprehensive research framework within the post-pandemic Indonesian manufacturing context. Previous studies have predominantly examined these variables separately, thereby failing to explain governance effectiveness based on the source of opportunistic managerial behavior being monitored. This study contributes to the literature on corporate governance and earnings management and provides practical implications for strengthening governance practices and improving the sustainability of financial reporting quality.

title: Readiness and Acceptance of Accounting Information Systems for Financial Reporting in Indonesian Village-Owned Enterprises: A TRAM Approach
summary: Despite the growing adoption of digital accounting applications, there is limited evidence on how technology readiness influences the acceptance of accounting information systems within village-owned enterprises. This study examines the readiness and acceptance of accounting information systems used for financial reporting in Indonesian village-owned enterprises, using the Technology Readiness and Acceptance Model (TRAM). Data were collected through an online survey of personnel from village-owned enterprises involved in financial reporting and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that perceived usefulness is the strongest determinant of intention to use accounting information systems. Optimism positively influences perceived usefulness, while innovativeness positively affects perceived ease of use. Interestingly, insecurity also positively affects perceived usefulness, suggesting that concerns about data security, transaction reliability, and information accuracy may increase users’ appreciation of accounting applications. In contrast, perceived ease of use does not significantly influence intention to use. These findings indicate that technology adoption in village-owned enterprises is driven primarily by perceived practical benefits rather than operational simplicity. The study extends the application of TRAM to village-owned enterprises and suggests that technology readiness may operate differently in accountability-oriented rural organizations. Practically, adoption initiatives should emphasize the benefits of accounting applications for reporting quality, efficiency, and accountability.

title: Pengaruh Corporate Governance terhadap Sustainability Report pada Perusahaan Sektor Energi dan Pertambangan yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2022-2024
summary: The increasing demand for corporate transparency regarding environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices has encouraged companies to improve the quality of sustainability reporting. However, previous studies have reported inconsistent findings regarding the role of corporate governance in sustainability report disclosure, particularly in environmentally sensitive industries. This study aims to examine the influence of corporate governance on sustainability report disclosure in energy and mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2024 period. A quantitative associative approach was employed using secondary data obtained from annual reports and sustainability reports. The sample consisted of 16 companies selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 48 firm-year observations. Sustainability report disclosure was measured using the Global Reporting Initiative (GRI) disclosure index, while corporate governance was represented by the board of commissioners, independent commissioners, and the audit committee. Multiple linear regression analysis was applied to test the proposed relationships. The findings indicate that corporate governance variables jointly have a significant effect on sustainability report disclosure. Partially, only the audit committee demonstrates a positive and significant influence, whereas the board of commissioners and independent commissioners do not show significant effects. These findings highlight the importance of an effective audit committee in strengthening corporate transparency and accountability in sustainability reporting within the energy and mining sectors.

title: AI-Based Inventory Management and Operational Efficiency
summary: Abstract The increasing complexity and dynamism of global supply chains have rendered traditional inventory management approaches insufficient for meeting contemporary operational demands. Artificial intelligence (AI) offers transformative capabilities for inventory optimization through enhanced demand forecasting, automated replenishment, cost reduction, and supply chain resilience. This paper examines the integration of AI technologies in inventory management and their impact on operational efficiency through a systematic literature review and analysis of real-world case studies. The findings reveal that machine learning and deep learning models substantially outperform traditional statistical methods in demand prediction accuracy, particularly for intermittent and volatile demand patterns. AI-driven automated replenishment systems reduce stockouts and excess inventory, while predictive analytics enable proactive risk mitigation. Case analyses of Amazon, Walmart, and Zara demonstrate that organizations leveraging AI achieve measurable improvements in inventory turnover, waste reduction, and supply chain responsiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of implementation challenges and future research directions, including the potential of generative AI and digital twin technologies.

title: Pengaruh Firm Size, Capital Intentisy dan Corporate Social Responsibility terhadap Agresivitas Pajak
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of Firm Size, Capital Intensity, and Corporate Social Responsibility on Tax Aggressiveness. The sample consists of Consumer Non-Cyclical sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. Data were obtained from financial statements and annual reports. Purposive sampling was employed, resulting in 12 companies observed over five years, yielding 60 firm-year observations. Panel data regression analysis was conducted using EViews 12 software. The findings show that Firm Size, Capital Intensity, and Corporate Social Responsibility simultaneously influence Tax Aggressiveness. Partially, Firm Size and Capital Intensity significantly affect Tax Aggressiveness, while Corporate Social Responsibility has no significant effect. These results suggest that larger firms and those with higher capital intensity tend to engage more in tax aggressiveness, whereas CSR activities do not alter tax behavior. The study contributes to understanding determinants of tax aggressiveness in Indonesia’s Consumer Non-Cyclical sector and provides insights for policymakers, regulators, and academics.

title: Digital Disruption in Accounting and Financial Reporting: AI-Supported Decision Support and Human Judgement in the Hospitality Industry
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI), business intelligence (BI) and analytics are increasingly used in hotel accounting, financial reporting and performance management. Existing research, however, has concentrated mainly on prediction, automation and operational optimisation. Their integration with the critical interpretation of accounting information and human judgement remains less clearly developed. This study provides a structured review and bibliometric mapping of research on AI-supported accounting and financial reporting in the hospitality industry. It adopts a structured bibliometric review combining science mapping with qualitative content-oriented interpretation. The review comprises three complementary search streams addressing: (i) AI, BI and analytics in hotel accounting; (ii) AI-supported reporting, dashboards and decision-support systems; and (iii) the broader contextual literature on human judgement and the interpretation of accounting information. The results identify machine learning, revenue management, forecasting and dynamic pricing as the most prominent and structurally influential areas within the retrieved literature. Research on reporting interpretation, dashboard-based judgement, anomaly detection and human validation is more fragmented and remains weakly integrated across the mapped literature. The principal research gap therefore concerns the limited connection between AI-supported technologies, reporting outputs and human interpretive judgement, rather than the absence of relevant research in these areas. The study proposes a human-centred perspective on AI in hotel accounting and identifies future research directions in which AI supports critical interpretation, professional judgement and responsible managerial decision-making.

title: Digital Transformation and Banking Profitability: The Mediating Role of Operational Efficiency
summary: This study empirically examines how digital transformation influences bank profitability, with operational efficiency as a mediating variable, in commercial banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period. The rapid expansion of digital banking and increasing competition from fintech companies have encouraged banks to intensify technology investments, raising questions regarding whether digitalization improves profitability directly or through operational efficiency gains. Therefore, this study aims to analyze both the direct and indirect effects of digital transformation on bank profitability. Using purposive sampling, 31 banks were selected, resulting in 155 panel data observations across five years. The analysis employed panel data regression in EViews 13 while a cluster bootstrap approach with 5.000 replications was applied to evaluate the mediating effect. The findings indicate that digital transformation has a positive and significant direct effect on profitability (ROA). However, digital transformation does not significantly affect operational efficiency (BOPO), while BOPO negatively and significantly affects ROA. Furthermore, the bootstrap test confirms that operational efficiency does not mediate the relationship between digital transformation and profitability. These findings suggest that digitalization primarily enhances bank profitability through revenue expansion rather than cost efficiency.

title: ESG and Financial Data Extraction and Correlation Analysis Using Multi‐Agent LLMs on Bank Reports
summary: ABSTRACT Assessing the relationship between environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices and financial performance has become a central concern in sustainable finance. However, existing studies largely depend on commercial ESG ratings, which lack transparency and obscure the contribution of individual indicators. In addition, ESG disclosures vary substantially across institutions, years and reporting formats, making cross‐bank comparison difficult. To address these challenges, this study introduces a unified multi‐agent framework powered by large language models (LLMs) to extract ESG and financial indicators directly from banks' annual reports. The framework employs category‐specific prompt designs that enable the models to recognise synonymous terminology, differing measurement scales and inconsistent reporting units, thereby transforming heterogeneous textual disclosures into structured and comparable datasets. Applying this LLM‐based approach to hundreds of reports from approximately 50 global banks over 7 years, we construct a harmonised dataset and conduct indicator‐level correlation analyses between ESG and financial performance measures. The results reveal heterogeneous yet systematic associations between specific ESG indicators and financial outcomes, with environmental variables showing relatively stronger and more consistent correlations with return on assets (ROA) and return on equity (ROE). This study presents the first scalable, transparent and reproducible LLM‐driven framework for ESG–finance analysis based on unstructured public disclosures, offering a methodological foundation that can be extended to other industries and domains.

title: Restructuring Global Supply Chains: Navigating Challenges of the COVID-19 Pandemic and Beyond
summary: Problem definition: The COVID-19 pandemic imposed unprecedented stresses on global supply chains (GSCs), compelling companies to reassess their supply chain structures and strategies. This crisis has also heightened awareness among businesses, consumers, and policymakers about the critical importance and far-reaching implications of GSC design and management. This unique moment presents a generational opportunity for Operations Management (OM) researchers to document and understand the ongoing restructuring of GSCs. Methodology/results: By analyzing microlevel data on U.S. customs import shipments (2019–2021), we uncover shifts in GSC strategies during the COVID-19 pandemic. Firms diversified suppliers within existing sourcing locations and reallocated volumes among them. Whereas dependence on China decreased, imports from other Asian nations like India and Vietnam, as well as North American countries like Canada and Mexico, increased. Industry-specific differences were pronounced, and a notable shift toward lower-frequency, higher-quantity shipments was also observed. Managerial implications: Beyond the challenges of COVID-19, recent years have witnessed other major supply chain disruptions, due to causes such as geopolitical tensions, natural disasters, and port worker strikes. We offer actionable insights for executives designing supply chain strategies to prepare for similar disruptions as they increase in frequency and severity. We identify future research avenues aimed at enhancing the resilience and adaptability of GSCs in a continuously evolving environment. title: The Regulatory Architecture of Sustainable Development: Corporate Accountability, Legal Compliance, and the Governance of ESG Integration
summary: The governance of sustainable development has undergone a profound legal transformation as regulatory frameworks increasingly mandate corporate accountability for environmental, social, and governance performance. This article examines the evolving legal architecture governing sustainable development management, with particular focus on the European Union's Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive, Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive, and their extraterritorial implications for global business governance. Drawing upon regulatory theory, corporate governance scholarship, and comparative legal analysis, the article argues that the convergence of sustainability management with legal compliance obligations represents a paradigmatic shift in how corporations internalise sustainable development objectives. The analysis reveals that while regulatory frameworks have created unprecedented transparency and accountability mechanisms, significant challenges persist regarding enforcement consistency, jurisdictional fragmentation, and the balance between regulatory ambition and business competitiveness. The article proposes a governance model grounded in regulatory coherence, proportionate liability, and transnational regulatory convergence to harmonise sustainable development imperatives with corporate operational realities. The findings carry implications for corporate managers, compliance officers, policymakers, and scholars seeking to navigate the intersection of law and sustainable development governance.

title: BI in SMEs Boosts Competitiveness and Decision-Making
summary: Small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) face increasing pressure to enhance competitiveness through data-informed strategies in the digital economy. Business Intelligence (BI) has emerged as a critical enabler, yet the mechanisms linking its adoption to performance outcomes in resource-constrained environments remain underexplored. This qualitative systematic review synthesizes the literature on BI applications in SMEs to examine how these tools reconfigure decision-making processes, contribute to competitiveness, and generate economic value, while critically analyzing implementation realities specific to the SME context. Following the PRISMA 2020 statement, a systematic search of the Scopus database (2018–2021) yielded 2,130 records. After a dual-independent screening process, 68 studies met the inclusion criteria and were subjected to Reflexive Thematic Analysis, enabling an interpretive synthesis of the literature. The analysis reveals three overarching themes. Strategic Reconstitution of Decision-Making describes a shift from intuition to evidence-based managerial cognition, alongside a persistent perception gap where leaders underestimate their existing data assets. Duality of BI Implementation captures the tension between idealized architectural models and the pragmatic reality of SMEs, which employ entrepreneurial bricolage—using low-cost, accessible tools—a strategy that enables accessibility but risks creating competency traps. Multidimensional Impact on SME Economic Vitality encompasses quantifiable financial gains, such as cost reductions and improved financial health, and intangible strategic capabilities, including organizational agility and enhanced dynamic capabilities that underpin sustained competitive advantage. BI enables SMEs to enhance strategic decision-making and profitability; however, value realization is contingent upon the interplay between resource configurations, capability development, and managerial cognition. The integration of PRISMA with Thematic Analysis demonstrates how procedural rigor and interpretative depth can be synergistically combined in qualitative evidence synthesis.

title: Ambidextrous innovation and digital transformation
summary: Ambidextrous innovation, which strategically integrates breakthrough and incremental innovation approaches, is a critical driver of corporate digital transformation by enabling dynamic knowledge recombination and organisational learning. Using panel data from listed companies between 2009 and 2023, the results demonstrate that firms with higher ambidextrous innovation capabilities achieve significantly advanced digital transformation levels. A key theoretical contribution of this study is identifying mitigating managerial myopia, reducing debt financing costs and improving environmental, social and governance performance as synergistic mechanisms through which ambidextrous innovation fosters digital transformation. Furthermore, corporate transparency, investor discernment capability and commercial credit availability are found to positively moderate this relationship. Heterogeneity analysis reveals that the effect is more pronounced for non-SOEs, high-growth firms and those operating in more developed regional economies. These findings provide actionable insights for firms seeking to orchestrate knowledge resources in pursuit of digital transformation and offer policymakers guidance for designing innovation incentive systems tailored to diverse organisational contexts.

title: Trade Policy as Geoeconomic Statecraft: Regulatory Positioning in Vietnam’s Rare Earth Supply Chains
summary: Vietnam combines substantial reported rare earth element (REE) reserves with limited extraction and processing capacity and rising domestic demand, a configuration that makes resource-based geopolitical leverage uncertain. Existing Vietnam-focused studies describe resource potential, demand, legal reform, and external partnerships, but do not compare the evidentiary support for multiple geoeconomic instruments while explicitly separating regulatory action from demonstrated strategic effects. This study asks which of Blackwill and Harris’s seven geoeconomic instruments are traceable in a purposively constructed documentary corpus on Vietnam’s REE sector during 2018–2025 and what strategic outcomes that corpus can support. Using a qualitative single-case documentary design, it applies directed content analysis to 18 official policy, bilateral, statistical, institutional, academic, and contextual sources selected for direct relevance to state action or supply-chain outcomes and cross-checked across source types. Within this corpus, trade policy receives the strongest evidentiary support through export-eligibility rules, processing requirements, and domestic-priority provisions. Reciprocal trade agreements provide an enabling market-access framework, but no REE-specific concession deliberately deployed to elicit a geopolitical response was identified. Japan-centred trade and the 2024 formal inclusion of REEs in Vietnam–Japan critical-mineral cooperation provide externally observable evidence of continued market access and institutional recognition. However, the available pre-2021 baseline does not establish that these external options or Vietnam’s institutional standing measurably improved because of the subsequent regulatory measures. The evidence therefore supports a bounded interpretation of regulatory positioning rather than a demonstrated positional gain, and it does not show coercive leverage, partner behavioural change, or political concessions.

title: The Effect of Sales Growth, Asset Efficiency, and Capital Structure on Financial Performance with Corporate Social Responsibility as a Moderating Variable: A Study on Consumer Non-Cyclical Companies
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of sales growth, asset efficiency, and capital structure on financial performance, with corporate social responsibility (CSR) as a moderating variable in consumer non-cyclical companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) for the 2020–2024 period. The research population comprised all 131 companies in the consumer non-cyclical sector listed on the IDX. Through purposive sampling, a final sample of 15 companies was obtained, yielding 75 observations over the five-year period. Secondary data from annual financial and sustainability reports were collected using the documentation technique. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Fixed Effect Model (FEM) approach. The t-test results indicate that sales growth and asset efficiency have a significant positive effect on financial performance, while capital structure has a significant negative effect. Furthermore, the moderation analysis reveals that CSR disclosure significantly strengthens the positive impact of sales growth on financial performance but weakens the positive impact of asset efficiency on financial performance. However, CSR is unable to moderate the effect of capital structure on financial performance. The implications of this study emphasize that integrating CSR practices can serve as a strategic catalyst to optimize sales growth for sustainable financial performance.

title: Beyond Profit: Peran Corporate Social Responsibility and Business Ethics in Building Sustainable Business Performance through Strategic Planning pada UMKM
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Business Ethics on Sustainable Business Performance among culinary MSMEs producing traditional souvenirs in Jombang, East Java, with Strategic Planning as the mediating variable. The research was motivated by the tendency of culinary MSMEs to neglect social responsibility and business ethics due to the pressure of short-term profit orientation, as well as a research gap—few studies have examined the role of strategic planning as a mechanism that bridges CSR and business ethics with sustainable performance at the MSME level. The research design was quantitative-causal, employing purposive sampling of 106 SME operators under the guidance of the East Java Provincial Cooperative and SME Agency who employed at least one employee. Data were collected via a 1–5 Likert-scale questionnaire and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). The test results show that CSR and Business Ethics each have a significant positive effect on Sustainable Business Performance, both directly and through the mediation of Strategic Planning—which was found to be significant in both indirect pathways—while Strategic Planning was also found to have a significant positive direct effect on sustainable performance. This study makes a theoretical contribution to the literature on Stakeholder Theory and the Resource-Based View at the MSME level, as well as a practical contribution to the East Java Cooperative and MSME Office and culinary business operators in designing capacity-building programs that simultaneously integrate ethical, social, and strategic aspects.

title: Co‐Creation Over R&D: External Knowledge as the Engine of Green Innovation in Italian SMEs
summary: ABSTRACT The transition towards a green and net‐zero economy has become a strategic priority for firms and policymakers, placing increasing pressure on SMEs to integrate diverse forms of knowledge to achieve both environmental and economic objectives. A recurring yet not fully resolved question is whether co‐creation among demand‐ and supply‐side actors is associated with firms' environmental performance while also contributing to firm‐level economic outcomes. Drawing on survey data from 6646 Italian firms, this paper investigates the associations between co‐creation, digital technologies, government support, and green innovation. Using a CDM‐inspired two‐stage econometric framework, we find that co‐creation and external enablers are strongly associated with green innovation. Green innovation is also positively associated with firm performance, suggesting that environmentally oriented innovation may be linked to economic benefits for SMEs. Moreover, our results indicate that internal R&D intensity has no significant direct association with green innovation among SMEs. These findings suggest that SMEs often rely on a network‐intensive model of green innovation, in which external collaborations play a central role, while internal R&D intensity becomes complementary only as firms develop greater organizational capacity.

title: From Resource Circulation to Sustainable Value Creation
summary: This paper examines the relationships among circular economy, green innovation and sustainable production systems through a structured review of recent academic contributions. It considers circular economy as a systemic approach to resource circulation, value retention and business-model transformation, while recognizing that circularity cannot be considered equivalent to sustainability without evaluating its environmental, economic and social outcomes. The review further examines green innovation as a mechanism through which firms translate environmental pressures, technological capabilities, organizational resources and institutional incentives into cleaner products, processes and managerial practices. Particular attention is given to the influence of regulation, stakeholder pressure, knowledge management, digitalization and organizational capabilities on environmental innovation and corporate performance. The final part addresses sustainable manufacturing, Industry 4.0 and sustainable supply-chain management, emphasizing the growing convergence between technological modernization, circular production, environmental management and interorganizational coordination. The reviewed literature suggests that sustainable production depends less on isolated environmental practices than on the integration of technological, organizational and institutional mechanisms across product life cycles and supply networks. Digital technologies can strengthen traceability, resource efficiency and circular material flows, but their contribution remains conditional on managerial capabilities, sustainability-oriented operations and appropriate governance arrangements. Overall, the paper highlights the need for integrated production strategies capable of combining circularity, innovation, supply-chain coordination and multidimensional performance measurement

title: Rethinking Legal Strategies for Gender Equality in Brazilian Corporate Governance
summary: This article critically analyses Brazil’s 2025 gender equity law, which mandates a 30 per cent gender quota on the boards of public companies. Drawing on feminist legal theories and over a decade of Brazilian parliamentary debates, we examine the justifications used by parliamentarians, from liberal and cultural feminism to a rationale grounded in social justice and intersectionality. Although the law represents an important legislative advancement, it faces two key limitations. First, its scope is restricted to public companies, leaving listed corporations to voluntary self-regulation, which data show has produced slower progress on gender and racial diversity; we argue that the public interest rationale that justifies mandatory quotas for public companies should also apply to listed corporations. Second, by focusing on top-tier positions, the law risks promoting a narrow and non-representative universal woman, disregarding the compounded disadvantages faced by Black and economically marginalised women, as shown by Brazilian labour market data. Despite these limitations, the law makes a unique contribution, combining an intersectional quota with mandatory data disclosure requirements. We conclude by proposing pathways for more comprehensive and transformative gender equity policies.

title: Social Protection Provisioning in Zimbabwe: Is Fintech the Real Deal?
summary: This article critically examines the integration of financial technology (Fintech) within social protection frameworks in Zimbabwe, addressing the significant systemic challenges that plague traditional distribution methods. The analysis reveals that developing nations, particularly Zimbabwe, face substantial barriers, including inadequate targeting mechanisms, limited accessibility, information deficits, escalating program costs, and pervasive corruption and fund misappropriation. These challenges exacerbate poverty and underline the urgent necessity for enhanced social protection measures. Through, a mixed-methods research design, data were collected from implementing staff across various humanitarian agencies using a structured questionnaire. The quantitative analysis employed SPSS, leading to the identification of critical constructs, including convenience, security, and cost management, that underpin Fintech’s potential to revolutionise social protection delivery. The findings indicate robust support for Fintech adoption among practitioners in the field, highlighting its capacity to optimise distribution efficiency and decrease logistical costs while simultaneously bolstering security for beneficiaries and administrators alike. Enhanced tracking, reporting, and accountability of funds were noted as key advantages of Fintech implementation. In conclusion, the study posits that Fintech presents a viable strategy to enhance social protection systems in Zimbabwe, offering an efficient, secure, and cost-effective distribution mechanism. This research provides significant empirical insights from a developing-country context and advocates further investigation into blockchain technology and climate-centric Fintech applications. The integration of Fintech into social services signifies a transformative shift in social protection delivery, effectively supporting vulnerable populations.
