title: Awareness Alone is not Enough – KSL Kupferschiefer Lausitz Caught Between the Need for Raw Material Security and Reality: “Mining with ESG” within the European Raw Materials Framework
summary: The European Union’s Critical Raw Materials Act (CRMA) has highlighted the strategic importance of domestic raw materials projects. At the same time, a tension is evident in specific projects: whilst Europe calls for more resilient supply chains, strategic autonomy and raw materials security, individual projects on the ground are assessed primarily on the basis of environmental compatibility, energy integration, the circular economy, regional value creation and social acceptance. The Spremberg-Graustein-Schleife copper project by KSL Kupferschiefer Lausitz GmbH, Spremberg/Germany, in Lusatia is a prime example of this new evaluation framework. This article outlines the project, assesses its significance in terms of the raw materials economy and mineral deposits, and demonstrates how Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) requirements are increasingly becoming technical design criteria – ranging from backfilling and water recycling, through dry-stack concepts, to potential regional energy and material cycles. The article is based on the authors’ presentation at the “MiningForum 2026”, held in Berlin/Germany from 18th to 19th June 2026.

title: Reassessing The Role of Political Embeddedness: ESG and Corporate Market Outcomes in Indonesia
summary: This study aims to test and analyze the role of political embeddedness on the relationship between ESG and corporate market performance in Indonesia. This study used data from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX), excluding financial sector companies. The final sample size was 1,281 firm-years. Panel data regression analysis techniques were used to test the research hypotheses. Furthermore, several tests, including robustness tests and further testing, were conducted to deepen the research. Regression results reveal that ESG plays a role in building market confidence in a company, thus increasing its value. Furthermore, political embeddedness plays a significant role in strengthening ESG's influence on corporate market outcomes. The integration of political embeddedness, ESG, and corporate market outcomes into a research model, along with its comprehensive analysis, makes this study valuable for advancing the literature. This study addresses a research gap and provides a broad perspective on the model analyzed.

title: Can natural capital accounting bring accountability for nature?
summary: With increasing global ecosystem degradation, new ways of governing the relationship between people and nature are needed. As Western societies increasingly turn to the emerging practice of Natural Capital Accounting (NCA), this is a critical time to consider its institutional role. In this paper we consider the effectiveness of NCA in bringing accountability for nature. This study theorises the link between accountability and NCA practice and explores this link empirically through quantitative and qualitative analyses of four methods of practice - the Capitals Coalition, Integrated Reporting, the System of Environmental Economic Accounting – Ecosystem Accounting, and Accounting for Nature®. The study found that NCA methods employ a range of technical mechanisms for delivering accountability, including data processes, external audit, and participation of, and transparency with, stakeholders; however, there were substantial limitations for their effectiveness. Our results highlight five challenges for NCA in delivering accountability for nature, underpinned by the broader governance environment in which this institution operates. We discuss governance options for bringing accountability for nature both with, and without, NCA. The findings of this study will help academics and policy makers to design institutional arrangements which are fit-for-purpose for bringing accountability for nature.

title: Digital Transformation and the Future of Higher Education: A Comprehensive Umbrella Review
summary: Digital transformation (DT) is fundamentally changing the higher education institutions (HEIs) around the globe. The COVID-19 pandemic has drastically increased using digitally enabled approaches for teaching, learning, research, and administration, driven by the convergence of technologies encompassing the industry 4.0. Despite the various existing reviews that tackle digital transformation separately, some, such as those on the technology adoption or strategic planning, or pedagogical innovation, have limited scope and do not offer an overall, multi-dimensional synthesis. This rather comprehensive umbrella review combines dimensions, technologies, strategic processes and actors related to the implementation of DT in HEIs, based on the systematic and multivocal literature reviews, analyses via PRISMA, and thematic synthesises of articles, published from 2015 to 2024, in Scopus, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, ScienceDirect, Springer Link and ACM Digital Library databases. A total of 47 studies in the analytical corpus, two of which were anchor reviews and 43 were complementary primary studies, were identified in an initial pool of 312 records. The findings showed that most digital transformation projects (DTIs) in the education sector are concentrated on competitive education (24%) and that the dominant enabling technologies are analytics (23%), cloud computing (20%), and artificial intelligence (16%). Most of all, just one-quarter of HEIs can speak with any degree of fluency about a digital strategy and only 56% of DTIs are part of a broader institutional agenda. The review concludes that, based on the importance of those topics in the curriculum, student demand satisfaction (12%) and digital culture (9%) fall short of expected levels of investment. The results are derived from the existing reviews and primary studies and thus share the limitations of the primary literature reviewed. The results highlight the need for university leaders to create digital strategies that are integrated, invest in faculty development and digital culture, and embrace a transformative approach instead of a technology-only approach to the implementation of digital transformation.

title: The Impact of Digital Transformation on Organizational Performance in Telecommunications Companies in Sudan
summary: هدفت هذه الدراسة إلى التعرف على أثر التحول الرقمي على الأداء المؤسسي بشركات الاتصالات في السودان. وتمثلت مشكلة الدراسة في التساؤل الرئيس حول مدى تأثير التحول الرقمي بأبعاده المختلفة في مستوى الأداء المؤسسي بشركات الاتصالات السودانية. واعتمدت الدراسة على المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، وتمثلت أبعاد التحول الرقمي في: البنية التحتية والتقنيات الرقمية، والاستراتيجية الرقمية، ورقمنة العمليات، والقدرات والمهارات الرقمية، والثقافة التنظيمية الداعمة للتحول الرقمي. ولأغراض الدراسة الميدانية تم تصميم استبانة وتطبيقها على عينة افتراضية من العاملين بشركات الاتصالات في السودان، واستخدام الأساليب الإحصائية المناسبة لتحليل البيانات واختبار فرضيات الدراسة. وأظهرت النتائج الافتراضية وجود علاقة إيجابية ذات دلالة إحصائية بين التحول الرقمي والأداء المؤسسي، كما أشارت إلى أن رقمنة العمليات والاستراتيجية الرقمية والبنية التحتية الرقمية من أكثر الأبعاد تأثيرًا في الأداء المؤسسي. وخلصت الدراسة إلى أن نجاح التحول الرقمي لا يعتمد على توفير التكنولوجيا فقط، وإنما يتطلب تكاملها مع الاستراتيجية التنظيمية وتطوير مهارات العاملين وبناء ثقافة تنظيمية داعمة للابتكار والتغيير. وأوصت الدراسة بضرورة زيادة الاستثمار في البنية التحتية الرقمية، وتطوير مهارات العاملين، وإعادة تصميم العمليات، ووضع استراتيجيات واضحة للتحول الرقمي وربطها بمؤشرات الأداء المؤسسي.

title: Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) Controversy: Tinjauan Sistematis Determinan Tata Kelola dan Konsekuensi Korporasi
summary: This study systematically synthesizes the literature on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) controversy by examining its determinants, corporate consequences, thematic evolution, and emerging research directions. Using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach based on PRISMA guidelines, this study analyzed 42 empirical articles indexed in the Scopus database and published between 2020 and 2026. Unlike previous ESG-related reviews that mainly focus on ESG performance and sustainability disclosure, this review specifically integrates the determinants and consequences of ESG controversy at the firm level within governance and sustainability contexts. The findings indicate that corporate governance mechanisms, firm characteristics, ESG disclosure practices, industry sensitivity, and institutional environments are the main factors influencing controversy exposure, with board independence, gender diversity, and ownership structure emerging as the most influential governance mechanisms. The review further reveals that controversy exposure generates multidimensional consequences, including lower financial performance and firm value, higher financial risk, reputational damage, and negative market reactions. The study contributes theoretically by providing an integrated understanding of how governance mechanisms and contextual factors shape sustainability-related corporate risks. This review also identifies research gaps related to measurement inconsistency, industry-specific contexts, and cross-country governance differences. However, this study is limited to Scopus-indexed empirical articles and may not fully capture findings from non-indexed literature. The findings provide practical implications for managers, investors, and policymakers in strengthening governance quality, improving ESG transparency, and mitigating sustainability-related risks.

title: Pengaruh Green Accounting, Kinerja Keuangan dan Good Corporate Governance terhadap Penghindaran Pajak pada Perusahaan Manufaktur di Bursa Efek Indonesia Tahun 2021-2024
summary: Penelitian ini mengkaji hubungan antara akuntansi hijau, kinerja keuangan, dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik serta pengaruhnya terhadap penghindaran pajak di antara perusahaan manufaktur yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (IDX) selama periode 2021–2024. Isu penghindaran pajak penting karena keputusan pajak perusahaan dapat dikaitkan dengan kondisi keuangan, praktik akuntansi lingkungan, dan implementasi tata kelola perusahaan. Penelitian ini mengadopsi pendekatan kuantitatif menggunakan data sekunder yang diperoleh dari laporan keuangan perusahaan, laporan tahunan, dan laporan keberlanjutan yang dipublikasikan selama periode pengamatan. Data dikumpulkan dari situs web resmi Bursa Efek Indonesia dan pengungkapan perusahaan yang relevan. Sampel ditentukan melalui purposive sampling berdasarkan kriteria yang telah ditentukan, menghasilkan 21 perusahaan manufaktur dan total 84 observasi. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan Statistical Package for the Social Sciences (SPSS) versi 25. Prosedur analitis terdiri dari analisis statistik deskriptif, uji asumsi klasik, dan analisis regresi linier berganda. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa akuntansi hijau memiliki pengaruh positif dan signifikan secara statistik terhadap penghindaran pajak. Sebaliknya, kinerja keuangan memiliki pengaruh negatif dan signifikan secara statistik terhadap penghindaran pajak. Sementara itu, tata kelola perusahaan yang baik tidak memiliki pengaruh yang signifikan secara statistik terhadap penghindaran pajak. Koefisien determinasi menunjukkan nilai Adjusted R Square sebesar 0,364, yang mengindikasikan bahwa akuntansi hijau, kinerja keuangan, dan tata kelola perusahaan yang baik secara kolektif menjelaskan 36,4% variasi dalam penghindaran pajak. Sisanya, 63,6%, disebabkan oleh faktor-faktor lain di luar model penelitian.

title: DOES THE DIGITAL ECONOMY INCREASE RURAL HOUSEHOLD INCOME? AN EMPIRICAL STUDY FROM CHINA
summary: In the era of rapid technological advancement, the digital economy has emerged as a crucial catalyst for socioeconomic transformation. This study comprehensively investigates the impact of the digital economy on rural household income in China, utilizing nationally representative microdata from the 2018 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS). To ensure reliability, we rigorously address potential endogeneity issues through advanced econometric techniques and conduct robustness checks. Baseline empirical results robustly demonstrate that the digital economy significantly increases rural household income. Mechanism analysis reveals that this positive effect is primarily driven by two pathways: facilitating the transition of the rural labor force into non-agricultural employment and substantially enhancing households’ entrepreneurial capabilities. Furthermore, a detailed heterogeneity analysis uncovers several nuanced patterns. First, a notable regional disparity exists; the income-enhancing effects are significantly stronger in the economically advanced eastern regions compared to central and western areas. Second, social capital exhibits a distinctive U-shaped moderating effect, meaning the digital economy’s impact is most pronounced at both extremely high and extremely low levels of social capital. Third, regarding income structure, the digital economy disproportionately benefits non-agricultural income rather than traditional agricultural income. Finally, terrain effects play a critical role; the positive impact is more evident in non-plain regions, which typically suffer from geographical disadvantages and information asymmetry. Ultimately, these findings provide compelling empirical evidence elucidating how the digital economy drives rural income growth, offering valuable insights and targeted policy recommendations for bridging the digital divide in China and other developing countries. Existing literature highlights that the relationship between broadband access and labor market outcomes has been a focal point for researchers and policymakers.

title: Personal Data Protection and Legal Accountability in the Digital Transformation of Public and Private Institutions
summary: Digital transformation in public and private institutions increases the processing of personal data while increasing the risk of privacy violations and unclear legal liability. This research aims to analyze the protection of personal data and the construction of institutional legal accountability in the implementation of digital systems. The research uses normative legal methods with legislative, conceptual, and comparative approaches. Data in the form of primary and secondary legal materials were collected through literature studies and analyzed qualitatively-prescriptively, without involving respondents or informants. The results show that the effectiveness of data protection depends on data controller compliance, processing security, clarity of legal obligations, and effective enforcement mechanisms. The research concludes that strengthening institutional accountability, data governance, and law enforcement consistency is needed to ensure the protection of data subjects' rights in digital transformation.

title: The relationship between corporate governance mechanisms and carbon emissions performance in advanced and emerging economies
summary: This study investigates how corporate governance attributes shape firms’ carbon emissions performance, with the aim of identifying internal governance mechanisms that support effective carbon management and highlighting governance gaps that may impede such performance. The study uses a balanced panel of 972 listed non-financial firms from the world’s five largest economies—the United States, China, Germany, Japan, and India- over the period 2020–2024. The analysis utilises multiple econometric approaches, including fixed effects models with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors, Pooled Ordinary Least Squares (POLS) with Driscoll–Kraay standard errors and industry, year and country dummies, and 2 SLS estimation to address potential endogeneity. Our results indicate that boards characterised by greater gender diversity and independence, and that meet more frequently are associated with lower carbon emissions intensity and improved carbon emissions performance. CEO non-duality is also associated with improved carbon emissions performance. However, board size does not appear to improve such performance. This study provides novel cross-country evidence on the governance–carbon emissions association using firm-level data from five major economies. It advances the literature by offering robust insights into how board structures influence corporate carbon mitigation within an international institutional setting.

title: Why we stay subscribed: interdependent self-construal as a driver of subscription retention in the digital economy
summary: Purpose The purpose of this paper is to investigate how self-construal, a previously unexamined psychological construct in this context, influences consumer decision-making within the burgeoning subscription economy. This research proposes that the effect of self-construal on subscription choices is driven by a fundamental need to belong, which is particularly salient for individuals with an interdependent self-construal. Design/methodology/approach Five studies were conducted to test the hypotheses. Study 1 employed a correlational survey to establish the initial link between self-construal and subscription retention. Studies 2, 3, 4 and 5 used controlled experimental designs to manipulate self-construal and examine its causal impact on different consumption behaviors, including subscription retention, new acquisition, and one-time purchases. Findings The results consistently demonstrate that individuals with an interdependent self-construal are significantly more inclined to retain an unused interpersonal subscription than those with an independent self-construal. This effect, however, is not a general preference for all interpersonal products; it is a specific motivation to maintain existing social bonds. Studies 4 and 5 provide crucial boundary conditions, showing that self-construal has no significant effect on the decision to acquire a new subscription or to make a one-time purchase of an interpersonal product. Originality/value This study extends the self-construal framework to non-material consumption contexts, specifically subscription services. By distinguishing between retention and acquisition, and by identifying one-time purchases as a boundary condition, this research provides a nuanced and precise theoretical explanation for the underlying motives that drive consumers to engage with the subscription economy.

title: Pengaruh Capital Intensity, Sales Growth, dan Komite Audit Terhadap Tax Avoidance
summary: Tax avoidance remains an important issue because differences in corporate characteristics and governance mechanisms may shape how companies manage their tax obligations. This study examines the effect of capital intensity, sales growth, and the audit committee on tax avoidance in Consumer Non-Cyclicals companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during 2020–2024. The study uses a quantitative associative approach with panel data. Purposive sampling produced 33 companies and 165 observations. The data were analyzed using panel data regression with EViews 13, and the Random Effect Model (REM) was selected based on the model selection tests. The findings indicate that capital intensity and sales growth do not have a significant effect on tax avoidance, whereas the audit committee has a significant effect. Simultaneously, capital intensity, sales growth, and the audit committee significantly affect tax avoidance. The adjusted R-squared of 9.38% indicates that the three independent variables explain a limited proportion of variations in tax avoidance, while the remaining variation is associated with other factors outside the model. These findings highlight the importance of corporate governance, particularly the audit committee, in understanding corporate tax-related decisions.

title: Emerging Risks, Fintech and Financial Sector Regulation: Performance Analysis, Science Mapping and Future Directions
summary: The study examined the scholarly output on the regulator`s response to emerging risks within the financial services sector. To attain this, a bibliometric approach was adopted that focused on performance and scientific mapping of the scholarly output. The data was retrieved from Scopus database covering the period 2016 to February 2026 resulting in 73 articles. The retreived articles were carefully screened using the Scientific Procedures and Rationales for Systematic Literature Review (SPAR-4-SLR) framework. Results were presented in terms of quantified annual scientific production, main authors, collaboration networks, and thematic research categories among others. The results indicate that regulatory response to emerging risks subject is growing evidenced by the number of annual publications, scholars and countries involved. Considerably, the scholarly research reflects very few collaborations who have played a critical influence in disseminating knowledge. Similarly, the results indicate a limited collaboration among countries, with institutional collaboration described as mainly locally concentrated. In conclusion, despite emerging risks, fintech is driving financial services transformation, with research mainly centred on financial regulation, artificial intelligence, blockchain, and digital financial ecosystems. Thus, the study provides evidence-based insights into fintech's increasingly complicated regulatory challenges for policymakers.

title: Strategic Pathways to De-Risk and Decarbonize Rare-Earth Supply Chains – A Responsible Supply Lens on Building Resilient, Low-Emission Rare-Earth Value Chains by 2030
summary: Rare-earth supply chains face a triple challenge: geographic concentration, high carbon intensity, and structural bottlenecks in the midstream. While demand from electric vehicles, wind energy, robotics, and defence is projected to reach approximately 100,000 t by 2030, the current supply architecture is not built to support this scale-up at speed. This article argues that rare-earth risk is not primarily a mining problem: the true point of control lies in the midstream: separation, metal and alloy conversion, and magnet manufacturing, where single-country concentration reaches an estimated 90 % or more. Diversification strategies that stop at mining, including popular “China+1” approaches, improve visibility but not control. Drawing on Beroe analysis and data from the United States Geological Survey (USGS), the International Energy Agency (IEA), Argus Media, and other industry sources, the article maps the policy landscape across Europe, the United States, India, and Japan, evaluates cleaner processing and circular feedstock as decarbonization levers, and sets out a 2030 roadmap in which competitiveness is defined jointly by cost, carbon, and resilience. It concludes with concrete actions for governments, OEMs, and procurement organizations. The article is based on the author’s presentation at the “MiningForum 2026”, held in Berlin/Germany from 18th to 19th June 2026.

title: THE EFFECT OF CAPITAL STRUCTURE ON FIRM PERFORMANCE WITH CORPORATE GOVERNANCE AS A MODERATING VARIABLE: EVIDENCE FROM CGPI-LISTED COMPANIES IN INDONESIA
summary: This study examines the effect of capital structure on firm performance and the moderating role of corporate governance. Firm performance is proxied by Return on Equity (ROE) and Tobin’s Q, while capital structure is measured using the Debt to Equity Ratio (DER). Corporate governance is represented by the Corporate Governance Perception Index (CGPI). The study employs a quantitative approach using purposive sampling on companies listed in the CGPI and the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2018–2022 period. Data were analyzed using multiple linear regression with moderation analysis (interaction effect) through SPSS 26. The findings indicate that capital structure does not have a significant effect on ROE and Tobin’s Q, suggesting that leverage decisions do not directly influence profitability or market valuation. Furthermore, corporate governance does not moderate the relationship between capital structure and ROE, indicating that governance mechanisms do not strengthen the impact of leverage on accounting-based performance. However, corporate governance significantly moderates the relationship between capital structure and Tobin’s Q, implying that strong governance enhances the positive perception of leverage in the market. These results highlight the importance of governance quality in shaping investor confidence and firm value. Keywords: capital structure, corporate governance, firm performance, tobin’s q

title: ФІНТЕХ ТА ESG: ЦИФРОВІ ІНСТРУМЕНТИ ДЛЯ СТАЛОГО ФІНАНСУВАННЯ
summary: The aim of the article is to substantiate the role of FinTech and ESG instruments in ensuring sustainable finance and to develop a functional approach to their integration into the processes of financial resource mobilisation, assessment, allocation and monitoring. Within the scope of the study, the roles of ESG and FinTech are differentiated: ESG is defined as the basis for the criteria underlying financial decisions, while FinTech is viewed as the technological mechanism for their implementation. In addition, the authors have developed a functional-integration approach to the interaction between ESG and FinTech within the sustainable finance system. Unlike approaches in which ESG and FinTech are considered primarily as separate areas or sets of instruments, their interrelationship is defined through the functions they perform at different stages of the movement of financial resources. ESG is regarded as the substantive and methodological basis for establishing the criteria for financial decisions, whereas FinTech serves as a technological mechanism for collecting, processing, analysing, automating and monitoring the relevant information. The study resulted in the development of a methodological approach to establishing the correspondence between ESG and FinTech instruments through the sequential implementation of the following stages: identification of the stages of the financial process; identification of ESG functions within the financial process; selection of ESG instruments and determination of their technological function; selection of FinTech instruments and determination of the expected outcome from applying the configuration of ESG and FinTech instruments; and verification of functional alignment. On this basis, a functional matrix of their interaction is proposed for the stages of financial resource mobilisation, assessment, allocation and monitoring. It is established that this approach makes it possible to avoid treating a specific FinTech technology as a mandatory technological equivalent of a particular ESG instrument and to determine technological solutions according to the functional requirements of the financial process. The practical value of the proposed approach lies in enabling financial institutions to use the matrix to select digital solutions according to the relevant ESG function.

title: Analisis Faktor Penentu Keberhasilan Implementasi Myob Accounting dalam Penyusunan Laporan Keuangan UMKM: Systematic Literature Review
summary: This study aims to analyze and synthesize various factors determining the success of the implementation of the MYOB Accounting application in supporting the financial reporting process for Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs). The research method used is a Systematic Literature Review (SLR). A total of 20 relevant scientific articles from accredited databases spanning the years 2019 to 2025 were extracted through content analysis and narrative synthesis. The study’s findings indicate that the success rate of MYOB adoption is influenced by five key determinants: business owners’ awareness, employees’ digital literacy capabilities, intensive mentoring support, the system’s technical alignment with the SAK EMKM accounting standards, and technological infrastructure readiness. Regular direct mentoring emerges as the most critical differentiating factor in overcoming users’ initial technical barriers. The implications of this research provide strategic guidance for SME business owners to improve the quality of their financial reports, while also serving as a theoretical reference for policymakers in accelerating accurate and sustainable digital accounting transformation programs.

title: Data-driven business models: a blueprint for new product development
summary: Purpose This study aims to develop and validate a comprehensive data-driven business model (DDBM) framework that serves as a strategic blueprint for new product development (NPD). Design/methodology/approach It uses a mixed-methods approach that combines qualitative and quantitative techniques, enabling the modeling of complex, feedback-driven, and nonlinear relationships among variables. In the qualitative phase, the study conducts semi-structured interviews with industry experts to identify the model's key dimensions. During the quantitative phase, the research applies the fuzzy cognitive map (FCM) method to test relationships among the identified DDBM dimensions. Findings The qualitative results identify 17 key variables within the DDBM, explaining how data influences activities ranging from understanding customer preferences to implementing smart logistics and optimizing revenue streams. The quantitative stage models the causal interdependencies among data assets, analytics capabilities, and mechanisms for the diffusion of innovation. Ultimately, by presenting a holistic framework that connects data to the NPD process, this research offers entrepreneurs insights into how to leverage data as a vital resource for value creation. Originality/value This study enhances the theoretical understanding of how businesses adopt data-driven approaches and provides a practical view of innovation processes. It also offers a comprehensive look at how the different parts of a DDBM interact, emphasizing the vital role of data in creating value and supporting NPD. Methodologically, this study is valuable for combining FCM and thematic analysis, offering a unique approach to addressing a gap in the entrepreneurship literature. This approach captures dynamic interactions among data flows, decision mechanisms, and innovation stages.

title: From Digital Rural Development to the Modernization of Agriculture and Rural Areas: Provincial Evidence from China
summary: Agricultural-rural modernization is increasingly shaped by digital transformation, yet the relationship between digital rural development (DRD) and agricultural-rural modernization (ARM) remains debated. Using a balanced panel of 28 Chinese provincial-level regions from 2015 to 2023, this study constructs multidimensional DRD and ARM indices and estimates their relationship with two-way fixed-effects models. To reduce measurement-driven correlation, we audit overlap between the two indicator systems and construct an overlap-adjusted DRD index. Results show that DRD is positively associated with ARM after controlling for socioeconomic conditions, province fixed effects, and year fixed effects. The relationship remains positive using the overlap-adjusted index and one-period lagged DRD. Flexible nonlinear models indicate a weak association at low DRD levels, a stronger association in the middle range, and flattening at higher levels. Gradient boosting with SHAP decomposition identifies digital economy and digital industry as the strongest predictors of ARM. Spatial analysis reveals clustering in both DRD and ARM, with the gravity center of DRD shifting westward after 2019. Overall, rural digitalization is most closely related to modernization when digital resources are embedded in production, market circulation, and industrial organization.

title: Chatbots and digital transformation in Colombian banking: Drivers of continuance intention in an emerging market
summary: This study investigates users’ continuance intention toward AI-powered chatbots in the Colombian banking sector, a setting characterized by institutional asymmetries, trust-related concerns around digital financial services, and the continued relevance of interpersonal service expectations. Drawing on a Global South perspective as an interpretive lens, this study examines chatbot continuance intention in an emerging-market banking context where digital service evaluation is shaped by usefulness, satisfaction, perceived quality, and trust. Rather than treating institutional conditions as directly measured mechanisms, the study uses the Colombian context to interpret how post-use service evaluations operate in a relational and highly regulated financial environment.Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM), data from 439 Colombian banking users were analyzed to assess four antecedents of continuance intention: perceived chatbot quality, trust, satisfaction, and perceived usefulness. The findings show that satisfaction is the strongest predictor of continuance intention, followed by perceived usefulness, perceived chatbot quality, and trust. Specifically, satisfaction showed the strongest effect (β = 0.380), followed by perceived usefulness (β = 0.250), perceived chatbot quality (β = 0.150), and trust (β = 0.110). The model explained approximately 58.1% of the variance in continuance intention. These results suggest that, in the Colombian banking context, positive post-use evaluations play a particularly central role in continuance intention, even when trust in digital financial technologies remains more cautious or uneven.

title: The evolution of robo-advisors in FinTech: a global bibliometric and thematic analysis, review and future agenda
summary: This study presents a longitudinal bibliometric and thematic analysis of the global robo-advisory research landscape from 2017 to 2026, using a total of 384 peer-reviewed publications selected from an initial dataset of 865 records retrieved from Web of Science and Scopus databases. By employing co-citation, co-authorship, bibliographic coupling, keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis, the study attempts to highlight the structural and conceptual evolution of the field. The co-citation analysis shows that robo-advisor research sits at the crossroads of finance, marketing, and information systems, built on foundational work like TAM, UTAUT, SEM, and Markowitz’s portfolio theory; the co-authorship network reveals a diverse field dominated by small, internally cohesive teams, with limited cross-border collaboration, despite the citations that show substantial convergence. Bibliographic coupling shows the central presence of a trust- and intention-focused core, supported by broad adoption and behavioural literature, and a newer wave of extending the field outward into more outcome-based peripheries. The keyword co-occurrence, cluster, thematic, evolutionary, and triangulation analysis differentiates well-known themes from accelerating ones. AI, trust, LLMs, UTAUT, perceived risk and value, anthropomorphism, GenAI, and DeFi remain robust across temporal specifications. The study concludes by providing actionable implications for researchers, practitioners, and policymakers with a call for future research by converting the findings into four research programs: adaptive and personalized investment intelligence, human–AI collaborative advisory, responsible and autonomous financial AI, and programmable and expanded investment ecosystems to ensure responsible and inclusive development of robo-advisory systems across diverse financial ecosystems.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility in India: A Legal Examination
summary: Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) is defined by the Companies (Corporate Social Responsibility Policy) Rules, 2014, as amended in 2021, as “the activities undertaken by a Company in pursuance of its statutory obligation laid down in section 135 of the Act”. In simple terms, Corporate Social Responsibility means that companies have a duty to contribute ethically and positively to society while conducting their business. Corporate Social Responsibility draws on the Triple Bottom Line approach, which measures a company’s success along three dimensions, people, planet and profit, and not by financial gain alone. This article examines Corporate Social Responsibility from a legal perspective, discussing its evolution and how it is treated under Indian law. It also explains the role of law in promoting Corporate Social Responsibility, why companies should engage in Corporate Social Responsibility activities, and the challenges faced in implementing and enforcing Corporate Social Responsibility.

title: Which Environment, Social and Governance Indicators Influence the Financial Distress Prediction? Evidence From Explainable Neural Networks
summary: ABSTRACT This study identifies which disaggregated environmental, social and governance (ESG) indicators influence financial distress prediction, combining an explainable artificial neural network, multinomial logistic regression and random forest on 9715 UK private firms (2020–2023). Relative to a benchmark using financial predictors alone, adding disaggregated ESG indicators raises holdout accuracy from 66.5% to 74.4% and the macro F1‐score from 0.657 to 0.748. Material information is concentrated in specific indicators rather than in the aggregate ESG score: executive remuneration and workforce‐ and stakeholder‐related practices provide the most convergent evidence, corporate governance receives moderate support and environmental indicators are heterogeneous. The aggregate score is consistently signed across methods but in the wrong direction, associated with a higher probability of distress, showing how composite ratings can invert the signals of their components. Materiality is stage‐ordered: long‐horizon practices are most informative among sound firms, governance controls among distressed firms and incremental value peaks in the grey zone.

title: CSR Disclosure Breadth and Earnings Management: Evidence Consistent with Opportunistic Reporting in an Emerging Market
summary: This study examines the contemporaneous association between earnings management (EM) and corporate social responsibility (CSR) disclosure breadth in an emerging-market setting. Using a balanced panel of 136 manufacturing firms listed on the Tehran Stock Exchange across eight annual panel periods (2017–2024; 1088 firm-year observations), CSR disclosure is measured with a 33-item binary content-analysis index with explicit coding boundaries. The primary Kothari-style performance-adjusted signed abnormal-accrual measure is positively associated with disclosure breadth (β = 0.198, p = 0.031). A secondary modified Dechow–Dichev-style signed accrual–cash-flow residual sensitivity is positive but marginal (β = 0.285, p = 0.060), and real earnings management is positive but marginal in the beta-regression specification (β = 0.254, p = 0.071). In firm- and year-fixed-effects OLS, AEM-K remains positive and significant, AEM-DD remains marginal, and REM is not statistically significant. The evidence is associational rather than causal and is consistent with—but does not establish—an opportunistic-reporting interpretation in which financial-reporting opportunism can coexist with broader CSR disclosure.

title: Peran Moderasi Agency Cost terhadap Kinerja Keuangan melalui Agresivitas Pajak dan Green Accounting
summary: Financial performance is influenced not only by operational and financial decisions but also by tax strategies, environmental practices, and agency relationships. Tax aggressiveness may provide tax-saving benefits, while green accounting can support resource efficiency and environmental risk management; however, both strategies may produce different financial consequences when agency conflicts and information asymmetry are present. This study aims to examine the conceptual role of agency cost in moderating the relationships of tax aggressiveness and green accounting with financial performance. The study adopts a quantitative research design using secondary data from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange, with purposive sampling based on the availability of financial, tax, and environmental information. The proposed moderation model examines the direct effects of tax aggressiveness and green accounting on financial performance and their interactions with agency cost. The conceptual analysis indicates that the relationship between tax aggressiveness, green accounting, and financial performance is context-dependent and may be influenced by agency costs, corporate governance, industry characteristics, and tax-related risks. Agency cost is therefore expected to condition how effectively tax and environmental strategies are translated into financial performance. Empirical conclusions regarding the proposed hypotheses require statistical evidence from the selected observations.

title: The Mediating Role of Good Corporate Governance in the Relationship between ESG Performance and Financial Sustainability among MSMEs in Medan, Indonesia
summary: This study examines the relationship between ESG Performance and Financial Sustainability among Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) by investigating the mediating role of Good Corporate Governance (GCG). While previous studies have predominantly examined the direct effects of ESG practices on organizational performance in large corporations, evidence on how governance mechanisms transmit ESG effects to financial sustainability among MSMEs in developing economies remains limited. This study addresses this gap by testing an ESG–GCG–Financial Sustainability framework among MSMEs in Medan, Indonesia. A quantitative cross-sectional design was employed using purposive sampling. Data were collected from 60 MSME owners and managers through a structured questionnaire using a five-point Likert scale and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results show that ESG Performance has a positive and significant effect on GCG (β = 0.864, p < 0.001), while GCG positively and significantly affects Financial Sustainability (β = 0.953, p < 0.001). GCG also significantly mediates the relationship between ESG Performance and Financial Sustainability (β = 0.823, p < 0.001), indicating that governance mechanisms play an important role in translating ESG practices into sustainable financial outcomes. This study contributes empirical evidence from MSMEs in an emerging economy and highlights governance as a mechanism linking ESG practices with financial sustainability. The findings provide implications for MSME owners and policymakers seeking to strengthen sustainable business development through improved governance practices. The results should be interpreted cautiously due to the relatively small sample and single-city context.

title: Rethinking digital transformation in higher education: a systematic review of technological, individual and institutional drivers
summary: Purpose Digital transformation is reshaping higher education, driving the adoption of online and blended learning platforms worldwide. Despite substantial investments in digital technologies, student adoption remains uneven and engagement often falls short, highlighting critical gaps in understanding the factors that enable effective digital learning. This study examines the technological, individual and institutional determinants that drive student adoption and sustained engagement. Design/methodology/approach This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 99 empirical studies conducted between 2020 and 2025 across diverse geographic and cultural contexts, examining how students perceive and adopt digital transformation initiatives in higher education institutions. Findings The review reveals that technological factors (e.g. perceived usefulness, ease of use and system quality) interact with individual factors (e.g. motivation, attitude and skills) and institutional factors (e.g. support and infrastructure) to influence behavioral outcomes such as adoption, engagement and intention to continue online learning. While dominant theoretical frameworks, including the technology acceptance model (TAM), unified theory of acceptance and use of technology and theory of planned behavior, remain widely applied, recent trends favor hybrid models integrating cognitive, affective, and contextual dimensions. Persistence gaps include overreliance on TAM, limited exploration of socio-emotional and cross-cultural factors and scarcity of longitudinal studies. Originality/value By synthesizing contemporary evidence this study provides a comprehensive framework for understanding digital adoption in higher education integrating behavioral, cognitive, and affective dimensions. It offers both theoretical and practical insights, guiding policymakers, educators and platform designers in enhancing engagement, usability and sustained adoption. This review supports equitable, effective, and long-term implementation of digital tools, fostering meaningful learning, bridging digital inequities and enabling innovation in higher education worldwide.

title: Pengaruh Ukuran Perusahaan, Profitabilitas, dan Likuiditas terhadap Kinerja Saham dengan Corporate Governance sebagai Variabel Moderasi pada Sektor Properti
summary: Between 2020 and 2024 the Indonesia Stock Exchange faced the COVID-19 pandemic, global geopolitical pressures, and monetary policy shifts. High volatility made investors more sensitive to fundamental information disclosed by listed firms. This study examines whether firm size, profitability, and liquidity explain stock performance under such conditions, and whether corporate governance moderates those relationships. Firm size is measured by the natural logarithm of total assets, profitability by return on equity, liquidity by the current ratio, and stock performance by annual stock return. Corporate governance is proxied by the proportion of independent commissioners. Purposive sampling of property and real estate firms yielded 25 companies and 124 firm-year observations. Independent variables were mean-centered before constructing interaction terms. Chow, Lagrange Multiplier, and Hausman tests indicated a fixed effects model. Because heteroskedasticity and serial correlation were detected, clustered standard errors were applied. Results show profitability is the only significant determinant, with a coefficient of 0.8998 and probability of 0.045. Firm size, liquidity, and independent commissioners are not significant, and none of the interaction terms is significant, indicating governance does not strengthen or weaken the link between fundamentals and returns. The model is jointly significant, with an F statistic of 44.16, probability of 0.0000, and within R-squared of 0.1469. For investors, earnings capacity is more relevant than asset scale or board composition. For regulators, the findings raise questions about whether independent commissioners function substantively or mainly fulfill listing requirements.

title: Pengaruh Komite Audit, Audit Tenure, dan Reputasi Kantor Akuntan Publik terhadap Kualitas Audit (Studi Empiris pada Perusahaan Sektor Infrastructures yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2020-2024)
summary: This study aims to analyze the effect of the audit committee, audit tenure, and the reputation of Public Accounting Firms (PAF) on audit quality in infrastructure sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2020–2024 period. This research employs a quantitative approach using panel data regression analysis. The study uses secondary data obtained from companies’ annual reports, with the sample selected through purposive sampling. The results indicate that the audit committee has a significant effect on audit quality, suggesting that the effectiveness of the audit committee as a monitoring mechanism can enhance audit quality. Audit tenure also has an effect on audit quality, indicating that the length of the audit engagement between the auditor and the client within the same Public Accounting Firm can influence the auditor’s understanding of the company’s condition as well as independence in conducting the audit. Furthermore, the reputation of the Public Accounting Firm affects audit quality, as firms with strong reputations tend to deliver higher-quality audits. This study provides implications for companies and auditors in improving audit quality through strengthening the role of the audit committee, managing audit tenure optimally, and selecting reputable Public Accounting Firms.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Manajemen Laba dan Leverage Terhadap Tax Avoidance pada Perusahaan Subsektor Logam Dasar dan Baja yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2022-2025
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of profitability, earnings management, and leverage on tax avoidance among basic metal and steel sub-sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2022–2025 period. A quantitative approach was employed using secondary data derived from corporate financial statements. The research sample consisted of 14 companies, yielding a total of 56 observations over the four-year study period. Data analysis was conducted using panel data regression with the Common Effect Model (CEM) approach. The results indicate that profitability has a positive and significant effect on tax avoidance, whereas earnings management and leverage do not show a significant influence. However, when analyzed simultaneously, profitability, earnings management, and leverage significantly affect tax avoidance. The Adjusted R-squared value of 11.16% indicates that the three independent variables explain 11.16% of the variation in tax avoidance, while the remaining 88.84% is influenced by factors outside the research model. These findings provide empirical insight into the determinants of tax avoidance within the basic metal and steel sub-sector and are expected to serve as an academic reference for future research on corporate taxation.

title: Analisis Persepsi Mahasiswa Akuntansi terhadap Peran Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dalam Pencegahan Fraud di Era Digital
summary: Digital transformation has strengthened the role of Accounting Information Systems (AIS) as a means of processing financial data that is fast, integrated, and technology-based. On the other hand, technological developments have also increased the complexity of fraud risks, necessitating more effective control systems. This study aims to explore accounting students’ perceptions of the role of AIS in fraud prevention in the digital age. The study employs a descriptive qualitative approach, with data collected through in-depth interviews with students who have taken courses in Accounting Information Systems, Auditing, and Internal Control. The data were analyzed through the stages of reduction, presentation, and drawing conclusions. The results indicate that students view AIS as a crucial tool in fraud prevention by enhancing transparency, recording accuracy, data security, and providing audit trails that facilitate transaction tracing. The use of technologies such as automation, big data, and artificial intelligence is also considered capable of supporting the early detection of fraud. However, the effectiveness of AIS remains dependent on the competence of human resources, individual integrity, and the quality of an organization’s internal controls. This study is expected to provide input for the development of accounting education and to enhance the readiness of prospective accountants to face organizational governance challenges in the digital age.

title: Dukungan Manajemen sebagai Penguat Pengaruh Teknologi Informasi terhadap Efektivitas Audit Internal
summary: The effectiveness of local government internal audit remains a critical issue amid digital transformation and the generally low capability of Government Internal Supervisory Apparatus (APIP) in Indonesia, particularly in North Sulawesi Province, where auditors' use of information technology remains limited despite consecutive unqualified (WTP) opinions on regional financial statements. Prior studies have not explicitly examined management support as a moderating variable on the relationship between information technology and internal audit effectiveness, so this study aims to examine the effect of information technology on internal audit effectiveness for fraud prevention and to test the moderating role of management support on that relationship. This study employed a quantitative survey approach involving all inspectorate auditors across North Sulawesi Province using a Likert-scale questionnaire, with data analyzed through Partial Least Square-Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) using SmartPLS. The results show that information technology has no significant direct effect on internal audit effectiveness, whereas management support significantly strengthens the effect of information technology on internal audit effectiveness. These findings indicate that the mere availability of technology is insufficient to enhance audit effectiveness without genuine support from management. The implication is that inspectorate leaders, local governments, and the North Sulawesi Representative Office of BPKP need to strengthen management support through budgeting, training, and clear policies so that investment in information technology can be optimally utilized to improve audit effectiveness and fraud prevention.

title: IMPROVING THE MECHANISMS FOR FINANCING ECONOMIC GROWTH IN UZBEKISTAN UNDER GLOBAL FINANCIAL INTEGRATION
summary: This article analyzes the mechanisms for financing economic growth in Uzbekistan under conditions of global financial integration. It examines the role of bank lending, foreign investment, financing from international financial institutions, and capital markets in promoting economic growth. The study also considers currency, interest rate, and external debt risks associated with global financial integration and develops recommendations for diversifying financial resources, expanding long-term investment, and further developing the capital market.

title: Digital transformation as a moderator of green innovation and export performance: Evidence from Vietnamese exporting firms
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractThis study examines the relationships among green innovation, digital transformation, and export performance in Vietnamese exporting firms, with particular attention to the moderating role of digital transformation. Data were collected through a structured survey conducted between April and December 2025. The final sample comprised 292 valid firm-level responses, with one respondent representing each exporting firm. Respondents were managers, executives, or functional staff directly involved in export operations, production, logistics, or strategic decision-making. Ordinary least squares regression with an interaction term was employed to test the proposed relationships. When digital transformation was at its sample mean, green innovation was positively and significantly associated with export performance (B = 0.169, p < 0.001). Correspondingly, when green innovation was at its sample mean, digital transformation was positively and significantly associated with export performance (B = 0.235, p < 0.001). The interaction between green innovation and digital transformation was positive and statistically significant (B = 0.587, p < 0.001), indicating that the association between green innovation and export performance became more positive as digital transformation increased. Conditional-slope analysis revealed a crossover interaction: the relationship was negative at a selected lower level of digital transformation, positive at its sample mean, and substantially stronger at a selected higher level. The model explained 44.6% of the variance in export performance. These findings highlight the complementarity of green and digital capabilities and suggest that digital transformation is an important enabling condition for translating green innovation into stronger export-related outcomes in an emerging economy.

title: Analisis Penerapan PSAK 112 dalam Pelaporan Keuangan Dana Wakaf serta Implikasinya terhadap Akuntabilitas dan Kualitas Pelaporan Keuangan pada Dompet Dhuafa Republika dalam Mendukung Transparansi dan Pencapaian SDGs 16
summary: This study aims to analyze the implementation of PSAK 112 in the financial reporting of waqf funds and its implications for the accountability and quality of financial reporting at Dompet Dhuafa Republica in supporting transparency and the achievement of SDGs 16. This study uses a qualitative approach with descriptive methods. Data were collected through interviews, observations, and documentation, including the audited financial statements of Nazhir Yayasan Dompet Dhuafa Republika for 2023 and 2024. The results show that Dompet Dhuafa Republica has implemented PSAK 112 consistently and comprehensively in the aspects of recognition, measurement, presentation, and disclosure of waqf transactions. All five required components of financial statements have been presented according to standards. The implementation of PSAK 112 has implications for increasing accountability and the quality of financial reporting, which is reflected in the systematic and transparent presentation of waqf asset information. In addition, the implementation of PSAK 112 contributes to supporting SDGs 16, especially targets 16.6 and 16.10, through the development of effective, accountable, and transparent institutions and the disclosure of financial information to the public.

title: How Bridging and Bonding Social Capital Shapes Performance Expectancy of Digital Transformation Among Immigrants and Natives
summary: Performance expectancy, individuals’ beliefs about the usefulness of digital transformation, could impact individuals’ intention, use, and satisfaction with technologies, yet remains an understudied topic among immigrant populations. Drawing on social capital theory, we examine how bonding and bridging social capital shape performance expectancy across different domains of digital transformation and whether these associations differ by nativity status. Using the 2022 Digital Divide Survey (N = 8,400; 7,000 native South Koreans, 700 marriage immigrants, 700 North Korean migrants), regression analyses showed that bridging social capital had positive associations with performance expectancy (b ranging from 0.43 to 0.62, p < 0.001), whereas bonding social capital was negative, particularly for networking (b = −0.09, p < 0.001) and remote work/learning (b = −0.08, p < 0.001). North Korean migrants reported the highest adjusted means of performance expectancy across all domains. Results highlight that diverse social networks generate greater perceived benefits from digital transformation.

title: Research on the Impact of Green Finance on Regional Low-carbon Transformation: An Analysis of the Mediating Effect Based on Green Innovation
summary: Under the background of "double carbon" goal, green finance is an important institutional arrangement to promote green and low-carbon economic transformation. Based on China's provincial panel data from 2006 to 2023, this paper constructs a comprehensive evaluation index of green finance, and uses panel fixed effect model, mediating effect model and instrumental variable method to test the impact of green finance on regional carbon emission intensity. The results show that the development of green finance significantly reduces regional carbon emission intensity, and the conclusion is still valid after robustness test. Green finance reduces carbon emission intensity by increasing the output of green patents, and green innovation plays a complete intermediary role; Heterogeneity analysis shows that the promotion effect of green finance is more obvious in areas with low economic level and after the low-carbon policy node in 2015. This paper provides empirical evidence for improving the green finance policy system and promoting regional differentiated low-carbon development.

title: Mandatory Environmental Disclosure and Corporate Debt Maturity: Causal Evidence From China
summary: Mandatory environmental disclosure has become a central regulatory instrument for improving corporate transparency, yet its consequences for the structure rather than the cost of corporate financing remain insufficiently understood. Because debt maturity mismatch is a persistent structural impediment to long-term investment in bank-dominated economies, clarifying how disclosure mandates reshape the term structure of corporate debt matters for firms, creditors, and regulators alike. This study uses the 2010 Guidelines for Environmental Information Disclosure by Listed Companies as a quasi-natural experiment and employs a difference-in-differences approach to identify the causal effect of mandatory environmental disclosure on corporate debt maturity. Based on panel data for A-share listed companies in China from 2007 to 2019, the results show that mandatory disclosure significantly shortens debt maturity through a risk revelation mechanism (H1 supported). Pre-policy voluntary disclosure quality acts as a substantial moderator: high-quality prior disclosure attenuates the maturity-shortening effect by approximately 48% (H2 supported). Subgroup analysis by bank dependence reveals the simultaneous operation of supply-side creditor tightening and demand-side managerial adjustment. Mechanism tests show that mandatory disclosure brings previously unobservable environmental compliance costs and liabilities into the public domain, prompting creditors to reassess and reprice environmental risk, thereby reducing debt maturity. Heterogeneity analyses indicate that the effect is concentrated among non-state-owned enterprises and firms in regions with stronger environmental governance. This study contributes to the literature on the financial consequences of mandatory disclosure by extending its scope beyond financing cost to financing structure.

title: Erkenntnis allein reicht nicht – KSL Kupferschiefer Lausitz im Spannungsfeld zwischen Rohstoffsicherheitsbedarf und Realität: „Mining with ESG“ im europäischen Rohstoffrahmen
summary: Das Gesetz zu kritischen Rohstoffen (CRMA, Critical Raw Materials Act) der Europäischen Union hat die strategische Bedeutung heimischer Rohstoffprojekte sichtbar gemacht. Gleichzeitig zeigt sich bei konkreten Vorhaben ein Spannungsverhältnis: Während Europa resilientere Lieferketten, strategische Autonomie und Rohstoffsicherheit einfordert, werden einzelne Projekte vor Ort vor allem an Umweltverträglichkeit, Energieintegration, Kreislaufwirtschaft, regionaler Wertschöpfung und gesellschaftlicher Akzeptanz gemessen. Das Kupferprojekt Spremberg-Graustein-Schleife der KSL Kupferschiefer Lausitz GmbH, Spremberg, in der Lausitz steht exemplarisch für diese neue Bewertungssystematik. Der Beitrag skizziert das Projekt, ordnet seine rohstoffwirtschaftliche und lagerstättenkundliche Bedeutung ein und zeigt, wie ESG-Anforderungen (Environmental, social, and governance, ESG) zunehmend zu technischen Designkriterien werden – von Rückverfüllung und Wasserrecycling über Dry-Stack-Konzepte bis hin zu möglichen regionalen Energie- und Stoffkreisläufen. Der Beitrag basiert auf dem Vortrag des Autors im Rahmen des „MiningForum 2026“ vom 18. bis 19. Juni 2026 in Berlin.

title: Agroecology as a pathway for scaling climate-smart agriculture and strengthening food system resilience in Benin
summary: Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted to address food insecurity, climate variability, and environmental degradation in sub-Saharan Africa. However, evidence on scalable and context-specific pathways for CSA adoption in smallholder systems remains limited, particularly regarding agroecological transitions. This study assesses agroecology as a pathway for scaling CSA and strengthening food system resilience in three communes of Benin (Dassa-Zoumè, Bohicon and Parakou), examining contributions to the three CSA pillars of adaptation, mitigation and productivity. A mixed-methods design combined a structured household survey (n = 210), semi-structured interviews with key informants (n = 32), and secondary agricultural and climate data (2010-2024). A composite resilience index was constructed using principal component analysis (PCA) to compare agroecological and conventional systems. Results show that agroecological farms achieve a 23% higher soil fertility index, a 31% higher resilience capacity, and a 17% reduction in yield variability under climate stress, relative to conventional systems. Crop diversification is 28% higher among agroecological producers, while dependence on synthetic inputs declines by up to 40%, improving system stability and adaptive capacity. Despite these benefits, scaling remains constrained by limited access to climate information services (reported by 35% of respondents), weak extension coverage (30%), and low access to climate finance (20%). The study concludes that agroecology provides a robust, evidence-based pathway for scaling CSA in Benin, and that strengthening digital climate services, extension systems and inclusive climate finance is critical to accelerate resilient and sustainable agricultural transformation in West Africa.

title: Determinasi Pengungkapan Laporan Keberlanjutan pada Sektor Energi dan Bahan Baku
summary: This study is motivated by inconsistent sustainability disclosure practices and greenwashing in natural resource-based industries amid increasing demands for corporate transparency and accountability. The study aims to analyze the influence of profitability, leverage, independent commissioners, and audit committees on Sustainability Report disclosure, with firm size serving as a control variable. The theoretical framework of this study is based on stakeholder theory. The research method employs a quantitative approach using purposive sampling of energy and basic materials sector issuers listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022–2024 period. Secondary data comprising 60 observation samples were obtained from the companies’ annual reports and sustainability reports. Data analysis was conducted using multiple linear regression via IBM SPSS software version 26. The results indicate that profitability, proxied by Return on Assets (ROA), has a significant negative effect on Sustainability Report disclosure. Meanwhile, leverage, independent commissioners, and audit committees do not have a significant effect on Sustainability Report disclosure. This study concludes that profitability is a factor influencing Sustainability Report disclosure, whereas the corporate governance mechanisms examined have not been able to increase in Sustainability Report disclosure. The implications of this research show the importance of increasing corporate commitment to expanding sustainability disclosures and strengthen corporate governance functions to support transparency in reporting. Future research is encouraged to consider other variables and a longer observation period in order to provide a more comprehensive explanation of sustainability reporting.

title: Supply Chain Vertical Shareholding and Corporate ESG Performance: Evidence from China
summary: Using data from Chinese listed firms from 2009 to 2023, this study empirically examines the intensity impact of vertical shareholding among business partners within supply chains on corporate ESG performance, based on a final sample of 349 observations from 134 firms. We discover that the intensity effect of supply chain vertical shareholding on corporate ESG performance is significantly positive, and this positive effect is more pronounced in the S (social) component. Our main findings still hold under robustness testing, such as Heckman’s two-stage method, replacing the variable measurement method, and replacing the model. We also show that the intensity of supply chain vertical shareholding may improve corporate ESG performance by reducing financing costs. Our findings provide theoretical support and empirical evidence for promoting sustainable corporate development and optimizing supply chain cooperation.

title: Agroecology as a pathway for scaling climate-smart agriculture and strengthening food system resilience in Benin
summary: Climate-Smart Agriculture (CSA) is widely promoted to address food insecurity, climate variability, and environmental degradation in sub-Saharan Africa. However, evidence on scalable and context-specific pathways for CSA adoption in smallholder systems remains limited, particularly regarding agroecological transitions. This study assesses agroecology as a pathway for scaling CSA and strengthening food system resilience in three communes of Benin (Dassa-Zoumè, Bohicon and Parakou), examining contributions to the three CSA pillars of adaptation, mitigation and productivity. A mixed-methods design combined a structured household survey (n = 210), semi-structured interviews with key informants (n = 32), and secondary agricultural and climate data (2010-2024). A composite resilience index was constructed using principal component analysis (PCA) to compare agroecological and conventional systems. Results show that agroecological farms achieve a 23% higher soil fertility index, a 31% higher resilience capacity, and a 17% reduction in yield variability under climate stress, relative to conventional systems. Crop diversification is 28% higher among agroecological producers, while dependence on synthetic inputs declines by up to 40%, improving system stability and adaptive capacity. Despite these benefits, scaling remains constrained by limited access to climate information services (reported by 35% of respondents), weak extension coverage (30%), and low access to climate finance (20%). The study concludes that agroecology provides a robust, evidence-based pathway for scaling CSA in Benin, and that strengthening digital climate services, extension systems and inclusive climate finance is critical to accelerate resilient and sustainable agricultural transformation in West Africa.

title: ESG Controversies and Market-Based Firm Performance: The Moderating Roles of Board Independence and Board Gender Diversity in ASEAN-5 Countries
summary: ESG controversies expose firms to reputational, financial, and operational risks, yet research on emerging markets has concentrated on aggregate ESG performance rather than on controversy events, leaving their valuation consequences in Southeast Asia untested. The ASEAN-5 combines high ESG risk exposure with largely voluntary reporting and uneven enforcement across jurisdictions, conditions under which internal board oversight carries more of the monitoring burden. This study examines whether ESG controversies reduce market-based firm performance and whether board independence and board gender diversity moderate that relationship. Refinitiv controversy scores are multiplied by -1 so that higher values denote greater controversy involvement. Using an unbalanced panel of 1,970 firm-year observations from 586 non-financial firms over the 2020-2024 period, the study applies Moderated Regression Analysis within a two-way fixed effects model carrying firm and year effects, estimated with panel-corrected standard errors. Tobin's Q serves as the main dependent variable and market-to-book equity is used for robustness. ESG controversies reduce Tobin's Q by 0.0221 per point (p < 0.01), while the interaction terms for board independence (0.00120) and board gender diversity (0.00190) are positive and significant, indicating that both attenuate the loss. The findings hold under the alternative proxy and a one-year lagged specification addressing reverse causality. Because board composition is not randomly assigned, the evidence is associational rather than causal. The study extends agency theory by treating board attributes as boundary conditions on an externally triggered shock, and it shows that board structure conditions how far sustainability incidents depress valuation in the ASEAN-5.

title: ESG Disclosure and Firm Performance – The Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity
summary: Sustainability practices reflected in the concept of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) are considered capable of reflecting the quality of corporate management as well as the long-term sustainability prospects of a business. One aspect within the governance dimension that has gained increasing attention is gender diversity on the board of directors, which is believed to influence the quality of decision-making and consequently affect corporate profitability and firm value. In line with this, several countries have established policies regarding the proportion of women on boards of directors to promote greater inclusivity. However, countries in the Southeast Asian region have not yet implemented specific written regulations governing the proportion of women on boards of directors. This condition motivates this study to examine the role of gender diversity in moderating the effect of ESG practices on firm performance in Southeast Asia. This study uses a sample of 83 companies from Indonesia, the Philippines, Thailand, and Vietnam during the 2020–2024 period. The independent variable is measured using ESG scores, while the dependent variables are measured using ROA to represent profitability and Tobin’s Q to represent firm value. The moderating variable is measured based on the proportion of women on the board of directors, after which the data panel test is conducted to determine the most appropriate regression model and hypothesis testing method. The result shows that gender diversity play a role in strengthening the effect of ESG practices on firm value, however it doesn’t give any effect in strengthening or weakening the relationship on firm profitability.

title: When Detours Fail: Chokepoint Closures, Bypass-Route Disruption, and the Equity-Market Pricing of Supply-Chain Exposure, 2023–2026
summary: We examine how equity markets price firms’ exposure to maritime chokepoint disruptions when the bypass routes themselves become impaired. The paper develops a 2023–2026 event-study and panel framework centered on the Strait of Hormuz, the Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb corridor, and Saudi Arabia’s East-West Pipeline. We distinguish primary-route exposure from detour vulnerability through a Dual Chokepoint Exposure Index (DCEI) and an Independent Deliverable Capacity (IDC) measure that discounts nominal bypass capacity for terminal, vessel, insurance, inventory, transfer, and onward-route constraints. The design tests abnormal returns and volatility around route-disruption events; identifies a detour-failure premium by comparing primary-closure events with the 20 July 2026 Saudi port-navigation ban and the 10–11 September 2026 East-West Pipeline disruption; traces subsequent changes in cash holdings, inventories, trade credit, leverage, and capital expenditure; and models customer–supplier contagion through network-adjusted exposure. Documented evidence from 2023–2026 shows that maritime stress shifted rather than disappeared as trade was rerouted and that restoration of bypass capacity carried market-relevant information. The framework connects supply-chain resilience to asset pricing and corporate finance by treating independent deliverability—not nominal redundancy—as the financially relevant hedge against chokepoint risk.
