title: Corporate Governance and Firm Value in BRICS: A Cross-Country Analysis of Board Structure, Ownership, and ESG Practices
summary: This study examines the relationship between corporate governance and firm value across the BRICS economies Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa using a sample of 46 large-cap listed firms. We construct a composite Corporate Governance Index (CGI) incorporating board structure, ownership concentration, CEO duality, female director representation, and ESG scores. Our cross-sectional analysis reveals substantial cross-country heterogeneity in governance quality: South Africa and China exhibit the highest mean CGI scores (72.4), while Brazil and India lag behind (57.4 and 60.6, respectively). We document a positive relationship between CGI and Tobin’s Q, but this relationship is contingent on ownership structure and institutional context. Importantly, SOEs are associated with higher CGI scores but lower market valuations, which suggests that formal governance mechanisms may be used to serve political objectives rather than maximizing firm value. We further find that ESG scores complement rather than substitute for traditional governance metrics in predicting firm value. Our findings demonstrate that governance effectiveness is institutionally embedded and reforms cannot be transplanted from developed markets without accounting for local institutional contexts.

title: Improving the mechanisms of corporate governance of an enterprise
summary: This paper examines the current state and directions for improving an enterprise’s corporate governance mechanisms as a decisive prerequisite for enhancing investment attractiveness, transparency, and long-term competitiveness amid the structural transformation of the national economy and the harmonization of Ukrainian corporate legislation with European Union law. It is argued that corporate governance should be viewed not as a set of formal procedures for interaction among a company’s governing bodies, but as an integral system of checks and balances whose effectiveness depends on the coordinated operation of internal and external control mechanisms over management in the interests of shareholders and other stakeholders. Four levels of maturity of an enterprise’s corporate governance system are systematized – basic, regulated, balanced, and strategically integrated – together with their characteristic managerial practices, an indicative maturity index, and typical constraints associated with each level. A comparative analysis of three classical models of corporate governance is conducted – the Anglo-American, the continental European (German), and the insider (transitional) model characteristic of most Ukrainian enterprises – by ownership structure, the role of the supervisory body, and the predominant control mechanism. The toolkit for improving corporate governance is classified into two groups – internal mechanisms (supervisory board structure and independence, board committees, internal control and audit systems, remuneration policy) and external mechanisms (information disclosure, external audit, the market for corporate control, regulatory oversight) – with their functions, implementation mechanisms, and conditions for effectiveness. The study identifies key constraints on improving corporate governance at Ukrainian enterprises: concentrated ownership structures, the formal nature of supervisory board activity, insufficient information disclosure, and a weak market for corporate control. The study substantiates directions for enhancing the effectiveness of corporate governance, including strengthening the independence of supervisory boards, developing audit and remuneration committees, and adapting the disclosure system to the requirements of the Law of Ukraine “On Joint Stock Companies” and the G20/OECD Principles. Enterprise management and owners can use the findings to design corporate governance improvement programs. Keywords: corporate governance, governance mechanisms, supervisory board, joint stock company, transparency, information disclosure, corporate governance maturity, corporate governance model, enterprise competitiveness, European integration.

title: Human–AI Collaboration as a New Governance Paradigm? Unpacking China’s Land Policy Responses to Environmental Pressures and Digital Transformation
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly embedded in land governance, reshaping how environmental pressures and sustainability goals are addressed. Yet the institutional processes through which human–AI collaboration takes shape remain largely unexplored. This study examines whether human–AI collaboration is emerging as a new governance paradigm in China’s land sector, and if so, through what institutional pathways and practical forms it is being articulated and implemented. Drawing on a systematic analysis of 352 policy documents and case studies from coastal regions, the study develops and applies the CTI framework—an analytical lens that integrates Contextual conditions, Technological capabilities, and Institutional arrangements. The findings reveal three interrelated developments: (1) policy discourse constructs a coherent narrative in which environmental pressures and digital transformation jointly create an imperative for change; (2) a systematic division of labor between AI and human officials emerges in policy and is reflected in practice, with AI handling data processing and preliminary screening while humans retain final decision-making, value judgment, and accountability; and (3) this division is being institutionalized through a staged process of policy guidance, pilot mechanisms, and institutional adaptation. These developments suggest that human–AI collaboration may be taking shape as an emerging governance paradigm in land governance, one that is beginning to be codified and tested in policy and practice. The study contributes an integrative analytical framework, specifies the logic of human–machine division of labor, and extends collaborative governance theory beyond its traditional human-centric assumptions. The findings also carry implications for governance contexts where human–AI collaboration is reshaping land governance and other policy domains.

title: Decolonising Corporate Social Responsibility: A Bosadi-Informed Conceptual Framework for Social Sustainability and Restorative Justice in South African Mining Enclaves
summary: Contemporary Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) frameworks increasingly incorporate mitigating gender-based violence (GBV) as a core pillar of social sustainability. However, within emerging markets, particularly inside resource-rich sub-Saharan African extraction zones, these interventions systematically fail. They rely on Western-centric, neoliberal paradigms that prioritise corporate metric compliance over structural, community-level transformation. This conceptual paper introduces a novel theoretical synthesis that bridges decolonial criminology and sustainable development economics. By applying an African-centred Bosadi (womanhood) framework, this study overhauls corporate anti-GBV strategies, moving them away from top-down, state-centric formalistic policing toward localised, indigenous restorative justice systems. Grounded in a transparent, PRISMA-adapted systematic screening of 46 foundational peer-reviewed studies and institutional documents spanning 2015–2026, the paper presents a five-tiered synthesis of qualitative results and discussion. It exposes how multinational mining operations act as systemic criminogenic catalysts by driving extraction-induced land displacement, stripping rural women of agrarian livelihoods, and concentrating cash flow into male-dominated migrant networks. Furthermore, the paper critiques the performative nature of Eurocentric ESG metrics and demonstrates the institutional secondary victimisation inherent in formal policing. As an operational alternative, this study conceptualises the Bosadi-Informed Social Sustainability Framework, anchored by the Lekgotla la Bomme (The Women’s Council), localised grassroots safety hubs, and economic restitution networks. The framework demonstrates that decolonising victimology and restoring African women's financial autonomy are not merely ethical choices, but strict operational prerequisites for achieving genuine, long-term social sustainability and community economic resilience in the Global South.

title: Can New Energy Demonstration City policy improve ESG disclosure quality? Mechanism identification from the perspective of inhibiting corporate greenwashing
summary: Against the backdrop of the advancing "dual carbon" strategy and the global emphasis on sustainable development, ESG disclosure has become a critical dimension of corporate governance. However, the proliferation of ESG controversies, particularly corporate "greenwashing," has challenged the authenticity of these disclosures. This study constructs a quasi-natural experiment based on China's New Energy Demonstration City (NEDC) policy to systematically examine whether green policies can effectively curb ESG greenwashing and improve the quality of ESG disclosure. Using panel data from Chinese listed companies from 2009 to 2023, the study employs a difference-in-differences (DID) model to identify the causal effects. Empirical results show that the NEDC policy significantly reduces corporate greenwashing levels, demonstrating the practical effectiveness of mandatory green regulation in mitigating ESG controversies and improving disclosure quality. Mechanism analysis reveals that policies influence corporate disclosure behavior by enhancing media attention, alleviating financing constraints, and increasing the frequency of institutional research. Heterogeneity analysis indicates stronger governance effects in heavily polluting industries, non-manufacturing enterprises, and resource-based cities. Based on these findings, the study recommends transitioning green disclosure from "voluntary" to "mandatory," and establishing a collaborative supervision mechanism involving institutional investors and media to curb greenwashing, thereby enhancing the execution efficacy of green policies and corporate sustainable governance capabilities.

title: Inclusion financière et nouveaux modèles bancaires au Maroc
summary: Résumé Cette recherche analyse le rôle des nouveaux modèles bancaires dans l’amélioration de l’inclusion financière au Maroc, tout en identifiant les contraintes structurelles, institutionnelles et comportementales susceptibles d’en limiter l’impact. Adopte une approche qualitative, descriptive et exploratoire, l’étude combine l’exploitation de données secondaires issues de rapports institutionnels (Bank Al-Maghrib, Banque mondiale, FMI) et, le cas échéant, une enquête par questionnaire pour analyser les pratiques et perceptions des usagers des services financiers digitaux. L’analyse empirique repose sur des statistiques descriptives, des tableaux comparatifs et une lecture critique des tendances observées. Les résultats montrent que les nouveaux modèles bancaires (notamment le mobile banking, le mobile money et certaines innovations fintech) contribuent significativement à l’accès aux services transactionnels. Cependant, l’inclusion financière reste principalement transactionnelle, avec un impact limité sur l’épargne et le crédit, soulignant que l’innovation technologique seule ne suffit pas à garantir une inclusion financière durable et équitable. L’efficacité des nouveaux modèles dépend d’un écosystème plus large incluant les cadres institutionnels, la littératie financière, la confiance et les facteurs territoriaux. Cette étude apporte une contribution théorique en intégrant les transformations fintech dans la littérature sur l’inclusion financière et offre des éléments pratiques pour les décideurs publics, les institutions financières et les acteurs fintech. Mots clés : Inclusion Financière, Fintech, Mobile Banking, Services Financiers Digitaux, Littératie Financière, Contraintes Institutionnelles, Recherche Exploratoire. Abstract This research analyzes the role of new banking models in improving financial inclusion in Morocco, while identifying the structural, institutional, and behavioral constraints that may limit their impact. Adopting a qualitative, descriptive, and exploratory approach, the study combines the use of secondary data from institutional reports (Bank Al-Maghrib, World Bank, IMF) and, where appropriate, a questionnaire survey to analyze the practices and perceptions of users of digital financial services. The empirical analysis is based on descriptive statistics, comparative tables, and a critical reading of the trends observed. The results show that new banking models (particularly mobile banking, mobile money, and certain fintech innovations) contribute significantly to access to transactional services. However, financial inclusion remains mainly transactional, with limited impact on savings and credit, highlighting that technological innovation alone is not enough to guarantee sustainable and equitable financial inclusion. The effectiveness of new models depends on a broader ecosystem that includes institutional frameworks, financial literacy, trust, and territorial factors. This study makes a theoretical contribution by integrating fintech transformations into the literature on financial inclusion and offers practical insights for policymakers, financial institutions, and fintech players. Keywords: Financial Inclusion, Fintech, Mobile Banking, Digital Financial Services, Financial Literacy, Institutional Constraints, Exploratory Research.

title: Analisis Kesiapan Sumber Daya Manusia (SDM) Akuntan dalam menghadapi Transformasi Sistem Akuntansi Berbasis Big Data
summary: The rapid adoption of Big Data technologies has fundamentally changed accounting information systems, requiring accountants to develop new digital competencies beyond traditional financial reporting. Although technology adoption has been widely investigated, limited empirical evidence explains how organizational and behavioral factors shape accountants' readiness for Big Data-based accounting systems in the Indonesian context. This study aims to analyze the readiness of professional accountants by applying the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT). A quantitative explanatory design was employed using survey data collected from 120 accountants and auditors working in West Java. Data were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to examine the effects of performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, and facilitating conditions on technological readiness. The structural model explained 61.4% of the variance in accountants' readiness (R² = 0.614). The findings indicate that facilitating conditions and performance expectancy significantly enhance readiness, while social influence has a positive but weaker contribution. In contrast, effort expectancy does not significantly affect readiness, suggesting that perceived ease of use is no longer the primary concern among accounting professionals. These findings contribute to the literature by emphasizing that organizational support and perceived technological benefits are more influential than technological simplicity in preparing accountants for digital transformation.

title: Model Akuntansi Digital Berbasis Komunitas untuk Penguatan Tata Kelola Rantai Nilai Ekonomi Hijau: Studi Community-Based Tourism di Desa Oluhuta
summary: This study aims to identify a community-based digital accounting model for strengthening green-economy value-chain governance through Community-Based Tourism (CBT) in Oluhuta Village. A convergent mixed-methods design with qualitative dominance was employed. Data were collected through in-depth interviews with 20 informants, observation, focus group discussions, documentation, and questionnaires. Quantitative data were analyzed descriptively, while qualitative data were examined through data condensation, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification. The findings show that 65% of respondents still rely on manual bookkeeping, only 35% use digital devices for financial recording, and 15% use financial-management applications. Although all respondents own smartphones and 90% have internet access, the use of technology for accounting functions remains limited. Meanwhile, 90% require periodic financial reports, whereas only 30% currently prepare periodic summaries or reports. Integration of qualitative and quantitative evidence produced a model consisting of six processes: transaction recording, information processing, financial reporting, community verification and supervision, information distribution, and decision making. The model is guided by participatory, simple and accessible, transparent, accountable, integrated, and sustainability-oriented principles. The findings indicate that digital accounting in CBT should be treated as a socio-technical governance process linking technology, stakeholder roles, value-flow traceability, and community accountability rather than merely replacing manual records with electronic media.

title: Do Environmental Strategy Policies Improve Financial Performance? the Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity
summary: Environmental strategies are important in modern business, but evidence of their benefits is mixed. The board of directors plays a key role in shaping these strategies, and a diverse board can influence decision-making on environmental strategies. However, the influence of board diversity is still unclear, especially in Indonesia. This research investigates how environmental strategies relate to financial performance and explores the moderating effect of women on the board. Environmental strategies are measured through energy efficiency policy, emission reduction policy, and environmental supply chain management, while financial performance is measured by Return on Assets (ROA). Quantitative panel data regression is used to obtain the results. The study employs purposive sampling to select the sample, resulting in 1,205 unbalanced firm-year observations from 200 firms. This study uses random-effects panel regression with firm-clustered standard errors and robustness tests. Results show energy efficiency policy is positively associated with ROA; emission reduction is negatively associated with ROA, and environmental supply chain management is marginally and negatively associated with ROA. Women on the board significantly moderate the relationships between energy efficiency, environmental supply chain management, and ROA, but not emission reduction. These findings hold after adding year and industry fixed effects. However, the results do not hold with a one-year lag, which means that the association is immediate rather than delayed. This challenges the assumption that environmental strategies consistently benefit or influence financial performance. The study also offers practical and theoretical implications.

title: Three Billion Lives Protected Through the Polycrisis Century: How technological diffusion and sustainable development can reduce human suffering by 2100
summary: The report argues that by 2100, about three billion people—roughly 29% of the projected global population—could be durably protected from major deprivations if technological diffusion and sustainable development are treated as a single, compounding programme rather than separate agendas. This estimate is produced through the Protection Ledger, an accounting model that combines sourced global exposure pools with explicit assumptions about how much of each pool can be closed by 2100 and how much overlap exists between domains.The report identifies five domains where protection is technologically and institutionally feasible: energy and clean air, water and sanitation, food and nutrition, income/finance/connectivity, and climate hazard protection. Together these generate 7.1 billion gross protections, which net to ~3.0 billion unique people after adjusting for overlap. As the document states: “Because the same person is protected in 2.4 domains on average, that nets to about 3.0 billion unique people.”Field evidence—from Bangladesh’s cyclone programme, Kenya’s mobile money, India’s LPG rollout, Gavi’s immunisation system, and Africa’s solar uptake—demonstrates that diffusion works when paired with institutions, finance, and maintenance. The report formalises this through the LIFE Framework (Leapfrog, Institutionalize, Finance, Endure), emphasising that protection is a stock that depreciates unless maintained through shocks.The analysis is set against rising climate hazards, demographic concentration in vulnerable regions, and slowing progress in key SDGs. It warns that the binding constraint is not technology, but absorptive capacity, financial flows, and institutional durability. Scenario pathways range from 1.5 billion protected in a fractured world to 4.2 billion under accelerated convergence.The core claim is deliberately narrow: with existing technologies, paired with stronger institutions and sustained finance, protecting roughly three in ten people alive in 2100 is plausible—not utopian.

title: Paradoks Kenyamanan dan Erosi Pain of Paying Dalam Transaksi Digital: Studi Fenomenologi pada Mahasiswa Akuntansi Universitas Tadulako
summary: The introduction of QRIS (Quick Response Code Indonesian Standard) has revolutionized the way students interact with money, transforming transactional activities into a digital experience that is virtually seamless. This study aims to explore the lived experiences of accounting students at Tadulako University in adopting QRIS, while also capturing the psychological and behavioral effects that emerge in their personal financial management. Using a transcendental phenomenological approach, the essence of these experiences was explored through in-depth interviews with six accounting students. Data was carefully analyzed through the stages of epoché, horizontalization, and the construction of textual and structural descriptions to uncover the deepest meaning of the phenomenon. This study identified three main narratives: (1) Ease of use is not merely a matter of technical efficiency, but rather a multifaceted value that is highly dependent on the students’ daily contexts; (2) The emergence of the “convenience paradox,” in which digital convenience actually fuels consumerist behavior due to the diminishing “pain of paying”; and (3) the gap between knowledge and action. Students’ financial literacy does not automatically serve as a bulwark of self-control in an instant-gratification digital ecosystem. This study also reveals students’ adaptive side when they utilize their digital transaction history as a mirror of accountability to track their finances independently. These findings underscore the need for accounting education to begin addressing aspects of behavior and self-regulation, rather than merely transferring technical knowledge, in order to prepare students to face the psychological complexities of the fintech era.

title: Reconstructing the Brand Image of a Regional Public Hospital through a Multi-Channel Communication Approach amid Digital Transformation: A Case Study in Lhokseumawe
summary: Rapid digital transformation has intensified challenges for regional healthcare institutions in maintaining public trust and institutional credibility. In regional hospital settings, patients increasingly depend on multiple communication channels when evaluating healthcare reliability. However, previous studies on multi-channel communication have focused primarily on general digital marketing without empirically comparing formal institutional versus organic communication in healthcare contexts. This study addresses that gap by examining the contribution of Word of Mouth (WOM), Hospital-Created Social Media, User-Generated Social Media, and Hospital Advertisement to hospital brand image reconstruction. The study operationalizes this communication hierarchy by measuring the statistical influence of each communication channel on patients’ perceptions of institutional brand image. An explanatory quantitative approach was employed involving 100 patients of Rumah Sakit Arun in Lhokseumawe, Aceh, Indonesia, selected through purposive sampling. Multiple linear regression analysis was conducted to evaluate the contribution of each communication variable to hospital brand image reconstruction. The findings reveal that all communication channels positively and significantly influence hospital brand image. Hospital Advertisement emerged as the strongest predictor (t = 5.073), followed by Hospital-Created Social Media (t = 3.806), while User-Generated Social Media and WOM functioned as complementary mechanisms reinforcing institutional credibility. These findings indicate that, within this single-hospital case, formal institutional communication remains more influential than organic communication in shaping patient trust during digital transformation. The study provides context-specific empirical insights exclusively relevant to the operational environment of Rumah Sakit Arun in Lhokseumawe, Aceh, Indonesia.

title: Peran Good Corporate Governance dalam Hubungan Profitabilitas, Risiko, dan Ukuran Perusahaan terhadap ESG
summary: This study aims to examine the effect of internal company characteristics, namely profitability, company risk, and company size, on Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) performance, as well as the moderating role of Good Corporate Governance (GCG). ESG has become an important indicator of corporate sustainability and long-term business performance, particularly in emerging markets where companies are increasingly expected to adopt sustainable and transparent business practices. This research employs a quantitative approach using secondary panel data from companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the 2016–2023 period. The data were collected from annual reports, sustainability reports, and the Refinitiv database, and analyzed using panel data regression with a fixed effect model and Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA). The findings indicate that profitability and company risk have a positive and significant effect on ESG performance, suggesting that companies with stronger financial capabilities and higher risk exposure tend to strengthen ESG implementation as part of their sustainability and risk management strategies. Meanwhile, company size does not significantly affect ESG performance, indicating that larger firms do not necessarily demonstrate better sustainability practices. The results also show that GCG significantly moderates the relationship between profitability and ESG as well as between company risk and ESG, but does not moderate the relationship between company size and ESG. These findings emphasize the importance of effective corporate governance in supporting sustainability strategies and improving ESG performance, particularly in the context of emerging markets such as Indonesia.

title: Three Billion Lives Protected Through the Polycrisis Century: How technological diffusion and sustainable development can reduce human suffering by 2100
summary: The report argues that by 2100, about three billion people—roughly 29% of the projected global population—could be durably protected from major deprivations if technological diffusion and sustainable development are treated as a single, compounding programme rather than separate agendas. This estimate is produced through the Protection Ledger, an accounting model that combines sourced global exposure pools with explicit assumptions about how much of each pool can be closed by 2100 and how much overlap exists between domains.The report identifies five domains where protection is technologically and institutionally feasible: energy and clean air, water and sanitation, food and nutrition, income/finance/connectivity, and climate hazard protection. Together these generate 7.1 billion gross protections, which net to ~3.0 billion unique people after adjusting for overlap. As the document states: “Because the same person is protected in 2.4 domains on average, that nets to about 3.0 billion unique people.”Field evidence—from Bangladesh’s cyclone programme, Kenya’s mobile money, India’s LPG rollout, Gavi’s immunisation system, and Africa’s solar uptake—demonstrates that diffusion works when paired with institutions, finance, and maintenance. The report formalises this through the LIFE Framework (Leapfrog, Institutionalize, Finance, Endure), emphasising that protection is a stock that depreciates unless maintained through shocks.The analysis is set against rising climate hazards, demographic concentration in vulnerable regions, and slowing progress in key SDGs. It warns that the binding constraint is not technology, but absorptive capacity, financial flows, and institutional durability. Scenario pathways range from 1.5 billion protected in a fractured world to 4.2 billion under accelerated convergence.The core claim is deliberately narrow: with existing technologies, paired with stronger institutions and sustained finance, protecting roughly three in ten people alive in 2100 is plausible—not utopian.

title: Algorithmic Governance and Corporate Accountability: A Legal Framework for Responsible AI Deployment in Business Enterprises
summary: The rapid integration of artificial intelligence into corporate decision-making processes has generated significant governance challenges that existing legal frameworks are ill equipped to address. As business enterprises increasingly rely upon algorithmic systems for strategic planning, risk assessment, and operational management, the question of corporate accountability for algorithmic outcomes has become a matter of pressing scholarly and practical concern. This article examines the evolving legal landscape governing artificial intelligence deployment within business contexts across the European Union, the United States, and selected Commonwealth jurisdictions. Drawing upon corporate governance theory, fiduciary duty doctrine, data protection law, and emerging artificial intelligence specific legislation, the article argues that current accountability structures are insufficient to address the unique risks posed by algorithmic decision making. It proposes a principles-based governance model grounded in algorithmic transparency, human oversight, continuous risk auditing, and board level artificial intelligence literacy to harmonise innovation imperatives with legal accountability. The analysis reveals that jurisdictions adopting proactive artificial intelligence governance mandates are creating competitive advantages for their corporate sectors, while lagging regimes risk regulatory arbitrage and litigation exposure. The article concludes with actionable recommendations for boards, compliance officers, and policymakers seeking to navigate the intersection of artificial intelligence innovation and corporate liability.

title: Dividend Policy in the Managerial Ownership-Leverage-Performance Nexus: Evidence from Indonesian Consumer Goods Firms
summary: Consumer goods manufacturers must sustain operations and profitability amid post-pandemic macroeconomic uncertainty. Prior studies report inconsistent effects of managerial ownership and leverage on financial performance, while the mediating role of dividend policy remains underexamined, particularly in Indonesia's consumer goods sector. This study examines the effects of managerial ownership and leverage on financial performance and tests dividend policy as a mediator. The framework integrates Agency Theory, Pecking Order Theory, and Signaling Theory. The population comprised 97 consumer goods manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2020-2024. Purposive sampling yielded 95 firm-year observations from 19 companies. Secondary data were obtained from audited annual reports and official IDX publications and analyzed using IBM SPSS Statistics 25. Managerial ownership and leverage had significant positive effects on dividend policy. Managerial ownership had a significant positive effect on financial performance, whereas leverage had a significant negative effect. Dividend policy did not significantly affect financial performance. Sobel tests further indicated that dividend policy did not mediate either the managerial ownership-financial performance relationship or the leverage-financial performance relationship. The findings suggest that corporate governance alignment and capital-structure decisions influence financial performance more directly than dividend distribution does in this sample.

title: A Dual-Track LLM Framework for Traceable Supplier Delivery Risk Analysis in Electric Vehicle Supply Chains
summary: Supplier delivery instability can disrupt production continuity and increase inventory and coordination pressure. This study proposes a dual-track framework for supplier delivery reliability risk analysis under private, temporally sparse, small-sample enterprise data. A replaceable structured track produces on-time delivery estimates and risk grades for the next observed period. A locally deployed, LoRA-adapted large language model uses retrieved evidence to generate risk explanations and management recommendations. Numeric anchoring, multi-level verification, and provenance auditing connect the two tracks, and the language model does not alter the structured results. Under temporally frozen evaluation, persistence achieves the lowest MAE (0.252), and no learned predictor outperforms this baseline. Factorial experiments show that domain adaptation improves explanation coverage, numeric anchoring brings conditional anchor fidelity to 96.2%, and retrieval reduces the training-value restatement rate from 24.4% to 7.3%. However, 19.5% of outputs in the default configuration still degenerate. A blind evaluation by three domain experts indicates that the overall usefulness of the current explanations remains limited and that they require human review. By linking quantitative estimates with traceable explanations, the framework supports delivery risk analysis under human supervision. Its potential contribution to supply-chain resilience and resource efficiency requires further validation through prospective operational studies.

title: Pengaruh Cash Flow Shenanigans, Corporate Governance, dan Leverage terhadap Kecurangan Laporan Keuangan pada Perusahaan Sektor Consumer Non-Cyclical yang Terdaftar dalam Bursa Efek Indonesia Periode 2021–2023
summary: Kecurangan laporan keuangan merupakan salah satu bentuk kecurangan yang frekuensinya relatif lebih rendah dibandingkan skema kecurangan lainnya, tetapi dapat menimbulkan kerugian yang besar serta menurunkan kepercayaan pemangku kepentingan. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis pengaruh cash flow shenanigans, corporate governance, dan leverage terhadap indikasi kecurangan laporan keuangan pada perusahaan sektor consumer non-cyclical yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia periode 2021–2023. Penelitian menggunakan data sekunder berupa laporan keuangan dan laporan tahunan. Dengan teknik purposive sampling diperoleh 91 perusahaan atau 273 observasi perusahaan dalam 3 tahun. Kecurangan laporan keuangan diukur menggunakan Dechow F-Score, sedangkan cash flow shenanigansdiproksikan dengan days payable outstanding, corporate governance dengan managerial ownership, dan leverage dengan debt to equity ratio. Analisis dilakukan menggunakan regresi data panel dengan fixed-effect model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa cash flow shenanigans berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap indikasi kecurangan laporan keuangan, managerial ownership berpengaruh positif dan signifikan, sedangkan leverage berpengaruh positif tetapi tidak signifikan. Secara simultan, ketiga variabel independen berpengaruh signifikan terhadap indikasi kecurangan laporan keuangan. Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa karakteristik arus kas dan struktur kepemilikan manajerial perlu memperoleh perhatian dalam penilaian risiko pelaporan keuangan pada sektor consumer non-cyclical.

title: Analisis Tantangan Pemungutan Pajak atas Ekonomi Digital di Indonesia dalam Perspektif Kepatuhan dan Regulasi
summary: The rapid growth of the digital economy in Indonesia has significantly increased technology-based economic activities and created substantial opportunities to enhance state tax revenue. However, the borderless nature of digital transactions, relatively low taxpayer compliance, and regula tory frameworks that have not fully adapted to technological developments continue to challenge effective tax collection. This study aims to analyze the challenges of tax collection in Indonesia's digital economy from the perspectives of taxpayer compliance and tax regulation, while identifying strategies to improve the effectiveness of digital tax administration. The research employs a qualitative approach using a literature study method by analyzing scientific journals, tax regulations, government reports, and other relevant publications. The findings indicate that the expansion of the digital economy has broadened the tax base and contributed to increasing government revenue. Nevertheless, the optimization of digital tax collection remains constrained by limited taxpayer awareness and compliance, insufficient supervision of digital transactions, and regulatory frameworks that struggle to keep pace with rapid technological change. The study concludes that optimizing digital tax collection requires synergy between improving taxpayer compliance, developing adaptive tax regulations, strengthening digital tax administration systems, and enhancing institutional coordination to maximize sustainable tax revenue from the digital economy.

title: Financializing the subsoil: Technical disclosure, extractive governance, and asymmetrical accountability in an emerging copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon
summary: This article examines how technical disclosure frameworks contribute to the financialization of mineral resources and shape forms of information disclosure within contemporary extractive governance. Focusing on the Warintza copper project in the Ecuadorian Amazon, the study analyzes how geological information, investor-oriented valuation, environmental considerations, and community relations are structured within corporate disclosure practices. The research is based on qualitative documentary analysis of 18 publicly available disclosure documents produced between 2015 and 2024, including a NI 43–101 technical report, investor presentations, corporate reports, and sustainability-related documents. NI 43–101, a Canadian securities regulation designed to inform investors, structures highly detailed technical disclosures while offering only limited treatment of social and environmental dimensions. The findings show that disclosure systems prioritize geological and investor-oriented information through highly structured quantitative frameworks. Resource classification, drilling results, and corporate narratives of project potential translate geological uncertainty into investor expectations and position the deposit within global investment networks. By contrast, environmental and social dynamics are primarily represented through narrative descriptions that remain only partially integrated into investor evaluation. Rather than framing this as a problem of asymmetrical accountability, the article conceptualizes these dynamics as a condition of asymmetrical information disclosure across distinct governance domains. Different regulatory systems produce differentiated informational outputs, structuring what is disclosed, to whom, and with what level of precision. The findings also indicate that the limited disclosure of social conflict and Indigenous opposition may constitute a material gap in the representation of project-related risks within investor-oriented disclosure systems. By examining disclosure practices in an emerging mining region, the study contributes to debates on extractive governance, transparency regimes, and the financialization of natural resources.

title: Beyond Compliance: AI, GDPR, and ESG as Pillars of Emerging Responsible Corporate Governance in the EU Regulatory Landscape
summary: The European Union’s regulatory landscape is undergoing a fundamental transformation, characterised by the simultaneous emergence of three distinct yet interconnected governance frameworks: the Artificial Intelligence Act, the General Data Protection Regulation, and the expanding ESG obligations encompassing sustainability reporting and due diligence. While traditionally treated as separate compliance domains, this paper argues that these frameworks increasingly operate as interconnected mechanisms of corporate responsibility, requiring companies to integrate technological, informational, social, and environmental considerations into governance processes. Through a systematic analysis of the accountability principles embedded within each framework, this paper demonstrates that AI regulation, GDPR obligations, and ESG requirements are converging into a unified governance architecture that extends corporate responsibility beyond traditional compliance toward proactive, stakeholder-oriented governance. The paper develops an integrated governance model that positions AI governance (algorithmic responsibility), GDPR (information responsibility), and ESG (societal responsibility) as three interconnected pillars of responsible corporate governance in the EU. This paper extends this literature by demonstrating how these three frameworks collectively form an integrated model of corporate responsibility. The paper concludes that the EU is developing a distinctive model where legal compliance becomes the foundation for responsible corporate conduct, signalling a fundamental change in the purpose and practice of corporate governance.

title: Dampak Transformasi Digital Akuntansi terhadap Transparansi Keuangan Dengan Tata Kelola yang Baik sebagai Mediator (Studi Empiris pada Perusahaan Sektor Transportasi yang Terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia)
summary: Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis pengaruh transformasi digital akuntansi terhadap transparansi keuangan dengan Good Corporate Governance (GCG) sebagai variabel pemediasi pada perusahaan sektor transportasi yang terdaftar di Bursa Efek Indonesia (BEI) periode 2021–2024. Penelitian kuantitatif eksplanatori ini menggunakan data sekunder dari laporan tahunan perusahaan. Sampel ditentukan melalui teknik purposive sampling. Pengukuran transformasi digital akuntansi (X) menggunakan metode text mining yang ditransformasikan dengan logaritma natural, transparansi keuangan (Y) diukur melalui nilai absolut discretionary accruals (Modified Jones Model), dan GCG (Z) diukur menggunakan indeks komposit ter-normalisasi. Analisis data dilakukan dengan Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) menggunakan perangkat lunak SmartPLS 4.0. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa transformasi digital akuntansi berpengaruh signifikan dengan arah negatif terhadap nilai absolut akrual diskresioner, yang berarti secara langsung meningkatkan transparansi keuangan (H_1 diterima). Transformasi digital akuntansi juga berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap GCG (H_2 diterima). Namun, GCG tidak berpengaruh signifikan terhadap transparansi keuangan (H_3 ditolak). Akibat terputusnya jalur hilir tersebut, GCG terbukti tidak mampu memediasi hubungan antara transformasi digital akuntansi dan transparansi keuangan (H_4 ditolak). Temuan ini mengonfirmasi Agency Theory dan TOE Framework bahwa teknologi akuntansi bekerja secara mandiri (independent penetration) dalam menekan asimetri informasi dan rekayasa laba, tanpa bergantung pada fungsi birokrasi pengawasan internal. Perusahaan transportasi disarankan untuk memperkuat integrasi sistem digital guna menjamin keandalan dan keterbukaan pelaporan keuangan.

title: Market Performance dalam Perspektif ESG, Investment Opportunity Set dan Financial Risk: Peran Moderasi Board Size
summary: This study examines the effects of ESG Disclosure, Investment Opportunity Set (IOS), and Financial Risk on Market Performance, as well as the moderating role of Board Size in Indonesian ESG-oriented firms. The study contributes to the literature by integrating sustainability disclosure, growth opportunities, and financial risk within a single framework while comparing firms listed in the SRI-KEHATI and SMINFRA18 indices, which represent sustainability-driven and infrastructure-based investment markets. Using a quantitative approach, this study analyzes 84 firm-year observations from 21 companies during the 2021–2024 period. Panel data regression with the Random Effects Model (REM) and robust standard errors is employed for hypothesis testing. The results indicate that ESG Disclosure and Financial Risk do not significantly affect Market Performance, whereas Investment Opportunity Set has a positive effect on Market Performance. Board Size does not moderate the relationship between ESG Disclosure and Market Performance but strengthens the effects of Investment Opportunity Set and Financial Risk on Market Performance. The findings extend signaling theory and stakeholder theory by demonstrating that market participants place greater emphasis on growth opportunities and governance mechanisms than sustainability disclosure alone. Practically, the study highlights the importance of effective board oversight in enhancing market valuation through investment and risk management decisions.

title: ESG Disclosure and Audit Fees: The Moderating Role of Board Gender Diversity in an Emerging Market Context
summary: Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosure has become increasingly important in corporate reporting and accountability; however, evidence regarding its implications for audit pricing remains mixed and is particularly limited in emerging markets, where ESG reporting and assurance practices are still evolving. This study investigates the association between ESG disclosure and audit fees and examines whether board gender diversity moderates this relationship in the Egyptian institutional context. Using a panel dataset of 80 non-financial firms listed on the Egyptian Exchange (EGX100) from 2018 to 2023, comprising 480 firm-year observations, the study applies pooled ordinary least squares and fixed-effects regression models. Sensitivity analyses and instrumental variable estimation are employed as additional robustness and endogeneity checks. The findings indicate a significant positive association between ESG disclosure and audit fees, consistent with the argument that ESG reporting may entail additional audit complexity and risk assessment. Board gender diversity is negatively associated with audit fees and significantly attenuates the positive association between ESG disclosure and audit fees. This moderating pattern is consistent with the view that gender-diverse boards may strengthen governance and the credibility of corporate disclosure, although the underlying auditor-risk and audit-effort mechanisms are not directly tested. The study contributes to the audit-pricing and ESG literature by identifying board gender diversity as an important governance contingency in the association between ESG disclosure and audit fees within an emerging-market setting.

title: Trade and environment governance at the World Trade Organization Committee on Trade and Environment
summary: This PHD reviews the work of the WTO Committee on Trade and Environment and the work outputs that have been generated throughout its 21 years of its existence, and utilizes three theoretical frameworks to aid the analysis and appreciation of the processes and seeming paucity of new rules for trade and environment governance. The work also examines the coherence / conflict dilemma arising from the committee’s tradedevelopment- environment triple-win mandate in the market access area. The research emphasizes the IL-IR dynamic of environmental rule-making and environmental governance that requires a balancing of the three competing frameworks of singular global governance, increased expert and professional bureaucracy, or more community-based localized solutions and multi-faceted institution-building.

title: ESG Practices and SME Performance in Surabaya: Moderating Effects of Digital Transformation and Government Support
summary: This study examines the effect of Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) practices on SME performance in Surabaya, Indonesia, and evaluates the moderating roles of digital transformation and government support. Using a quantitative cross-sectional design, data from 100 Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SME) owners and managers were collected through purposive sampling and analyzed using PLS-SEM with SmartPLS 4. The measurement model met reliability and validity criteria after removing two weak ESG indicators. ESG practices positively affected SME performance (β=0.348, t=3.137, p=0.002), and government support also had a significant effect (β=0.342, t=3.621, p<0.001), while digital transformation showed a positive but non-significant effect (β=0.219, t=1.802, p=0.072). The moderating effects of digital transformation (β=0.108, t=1.423, p=0.155) and government support (β=-0.085, t=0.863, p=0.388) were not significant. The model explained 51.3% of SME performance variance (R²=0.513) and showed positive predictive relevance (Q² predict=0.457). This study is limited by its cross-sectional design and focus on SMEs in a single urban context, which may affect generalizability. The findings contribute to the resource-based and dynamic-capability perspectives by demonstrating that ESG and government support directly enhance SME performance, while digital transformation does not automatically strengthen ESG outcomes.

title: Food loss analysis in the upstream supply chain of large broilers
summary: Food loss in upstream broiler supply chains remains an underexamined challenge with implications for sustainability and economic efficiency. Reported losses highlight systemic inefficiencies but lack integrated, context-specific analysis. This study quantifies broiler food loss across the farm, transport, and slaughter stages in Thailand, identifies key drivers of loss, and proposes mitigation strategies. One-year batch-level data from 79 farms, 6330 trips, and a commercial slaughterhouse were analyzed. Variables included farm scale, flock size, stocking density, transport distance and duration, ambient temperature, humidity, and lairage waiting time. Losses were assessed using descriptive statistics and benchmarked against the literature. Inferential analyses using the Mann–Whitney U and Kruskal–Wallis tests examined group differences, while Spearman's rank correlation assessed variable associations. Count-data models quantified the effects of operational and environmental factors on mortality. Mean on-farm mortality was 2.66%, with higher losses in medium-scale farms, suggesting managerial and resource constraints. Transport losses averaged 0.10%, with regression results indicating significant positive effects of stocking density, temperature, transport distance, and waiting time on mortality. Mortality was highly sensitive to heat stress and longer lairage. Higher humidity and lower temperatures were associated with reduced losses. Slaughterhouse losses (0.04%, excluding contamination) were predominantly due to trimming, with seasonal variation linked to scalding efficiency and disease-related defects. Kruskal–Wallis tests confirmed that environmental factors did not significantly influence processing-stage losses. This study integrates multi-stage evidence into a single supply chain, translating the findings into twelve targeted interventions and four priority measures to reduce losses and enhance supply chain resilience.

title: Reframing mine rehabilitation: a systematic review of adaptive ecological restoration, with special reference to the implications for South Africa's mined landscapes
summary: This paper provides a chronological synthesis of scholarship on adaptive ecological restoration and examines its emergence within mine rehabilitation literature, with particular reference to its implications for South Africa's mining sector. Mining landscapes are characterized by long-term ecological degradation, hydrological instability, and social-ecological vulnerability, while conventional rehabilitation approaches have increasingly been criticized for their limited capacity to respond to environmental uncertainty and changing ecosystem conditions. Adaptive ecological restoration has therefore emerged as a more flexible, learning-oriented, and systems-based approach. The study employed a systematic literature review using peer-reviewed publications sourced from Google Scholar, Scopus, and Web of Science. Literature published between 2000 and 2025 was identified using the keywords “adaptive ecological restoration,” “adaptive management,” “mine rehabilitation,” “mine closure,” “ecological restoration,” and “post-mining landscapes.” Following predefined inclusion and exclusion criteria, the selected studies were analyzed through thematic and chronological synthesis. The paper also presents illustrative South African practice vignettes demonstrating how adaptive restoration principles may be operationalised in post-mining landscapes. The findings identify three phases in the evolution of adaptive ecological restoration scholarship: an early conceptual phase emphasizing ecological resilience and adaptive management; a transitional phase integrating social-ecological systems and environmental governance; and a contemporary phase characterized by stakeholder-inclusive, ecosystem-based, and climate-responsive restoration strategies. The review further identifies core principles, including long-term monitoring, iterative decision-making, ecosystem resilience, community participation, and integrated environmental governance. The study concludes that adaptive ecological restoration provides a robust governance and learning framework for addressing uncertainty in mine rehabilitation, supporting resilient post-mining landscapes, and advancing sustainable restoration practice in South Africa and other mining-dependent regions.

title: Resilience of Critical Defence Buildings and Building Services Infrastructure to Hybrid and Climate Threats: A Multicriteria Assessment Framework
summary: Defence missions depend on buildings, utilities, operational technologies, and external services that increasingly function as an interdependent cyber-physical system. Conventional asset-condition assessments do not adequately capture mission continuity under simultaneous physical, cyber, energy, and climate disruptions. This article proposes a transparent multicriteria framework for the preliminary assessment of the resilience of critical defence building and building-services infrastructure without disclosing sensitive operational data. The framework integrates seven dimensions – governance and continuity, physical and structural safety, energy, water and building services, digital security/operational technology and BIM (Building Information Modelling), logistics and supply chains, and recovery and climate adaptation – operationalized through 28 evidence-based indicators. Equal weighting, a five-level maturity scale, non-compensatory critical thresholds and sensitivity tests limit false precision and make the model auditable.A synthetic, non-operational demonstration case yields an initial score of 50.0/100 and a target score of 79.3/100 after a prioritised package of measures is applied. The contribution is a mission-centred tool suitable for portfolio assessment, investment prioritisation and periodic reassessment.

title: Capital Market Opening-up and High-Quality Innovation of Enterprises
summary: At present, China’s innovation field is facing the structural dilemma of quantity priority and insufficient quality. In the critical window period when the economy turns to high-quality development, the improvement of enterprise innovation level has become an important issue. Based on the quasi-natural experimental scenario of capital market opening, this paper constructs a multi-period difference-in-differences model to test the effect of capital market opening on the quality of enterprise innovation. Both theoretical deduction and empirical test show that capital market opening helps to improve the quality of enterprise innovation, and this effect is more significant in state-owned enterprises and enterprises with overseas business income. From the perspective of mechanism, on the one hand, the opening of capital market promotes the improvement of innovation quality by improving corporate governance and alleviating financing bottlenecks ; on the other hand, due to the increase of stock liquidity, the quality of innovation is suppressed. Overall, the positive effect is dominant. This paper not only expands the theoretical analysis of the relationship between capital market opening and enterprise innovation, but also provides a useful reference for policy practice.

title: Beyond Certification: Vernacular Eco‐Branding and Environmental Legitimacy in Post‐Mining Indonesia
summary: ABSTRACT Dominant frameworks of green innovation often associate environmental responsibility with certification, metrics, formal compliance, and standardized sustainability indicators. These frameworks are less able to explain how environmental legitimacy is constructed by micro and small enterprises operating in peripheral and post‐extractive settings where formal certification systems are absent or inaccessible. This study examines how micro and small enterprises in post‐mining Bangka Belitung, Indonesia, construct environmental legitimacy through vernacular eco‐branding. Drawing on thematic analysis of 32 semi‐structured interviews, field observations, and documentary materials, the study shows that legitimacy is produced through material practices, symbolic communication, audience recognition, and institutional mediation. Enterprises use locally sourced and repurposed materials, community narratives, and reclaimed post‐mining landscapes as visible signals of environmental responsibility. Community recognition and repeated observation function as vernacular accountability, whereas government agencies, CSR programs, exhibitions, and PT Timah‐related support expand visibility but also shape which recovery narratives become publicly recognizable. Vernacular eco‐branding differs from greenwashing when claims are grounded in observable practices, community recognition, and sustained ecological care but becomes vulnerable to symbolic legitimation when selectively amplified. The article contributes to business and society scholarship by showing how small enterprises mediate environmental legitimacy, institutional power, community recovery, and ecological responsibility in post‐extractive economies.

title: Presumptive Taxation in India: Balancing Simplified Taxation with Enhanced Financial Disclosure
summary: Digital transformation is the incorporation of novel technologies across all facets of an organization. This technology integration will need a transformation of conventional business models. Likewise, artificial intelligence has emerged as one of the most transformative technologies of recent decades, possessing significant potential to affect both businesses and individuals. Cognitive methodologies that replicate human behaviour and cognition are yielding sophisticated analytical models that assist firms in enhancing sales and customer engagement, optimizing operational efficiency, refining offerings, and ultimately generating pertinent insights from data. These decision-making methods rely on descriptive, predictive, and prescriptive analytics. This requires a legislative framework that uniformly controls all digital changes across countries and facilitates an effective digital transformation process under defined regulations. Conversely, it is imperative that this digital disruption is not impeded by the regulatory structure. This study will illustrate that AI and digital transformation will be integral to numerous applications and hence will be universally implemented. Nonetheless, this implementation must adhere to established regulations and align with the current circumstances.

title: The secret to retention: How CSR and a positive work environment keep employees engaged in Vietnam’s accommodation sector
summary: Employee retention and organizational citizenship behavior cultivation remain enduring challenges for family-owned businesses in the accommodation sector. Addressing these issues, this study investigates the effects of the work environment and corporate social responsibility (CSR) on employee satisfaction and retention using survey data collected from 400 employees. The analysis demonstrates that a supportive work environment and a strong CSR reputation significantly enhance employee satisfaction, foster organizational citizenship behavior, and strengthen retention. The results underscore the importance of cultivating a service-oriented and employee-centered work climate, alongside implementing responsible and ethical business practices. These findings offer actionable insights for family-owned accommodation businesses, highlighting strategic pathways for improving human resource management, reducing turnover, and encouraging employees to engage in positive discretionary behaviors that contribute to organizational sustainability.

title: Blockchain Traceability and Visual Warning Based on Merkle Tree in Enterprise Data Assetization Transformation
summary: Large enterprise groups face issues such as low efficiency in data traceability and a disconnect between security and visualization in their data assetization transformation. Therefore, this paper raises a security threat perception and visualization warning model based on data visualization and blockchain traceability algorithm. This model combines Merkle Tree (MT), double hash chain, attribute encryption, and zero knowledge proof to achieve lightweight on chain auditing and privacy protection. It also collaborates with ForceTars2 and layered edge binding layout to generate dynamic risk topology, supporting full lifecycle trusted auditing and real-time threat perception. The experiment on the self-made enterprise supply chain threat perception dataset shows that the threat detection rate of the model is 98.11%, the false alarm rate is only 0.82%, the visual cognitive efficiency is 96.83%, the trusted data asset utilization rate is 96.82%, and the delay is controlled within 100 ms. Superior to existing mainstream solutions such as lightweight tracking algorithms based on MT and attribute based encryption privacy protection algorithms. The experimental results demonstrate that the model has good accuracy and applicability in enterprise level data security governance, providing an integrated governance solution with high concurrency, low latency, and high trustworthiness for data assetization transformation.

title: Peran Risiko Keuangan dan Tata Kelola Terhadap Kinerja Perusahaan Perbankan
summary: This study aims to analyze the effects of financial risk and corporate governance characteristics on the performance of banks listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX). Financial performance is measured using Return on Assets (ROA) as the dependent variable. The independent variables include liquidity risk, credit risk, operational risk, board size, board meeting frequency, board independence, and operational efficiency. Bank size and leverage are also incorporated as control variables to strengthen the analytical model. The sample consists of 48 banks listed on the IDX during the 2020–2024 period. Panel data regression analysis was conducted using EViews 9. The model selection tests indicate that the fixed effects model is the most appropriate specification. The novelty of this study lies in the inclusion of operational efficiency to examine its role in enhancing bank financial performance and as an indicator of a bank’s ability to effectively manage operational resources amid financial risks. The results show that liquidity risk, credit risk, and board meeting frequency have significant negative effects on financial performance, whereas bank size has a significant positive effect. Meanwhile, operational risk, board size, board independence, operational efficiency, and leverage do not exhibit statistically significant effects in the hypothesized directions. These findings highlight the important role of risk management and corporate governance in optimizing bank profitability. Therefore, banks should strengthen risk controls, improve operational efficiency, and enhance governance quality to achieve more sustainable financial performance.

title: Pengaruh Mekanisme Internal Corporate Governance terhadap Tingkat Leverage Keuangan pada Perusahaan Manufaktur yang Terdaftar di BEI Periode 2022-2024
summary: This study aims to test and analyze the influence of the internal corporate governance mechanism consisting of an independent board of commissioners, managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and audit committee on the level of financial leverage (Debt to Equity Ratio) in manufacturing companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2022-2024 period. This study uses a quantitative approach with a sample of 57 companies selected through the purposive sampling method. The analysis technique used is panel data regression with a Random Effect Model (REM) model based on the results of the Chow Test, Hausman Test, and Langrange Multiplier Test. The results of the study show that simultaneously the four independent variables have a significant effect on leverage. However, partially, only institutional ownership has a negative and significant effect on leverage, while independent board of commissioners and managerial ownership have no significant effect on the negative direction, and the audit committee does not have a significant effect on the positive direction. These findings indicate that institutional investors have a more effective supervisory role than other internal governance mechanisms in controlling corporate debt policies.

title: A Systematic Review of the Impact of E-Governance on Competitive Advantage in the Government Sector in the Sultanate of Oman
summary: The present research aims to explore the role of e-governance in enhancing competitive advantage in the government sector in Oman. The paper examines the impact of variables such as digital transformation, service quality, transparency, innovation, and technological capabilities on government performance and strategic positioning in line with Oman Vision 2040. This study uses a systematic literature review methodology. It scans recent research on e-governance, digital transformation, innovation in the public sector, and competitive advantage. The literature reviewed includes both empirical and conceptual studies published during (2018 – 2025). The results also show that e-governance has a positive impact on competitive advantage in the public sector through its links to service quality, operational efficiency, transparency, digital services, and citizen satisfaction. Furthermore, this relationship is mediated by IT governance and dynamic capabilities to enable the sustainability of competitive advantage. Moreover, this relationship is mediated by dynamic capabilities and IT governance, facilitating the sustainability of competitive advantage. The research offers insights to policymakers and government leaders in Oman on the need to strengthen digital governance efforts and competitive positioning in government. This study contributes to the literature by integrating e-governance and competitive advantage perspectives in the Omani government sector.

title: PENGARUH GREEN ACCOUNTING, SUSTAINABILITY REPORT DAN GOOD CORPORATE GOVERNANCE TERHADAP NILAI PERUSAHAAN
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of Green Accounting, Sustainability Reporting, and Good Corporate Governance (proxied by institutional ownership) on the Firm Value of mining companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange for the 2021–2024 period.The research employs a quantitative approach using a causal-associative method. The data used is secondary, consisting of annual reports from 50 companies selected through purposive sampling, resulting in 200 observations. The results indicate that, partially, Green Accounting does not have a significant effect on Firm Value. Sustainability Reporting has a negative and significant effect on Firm Value, while Good Corporate Governance, as proxied by institutional ownership, also does not have a significant effect on Firm Value. Simultaneously, Green Accounting, Sustainability Reporting, and Good Corporate Governance have a significant influence on Firm Value. This demonstrates that integrating these three elements is a strategic step for management to meet regulatory expectations while simultaneously creating added value for shareholders

title: The Role of Internal Audit in Enhancing Corporate Governance Principles and Risk Management in the Saudi Arabian Private Sector
summary: This study investigated the contribution of internal audit to improving corporate governance principles and strengthening risk management practices in Saudi private sector organizations. Amid increasing regulatory, operational, and technological pressures, internal audit has evolved beyond its traditional compliance function to become a governance mechanism that promotes transparency, accountability, and organizational resilience. The study adopted a quantitative research design based on the positivist paradigm. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire completed by professionals involved in internal audit and risk management functions. Descriptive statistics, reliability analysis, t-tests, ANOVA, chi-square tests, and regression analysis were conducted using SPSS. The findings indicate that internal audit efficacy significantly improves corporate governance implementation and risk management practices by enhancing transparency, accountability, board oversight, ethical compliance, and risk identification, assessment, and mitigation. Overall, strengthening internal audit capacity, independence, and integration with governance and risk management promotes organizational control, sustainable performance, effectiveness, and resilience.
