title: Energy infrastructure construction and enterprises’ Artificial Intelligence development: Evidence from China’s ultra-high voltage transmission projects
summary: Ultra-high voltage (UHV) transmission projects are a key component of China's energy supply-side reforms, improving the efficiency and reliability of the power system. While their macro-level importance is well recognized, evidence on their impact on firm-level artificial intelligence (AI) development remains limited. This study addresses this gap by exploiting the staggered rollout of UHV transmission projects across prefecture-level cities as a quasi-natural experiment. Using a multi-period difference-in-differences (DID) approach on a panel of Chinese listed enterprises from 2007 to 2023, this study finds that UHV transmission projects significantly promote enterprises' AI development. The effect is stronger for non-state-owned enterprises, enterprises located in inland regions, enterprises with CEO-chair duality, and high-tech enterprises. Mechanism analyses show that UHV transmission projects enhance enterprises' AI development by strengthening technological innovation, expanding enterprises' organizational resource base, and improving regional financial development. Further analyses indicate that UHV transmission projects also improve resource allocation efficiency and alleviate development bottlenecks. By linking physical energy infrastructure with firm-level AI development, this study highlights the importance of reliable electricity supply for technology adoption and digital transformation.

title: Digital Transformation in Government Auditing Using Artificial Intelligence: A Proposed Framework for Enhancing Transparency and Sustainability in Supreme Audit Institutions
summary: تناولت هذه الدراسة التحول الرقمي في المراجعة الحكومية باستخدام تقنيات الذكاء الاصطناعي بوصفه توجهاً استراتيجياً لتطوير دور الأجهزة العليا للرقابة المالية والمحاسبة وتعزيز قدرتها على تحقيق الشفافية والمساءلة والاستدامة. وتنطلق الدراسة من تنامي استخدام الذكاء الاصطناعي وتحليل البيانات في البيئة الرقابية الدولية، في حين لا تزال العديد من الأجهزة الرقابية تعتمد بدرجات متفاوتة على أساليب المراجعة التقليدية. هدفت الدراسة إلى تحليل مجالات توظيف الذكاء الاصطناعي في المراجعة الحكومية، بما يشمل تحليل البيانات الضخمة، والتعلم الآلي، ومعالجة اللغة الطبيعية، والأتمتة الروبوتية للعمليات، إلى جانب تحليل الأدبيات والدراسات السابقة واستعراض تجارب رقابية دولية وعربية، وبناء إطار الرقابة الرقمية الذكية الخماسي المتوازن (Balanced Five-Dimensional Smart Audit Framework). ويتكون الإطار من ثلاثة أبعاد بنائية: التقني، والمؤسسي/الحوكمي، والبشري/المعرفي، وبُعدين عابرين هما الأخلاقيات وإدارة المخاطر، والاستدامة المؤسسية والرقمية. واعتمدت الدراسة المنهج الوصفي التحليلي، من خلال تحليل الدراسات والوثائق العلمية والمؤسسية ذات الصلة، ومراجعة تقارير INTOSAI وIDI وOECD، وتحليل ثلاث تجارب رقابية هي اليونان والأردن ومصر. وأظهرت النتائج أن نجاح التحول الرقابي الذكي لا يعتمد على التكنولوجيا وحدها، بل يتطلب تكاملاً بين الجاهزية الرقمية والحوكمة والقدرات البشرية والضوابط الأخلاقية وإدارة المخاطر، مع الحفاظ على الحكم المهني للمراجع. كما قدمت الدراسة خارطة طريق تدريجية تبدأ بتقييم الجاهزية والمشروعات التجريبية، ثم التوسع وبناء القدرات، وصولاً إلى التكامل والمراجعة المستمرة القائمة على البيانات.

title: Corporate Social Responsibility and Carbon Efficiency in the Airline Industry: Implications for Sustainability and Corporate Value
summary: The airline industry faces increasing pressure to balance economic performance with social and environmental responsibilities. This study investigates the influence of corporate social responsibility (CSR) on corporate value, incorporating the moderating role of carbon performance and the mediating effect of customer perception. A comprehensive CSR assessment framework based on ISO 26000 is developed across six dimensions: organizational governance, labor practices, the environment, consumer issues, fair operating practices, and community involvement. Panel data from 20 global airlines over 2017–2024 are used to test the proposed relationships. The results indicate that higher CSR scores are positively associated with corporate value and that customer perception, measured through Skytrax ratings, provides partial mediation. In addition, lower unit carbon intensity strengthens the positive CSR–value relationship, highlighting the importance of verifiable carbon performance in improving the financial returns to CSR. These findings distinguish broad CSR engagement from operational carbon outcomes and reinforce the role of carbon efficiency in sustainable airline strategy.

title: Pengaruh Fraud Diamond Terhadap Kecurangan Laporan Keuangan dengan Moderasi Transparansi pada Sektor Industri (2021–2024)
summary: Financial statement fraud remains a serious issue that can reduce the quality of financial information, harm stakeholders, and decrease public trust in companies. This study aims to analyze the effect of Fraud Diamond Theory, consisting of pressure, opportunity, rationalization, and capability, on financial statement fraud with financial statement transparency as a moderating variable in industrial sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2021–2024 period. This study employed a quantitative approach using secondary data obtained from company financial statements. The sampling technique used purposive sampling. Financial statement fraud was measured using the Beneish M-Score, while hypothesis testing was conducted using logistic regression analysis with SPSS version 26. The results showed that pressure, opportunity, rationalization, and capability had no significant effect on financial statement fraud. In addition, financial statement transparency was unable to moderate the effect of these four variables on financial statement fraud. These findings indicate that financial statement transparency has not been effective in strengthening or weakening the relationship between Fraud Diamond factors and financial statement fraud. Therefore, companies need to strengthen internal control systems and corporate governance comprehensively to minimize the risk of financial statement fraud.

title: Analisis Penerapan Akuntansi pada Instrumen Lindung Nilai Berdasarkan PSAK 71 dalam Meminimalisir Risiko Eksposur Transaksi
summary: This study aims to compare the effectiveness of three hedging techniques : forward contract hedging, money market hedging, and currency option hedging and to evaluate their eligibility for hedge accounting under PSAK 71 based on three qualifying criteria: economic relationship, credit risk effect, and hedge ratio, in mitigating transaction exposure risk arising from import liabilities. The study employs a quantitative approach using secondary data from annual reports of metals and minerals subsector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during 2020–2024. The sample comprises an unbalanced panel of 39 firm-year observations from eight companies. Data were analyzed using the Dollar Offset Method to assess compensation levels and Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) regression, supported by classical assumption tests. The findings indicate that all three hedging techniques effectively mitigate transaction exposure risk, although with different compensation profiles. Forward contract hedging and currency option hedging satisfy the classical assumption tests, whereas money market hedging exhibits mild heteroscedasticity that likely reflects differences in transaction scale and interest rate differentials across sample companies. The Dollar Offset Method confirms that the compensation levels of all three techniques are consistent with the principle-based approach of PSAK 71, which replaces the 80%–125% quantitative threshold under PSAK 55. Furthermore, the evaluation demonstrates that all three hedging techniques satisfy the qualifying criteria for hedge accounting under PSAK 71, with forward contract hedging and currency option hedging exhibiting the most precise economic relationship and hedge ratio, while money market hedging requires more comprehensive documentation of hedge ineffectiveness and periodic rebalancing to maintain hedge ratio consistency. These findings provide empirical support for the adoption of hedge accounting under PSAK 71 by Indonesian mining companies to enhance financial reporting stability and better reflect corporate risk management activities.

title: Environmental courts, industrial pollution, and grain production: the reach of judicial environmental enforcement in Chinese cities
summary: Judicial environmental enforcement operates through litigation, therefore the entitlements it protects are only binding when a discharge can be traced to an identified source within the jurisdiction that adjudicates it. This delineation logic implies that specialized environmental courts reduce pollution selectively, and that their reach stops short of sectors they do not adjudicate. The second implication is important for food systems, because increasing environmental governance in agrarian economies is widely expected to cost local food production. We test both using the staggered establishment of environmental courts in Chinese prefecture-level cities during 2003–2018, utilizing a common sample of 4,168 city-year data from 285 cities, 109 of which had a court. Two-way fixed-effects and Callaway–Sant’Anna estimates are shown on identical samples, together with a balanced panel, event-time paths, adoption-hazard and trend diagnostics, and HonestDiD sensitivity. Both estimators include industrial wastewater density, which is a point-source discharge that occurs within municipal boundaries. Sulfur dioxide, which disperses across jurisdictions, is only considered in pooled estimate, and the formal contrast between the two responses is negative in every cohort-aware specification. Sensitivity analysis limits how far these conclusions travel: the wastewater sign holds under trend assumptions similar to the observed pre-establishment pattern, and the cross-pollutant gap is smaller than this design resolves. Grain production per resident does not decline, and equivalence tests limit the largest decline these data admit. Specialized environmental adjudication develops as a selective, attribution-dependent enforcement whose reach is limited to what a court can attribute, with no detectable impact on local grain production.

title: Beyond Efficiency: Governance, Accountability, and Institutional Capacity in AI-Driven Public Administration
summary: Digital transformation has evolved from an administrative modernization agenda into a structural dimension of governance, with artificial intelligence (AI) increasingly reshaping how public institutions organize, decide, and interact with citizens. While AI offers important opportunities for responsiveness, innovation, and service improvement, its implications for accountability, legitimacy, transparency, and public trust remain insufficiently understood; this study asks how AI is redefining governance capacity in public administration. Drawing on the literature on public administration, digital governance, and public sector innovation, the study develops a conceptual framework examining both the capacity gains and risks of AI integration, treating digital transformation as a governance challenge involving administrative reform, public value creation, democratic oversight, and institutional adaptation rather than a purely technical matter. The analysis shows that AI can strengthen evidence-based policymaking, accelerate administrative processes, and personalize service delivery, but that these gains may be offset by algorithmic bias, opacity, accountability gaps, and digital exclusion when adopted without adequate institutional safeguards. The paper’s value lies in showing that AI’s contribution to public management depends on the institutional, legal, and normative environment in which it is embedded, which in turn requires regulatory capacity, qualified human resources, and mechanisms for oversight and contestability. Future research should test this framework empirically across diverse administrative contexts. Keywords: Artificial intelligence, Digital transformation, Public management, Accountability, Institutional capacity.

title: Pengaruh Profitabilitas, Solvabilitas, dan Cost to Sales Ratio terhadap Manajemen Laba pada Perusahaan Sektor Industrial di Bursa Efek Indonesia
summary: This study examines the effect of profitability (ROE), solvency (DAR), and Cost to sales ratio on earnings management in industrial companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2020–2024). Using purposive sampling , 38 companies (190 firm-year observations) were analyzed via panel data regression (EViews 12), with earnings management measured using the Stubben (2010) discretionary revenue model and a dummy variable controlling three outlier observations. Results show profitability, solvency, and Cost to sales ratio do not partially affect earnings management (prob. 0.4097; 0.5181; 0.8114; p > 0.05), but jointly affect it significantly (F = 7.189892; prob. 0.000021; p < 0.05). Adjusted R-squared of 11.58% indicates most variation is explained by factors outside the model, such as corporate governance, audit quality, and firm size. Findings suggest earnings management during the post-pandemic recovery is driven by combined financial characteristics rather than a single indicator, contributing new evidence on cost efficiency (Cost to sales ratio) as an underexplored factor in earnings management research.

title: Impact of Cybersecurity Threats on Consumer Trust in Digital Banking: Reference to the Indian Banking Ecosystem
summary: As India trudges towards a $1 trillion digital economy, the banking sector has transitioned from a "branch-first" to a "digital-only" philosophy. However, this metamorphosis is shadowed by an escalating landscape of cyber threats. This paper investigates the symbiotic affiliation amid cybersecurity resilience and consumer conviction within the Indian context. Utilizing a mixed-methods slant, the study analyses recent trends like AI-driven phishing and "bank.in" domain migrations mandated by the RBI. Findings suggest that while UPI-led expediency is high, "trust-deficit" remnants a significant fence for high-value digital transactions. The paper concludes with premeditated endorsements for banks to move yonder technical compliance toward "Trust-as-a-Service." Key words – Economy, Digital Banking, RBI, Consumer, Frauds, Deepfake scams, Indian Banking

title: A review of green supply chain management
summary: Green supply chain management is a comprehensive approach that balances maximum profitability with minimizing environmental impact. This approach covers the entire supply chain (from raw material procurement to product recycling) by transforming a traditional supply chain into a green supply chain, enhancing organizational performance and increasing competitiveness. This study is developmental in terms of its purpose. The method employed for gathering data in this research involved conducting a systematic review. The collected sources included reputable articles related to green supply chain management keywords. The findings show that initially, 343 articles were identified based on the keywords; after filtering and closer examination, this number was reduced to ten articles. The results indicate that the successful implementation of green supply chain management not only reduces pollution and waste but also offers benefits such as improved brand image, reduced long-term costs, increased resource efficiency, and achieving a competitive advantage. Finally, strategies such as collaboration among supply chains, enhancing green supply chain management performance, and similar recommendations are provided. The main research question is: "What are the main variables in implementing green supply chain management?" Experts have examined and confirmed that these include process-related factors such as green design, green purchasing, and competition

title: Pengaruh Digitalisasi Sistem Informasi Akuntansi dan Transparansi Informasi Keuangan terhadap Minat Investasi dengan Persepsi Nasabah sebagai Variabel Mediasi
summary: The rapid development of digital technology has encouraged financial institutions to implement digital-based accounting information systems and enhance financial information transparency to improve service quality for customers. As one of Indonesia’s non-bank financial institutions, PT Pegadaian has implemented digital transformation through the Pegadaian Digital (Tring!) application, which facilitates customers in conducting various gold investment transactions. However, the convenience offered by digital services does not necessarily lead to an increase in customers’ investment interest. Therefore, this study aims to analyze the effect of Accounting Information System Digitalization and Financial Information Transparency on Investment Interest, with Customer Perception serving as a mediating variable at PT Pegadaian Sukabumi Branch. This study employed a quantitative approach using a survey method involving 89 customers of PT Pegadaian Sukabumi Branch who use the Pegadaian Digital (Tring!) application. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling–Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) with SmartPLS 4 software. The results indicate that Accounting Information System Digitalization has no significant effect on either Customer Perception or Investment Interest. In contrast, Financial Information Transparency has a positive and significant effect on both Customer Perception and Investment Interest. Furthermore, Customer Perception has a positive and significant effect on Investment Interest. The mediation analysis reveals that Customer Perception does not mediate the relationship between Accounting Information System Digitalization and Investment Interest, but it partially mediates the relationship between Financial Information Transparency and Investment Interest. These findings indicate that Financial Information Transparency plays a more dominant role than Accounting Information System Digitalization in enhancing customers’ investment interest.

title: Does supply chain digitalization affect corporate tax avoidance?
summary: Purpose The impact of supply chain digitization on corporate tax avoidance is a critical yet under-explored issue in tax governance within the digital economy. Against this backdrop, this paper aims to conduct an in-depth analysis of the underlying mechanisms and boundary conditions governing the relationship between the two. Design/methodology/approach This paper uses data from Chinese A-share listed companies (2011–2022) and uses a two-way fixed-effects model to test for direct effects, as well as conducting robustness tests, mediation tests, moderation tests and heterogeneity tests. Findings Supply chain digitalization significantly inhibits corporate tax avoidance, and the alleviation of financing constraints exerts a positive mediating effect in this relationship. Public scrutiny reinforces this curbing effect, while management myopia weakens it. Furthermore, this effect exhibits significant heterogeneity across different firms. In terms of economic consequences, the curbing effect of supply chain digitization on tax avoidance further reduces corporates’ risk-taking and enhances their reputation. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this paper provides the first empirical evidence that supply chain digitalization curbs corporate tax avoidance. By examining moderating effects and heterogeneous roles, and by linking the reduction in corporate tax avoidance to subsequent risk-taking and reputational outcomes, this paper further extends the boundaries of the literature in relevant fields. These findings offer several policy implications.

title: Legitimizing segregation, subsidizing captivity: Mexican state presence in corporate housing policy for farmworkers
summary: Abstract In Mexico, agroindustrial enclaves are hyper-segregated landscapes where transnational business groups build and restore overcrowded barracks, militarized bunkhouses, and other precarious housing developments for seasonal agrarian laborers. Disguised as employment benefits, corporate social responsibility practices, and social development initiatives, these agribusiness housing policies have functioned for decades as labor and spatial control measures against migrant farmworkers. Drawing on more than ten years of ethnographic and historical research in Mexico, the article questions these apparently stateless landscapes and policies by spotlighting the systematic actions of government agencies in reproducing agribusiness housing models of precarity, rule, and isolation. The article presents two case studies, a segregationist barracks system in a sugarcane valley and a captivity model of agricultural fields in a grape-exporting desert, to analyze the essential presence of the Mexican state in legitimizing and subsidizing these regional agribusiness housing policies. Bridging anthropological studies of state formation, critical border studies, and the tradition of studying the segregation and settlement of migrant farmworkers in Mexico and worldwide, this article contributes an ethnographic analysis showing that the state is neither absent nor negligent in the everyday operation of violent corporate housing policies. On the contrary, government agencies at different levels administer, monitor, and make legible the segregation and captivity of workers within contemporary agrarian capitalist geographies.

title: Organizational Dysfunction and the Loss of Technology and Talent in Modern Motorsports in Japanese
summary: In MotoGP—the pinnacle of modern motorcycle road racing—Honda Racing (hereinafter HRC) and Honda Motor Co., Ltd. (hereinafter Honda), which once boasted overwhelming dominance, have languished at the bottom of the constructors' standings (10th place or lower) since the mid-2020s; they retain no trace of the absolute supremacy they once commanded in the paddock. This article frames this technical and competitive dysfunction not merely as a "failure in machine development," but as a process of organizational collapse and the loss of vital talent (core competencies) precipitated by what might be termed an "internal hostile takeover" driven by corporate management. It then empirically examines the parallels between this situation and concepts found in corporate governance and organizational theory.

title: Asset Use Risk Management in the Agro-Industrial Complex: Theoretical and Methodological Foundations and Practical Solutions
summary: This article examines the asset use risk management process in the agro-industrial complex (AIC) under conditions of increased uncertainty, climate change, and digital transformation. The article explores the nature and classification of risks specific to tangible, intangible, and biological assets in the AIC. Based on a systems-process approach and international standards (ISO 31000, COSO ERM), an adapted risk management model has been developed that takes into account seasonality, biological cycles, technological vulnerability, and regulatory aspects of agricultural production. An algorithm for integrating risk-based management into corporate planning systems, digital platforms for precision farming, and predictive maintenance is proposed. Particular attention is paid to the development of key risk indicators (KRIs), scenario modeling, insurance and hedging instruments, and organizational and managerial mechanisms for implementing a risk culture. The study's results can be used by agricultural holding management, government regulatory agencies, research organizations, and educational institutions when developing sustainable development strategies for the agro-industrial complex.

title: Organizational Dysfunction and the Loss of Technology and Talent in Modern Motorsports in Japanese
summary: In MotoGP—the pinnacle of modern motorcycle road racing—Honda Racing (hereinafter HRC) and Honda Motor Co., Ltd. title: Endogenous Collapse: Optimising for Fragility — The First Theorem of Possibility Space Theory
summary: A system can be structurally intact and functionally collapsed. The alternatives are still on the map. They are no longer usable. Nothing was destroyed. The system spent them. This paper introduces Possibility Space Theory, a framework for describing dynamic constrained systems using a unified approach. It is substrate independent. It applies wherever constrained actualisation is the relevant dynamic: supply chains, financial networks, institutions, ecologies. And to the articulation between geopolitics and economics that first motivated it. Its central claim is that the board on which entities move is not a static stage. It is a structure reconfigured by the system's own history. Three operators, Access, Friction and Elasticity, capture the three temporal moments of any transition. What was available, what it cost, what remains. A Transition Theorem shows the decomposition is forced. The paper proves a non-trivial result within the framework. Under maintenance-by-use and bounded bandwidth, the strategy that minimises traversal cost monotonically increases the friction of the alternatives it forgoes. Access remains unchanged. Elasticity collapses. The collapse is endogenous, invisible, structural. It requires no external shock. This challenges the assumption that price signals capture systemic risk. Concentration on efficient routes atrophies alternatives and the collapse is invisible to the indicators used to monitor it. The framework does not replace existing tools. It gives them a common language. Written for researchers and practitioners working on systemic risk, complexity, network fragility, resilience and political economy. The framework was first developed in applied analysis of the 2026 Hormuz crisis. title: Bad news travels fast: comment letters, investor trading behavior, and stock liquidity
summary: Purpose This study investigates the effect of real-time disclosed regulatory comment letters on corporate stock liquidity and explores the underlying driving factors, using a unique sample from the Chinese stock market. Leveraging the timely nature of comment letter issuance and the subsequent reply mechanism in China, the paper aims to unambiguously identify the market consequences of comment letters and the associated mechanisms. Specifically, we focus on the role of different investor groups' trading behaviors, particularly retail net-sells and investor sentiment, in mediating the liquidity changes. Ultimately, this research provides new insights into the market monitoring effect of comment letters and regulatory enforcement in emerging markets. Design/methodology/approach We manually collected a sample of comment letters and their real-time replies issued by the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (SZSE) from 2014 to 2018. We employ event study methodology and Difference-in-Differences (DiD) models to analyze the changes in inquired firms' stock liquidity, measured by the Quoted Spread (QS) and Effective Spread (ES), following the comment letter disclosure. We proxy retail investor trading behavior using net sell volumes of small transactions and examine the driving role of retail net-sells and negative retail sentiment in the observed liquidity decline. This design leverages the unique institutional setting of real-time disclosure in the Chinese market. Findings The findings demonstrate that the stock liquidity of inquired firms significantly declines immediately after the comment letter disclosure. However, this decline does not significantly recover after the firms issue their subsequent replies. The short-term deterioration in liquidity is mainly driven by intense retail net-selling activities and heightened negative retail sentiment. Furthermore, the liquidity exhibits only a partial recovery over a longer period, extending up to 60 days post-disclosure. Finally, the negative effect of comment letters on stock liquidity is more pronounced for firms characterized by higher information uncertainty and greater corporate governance deficiencies. Originality/value This study uses the real-time disclosure mechanism of comment letters in the Chinese market to examine their impact on the trading behavior of different investor groups, particularly retail investors, thus mitigating concerns about insider trading. It confirms a significant regulatory effect of comment letters as a non-punitive regulatory tool in the capital market, filling a gap in the literature regarding their efficacy. By focusing on the unique emerging market context of China, this research enriches the global understanding of comment letters' impact and offers important practical implications for improving regulatory instruments worldwide.

title: Intangible Input Complementarities Along Supply Chains
summary: We study whether buyer-supplier relationships feature complementarities in intangible inputs. Using administrative data from the Dominican Republic, we show that foreign demand routed through intangible-intensive buyers raises a supplier’s own intangible purchase share, while demand from other buyers has no effect. Two event studies on firms not previously exposed to intangible-producing partners provide further evidence. Forming a first link with an intangible-industry buyer raises the probability of any intangible purchase by about 4 percentage points, and hiring a worker from an intangible-producing firm for the first time has an effect of the same size. A general equilibrium production network model with endogenous intangible input use, knowledge transfer through worker mobility, and endogenous intangible prices implies that supply-chain complementarities account for about 15 percent of aggregate intangible purchases and about 4 percent of output.

title: AI Agent–Driven Autonomous Service Delivery in Saudi Arabia: A Framework for Intelligent Telecom and Enterprise Operations under Vision 2030
summary: The telecommunications and enterprise sectors in Saudi Arabia are progressing from digitally based service operations towards more autonomous operating models in which artificial intelligence is able to understand objectives, identify situations, coordinate tools, and carry out specific actions. This report looks at the way in which AI agents can help to achieve autonomous service delivery in both telecom and enterprise operations while at the same time meeting the requirements relating to reliability, governance, cybersecurity, and human accountability that are linked to Saudi Vision 2030. The study makes use of a structured integrative review of peer-reviewed literature published between 2020 and 2025, with a focus on agentic AI, zero-touch network and service management, intent-based networking, AIOps, service operations, AI governance, human oversight, and Saudi digital transformation. The analysis highlights five interdependent capabilities: context-aware intent interpretation, multi-source observability, agentic reasoning and orchestration, closed-loop execution, and governance-by-design. It is shown that autonomy is most believable when it is implemented as bounded, observable, and reversible automation rather than as unrestricted machine control. Research in the telecom field has developed well-established foundations in the areas of intent life cycles, assurance, closed loops, and zero-touch management, whereas research relating to enterprise services brings in aspects such as incident intelligence, workflow enhancement, and service quality. The review introduces an Agentic Autonomous Service Delivery Framework that combines operational agents with policy constraints, confidence thresholds, digital audit trails, human escalation, and continuous assurance. This framework provides a practical research programme for Saudi organisations that wish to establish resilient, scalable, and trustworthy AI-enabled service operations in line with Vision 2030.

title: Uncovering the Role of Artificial Intelligence in Transforming Consumer Behavior and Purchase Intention: A Systematic Bibliometric Review
summary: Digital technologies have become an essential component of contemporary business ecosystems, and digital transformation continues to reshape modern marketing strategies. In this environment, Artificial Intelligence (AI) has emerged as a key technological driver, significantly influencing how consumers search for information, evaluate alternatives, and make purchasing decisions. As AI-based applications increasingly mediate consumer–brand interactions, understanding their effects on consumer behavior and purchase intention has become an important research topic. This study conducts a bibliometric analysis to examine the evolution of academic research on AI, consumer behavior, and purchase intention over the past 33 years. Using the keywords “Artificial intelligence,” “digital transformation,” “consumer behavior,” “marketing,” and “purchase intention,” data were collected from the Scopus and Web of Science databases, resulting in a final sample of 45 peer-reviewed articles. The analysis focuses on publication trends, country contributions, and leading journals in the field. The findings reveal a clear increase in research interest after 2018, reflecting the growing use of AI in digital marketing. Overall, the results indicate that AI positively influences consumer attitudes, engagement, and purchase intention, highlighting its strategic importance and future research potential in AI-enabled marketing.

title: Antara Transparansi dan Manipulasi: Peran Fraud Pentagon dan Sustainability Disclosure dalam Financial Statement Fraud
summary: To understand what drives financial statement fraud, this study analyzes the Fraud Pentagon elements within 18 transportation and logistics companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (2020–2024), positioning sustainability disclosure as a potential moderator. By evaluating 90 firm-year observations through Moderated Regression Analysis (MRA) and measuring fraud with the modified six-ratio Beneish M-Score, the findings reveal that only opportunity (p = 0.0422) and executive arrogance (p = 0.0010) directly trigger fraudulent reporting. Meanwhile, pressure, rationalization, competence, and sustainability disclosure alone do not show direct significant effects. Interestingly, rather than acting as a universal safeguard, sustainability disclosure specifically functions as a governance mechanism that successfully constrains the negative impact of executive arrogance on fraud (p = 0.0014). The data also indicates no meaningful differences in financial pressure, fraud incidence, or sustainability practices when comparing the COVID-19 era to the post-pandemic phase. Ultimately, by integrating ESG reporting into the Fraud Pentagon during an economic transition, this research highlights that corporate transparency is a targeted accountability tool rather than a blanket cure for all fraud risks.

title: Timing matters: how hunger shapes the effectiveness of donation feedback in digital platforms
summary: Purpose As platform companies increasingly integrate digital philanthropy into corporate social responsibility initiatives, personalizing donation feedback based on user scenarios has become ever more important. However, little is known about whether feedback timing, particularly donors' physiological states, influences feedback effectiveness. Drawing on cognitive accessibility theory and the elaborated intrusion theory of desire, this research examines how donors' momentary hunger state shapes the effectiveness of donation feedback in promoting willingness to donate again. Design/methodology/approach Four experimental studies were conducted with participants recruited from Credamo (N = 883). Hunger was either manipulated or measured to distinguish between hungry and satiated donors. Participants were exposed to donation feedback and reported their willingness to donate again. Mediation and moderation analyses were conducted to examine the underlying mechanism and boundary conditions. Findings Donation feedback is more effective at promoting re-donation when donors are relatively hungry than when they are satiated. This effect is driven by an enhanced sense of achievement. Moreover, feedback information framing moderates the effect: other-benefit framing strengthens the positive impact of hunger, whereas self-benefit framing weakens it. Originality/value First, it extends donation-feedback research by identifying state-contingent feedback timing as an important determinant of feedback effectiveness. Second, it advances research on hunger and prosocial behavior by showing that hunger can heighten responsiveness to psychologically-rewarding feedback cues rather than uniformly reducing prosocial motivation. Third, it identifies sense of achievement as the underlying psychological mechanism and feedback framing as a boundary condition, while offering practical guidance for digital platforms seeking to sustain donor engagement.

title: Axiology of Basic Education in the Land of Batak: Tension Between Traditional Values of Hamoraon, Hagabeon, Hasangapon And Modernization
summary: Basic education in Batak Land has long been driven by three cultural values: Hamoraon (prosperity), Hagabeon (descendants), and Hasangapon (honor). Modernization now challenges this value system through individual aspirations, a digital economy, language shift, and weakening communal social control. This study aims to describe how the three values operate as an axiological system in basic education, to identify the tensions that modernization produces, and to formulate a model of axiological reconciliation. A qualitative library research design was used. The corpus consisted of 33 documents published between 2018 and 2026, screened against explicit criteria and analyzed through content analysis with thematic coding. The results show four strands of literature: meaning and practice of Batak values (8 documents), axiological framing (6), integration of local wisdom into curriculum (11), and modernization pressures (8). One document reports that only 30% of Batak Toba adolescents aged 15 to 18 in a Medan district maintain the language, and another reports 17 million Indonesians identifying as content creators. None of the six axiological documents was situated in a Batak community. The study concludes that the tension is a problem of interpretation and transmission rather than a clash of rival value systems. A reconciliation model combining reinterpretation of the values, curricular embedding, and community partnership is proposed, with mother-tongue value vocabulary as an enabling condition. Implications are discussed for curriculum design, teacher education, and regional education policy.

title: Exploring how intellectual capital channels the effect of multiple directorships on firm performance
summary: Purpose Drawing upon the absorptive capacity and dynamic capabilities framework, this study explores how multiple directorships shape firm performance through their influence on intellectual capital efficiency. Design/methodology/approach Based on a sample of 975 firm-year observations of Spanish listed companies over the period 2008–2020, and following previous literature, this study elucidates the role of multiple directorships in corporate governance. The analysis focuses not so much on multiple directorships as controllers but rather as coordinators, creators and disseminators of knowledge among agents by improving intellectual capital efficiency. Findings The impact of multiple directorships on firm performance is moderated partially by the efficient use of external intellectual capital resources in internal decision-making and management. Research limitations/implications The findings provide empirical support for the assumptions of the dynamic capabilities and absorptive capacity frameworks, confirming that enhancing intellectual capital efficiency is a key mechanism through which organizations leverage multiple directorships to improve performance outcomes. Practical implications Firms should develop processes and resources relating to human, structural and relational capital that enable them to capitalize on the knowledge, experience and networks of multiple directorships. Originality/value This study contributes to understanding how multiple directorships' abilities and capabilities to generate, assimilate and disseminate knowledge influence firm performance.

title: Digital Transformation in Commerce & Business Management: Emerging Trends and Future Prospects
summary: Digital transformation has emerged as a fundamental driver of change in commerce and business management, reshaping how organisations operate, compete, and create value. The integration of technologies such as artificial intelligence, cloud computing, big data analytics, blockchain, Internet of Things, automation, and digital payment systems has transformed traditional business models and consumer interactions. This paper examines the emerging trends in digital transformation and evaluates their implications for commerce and business management. It focuses on the increasing adoption of e-commerce, data-driven decision-making, intelligent automation, personalised customer experiences, digital supply chains, and platform-based business models. The study also considers challenges related to cybersecurity, data privacy, digital skills, technological costs, and organisational resistance to change. Further, it explores future prospects associated with artificial intelligence, predictive analytics, immersive technologies, and sustainable digital business practices. The paper highlights the need for organisations to develop adaptive strategies, technological capabilities, and digitally skilled human resources to achieve sustainable growth in an increasingly technology-driven business environment

title: Regarding the problem of implementing the employee's right to rest and the right to disconnect
summary: In the current conditions of the development of the digital economy, the growth of remote employment and flexible forms of work organization, the boundaries between working time and rest time are becoming increasingly blurred. This makes the issue of reviewing existing legal mechanisms and adapting them to new socio-economic realities relevant. Particular attention should be paid to the issues of establishing minimum guarantees of rest time, mechanisms for their observance by employers and means of legal protection of employees in case of violation. It is important to emphasize that the right to rest is not limited to the provision of vacation, but it’s a complex institution that includes various types of breaks, days off, holidays and other guarantees. This right doesn’t only ensure the economic stability of a person, but also affects his social, psychological and moral-physical condition. The digital revolution has changed approaches to the organization of work. Remote work, flexible schedules and constant availability of employees create new challenges for the institution of rest time. The problem of the “right to disconnect” is one of the key ones in European research. Ukrainian legislation only partially takes into account the challenges of digitalization, therefore new mechanisms for controlling working hours, ensuring an appropriate level of privacy and psychological health of employees are necessary. Another modern trend that affects the regulation of rest time is the digitalization of the labor sphere. In a world where technologies are increasingly penetrating everyday life, the issue of maintaining a balance between work and personal life is becoming particularly relevant. One of the manifestations of this balance violation is the expectation that the employee will be constantly available to the employer, even during non-working hours. This phenomenon is called the violation of the “right to disconnect”. The “right to disconnect” means the right of an employee to refuse to perform work tasks and respond to work calls, e-mails, etc. during non-working hours. This right is a logical extension of the general right to rest and is designed to protect employees from professional burnout and other negative consequences of constant availability. Given the dynamic development of the labor market, the situation of digitalization and the European integration course, the modernization of the institution of rest time is a necessary condition for improving the quality of labor relations. It is important to ensure the real, rather than formal, implementation of an employee’s rights. It should be noted that the introduction of martial law has an impact on the right to rest, its implementation and restriction give grounds for concluding that the restriction of workers' right to rest and other labor rights has necessitated ensuring the country's defense capability, since some categories of workers are involved in work to prevent or eliminate the consequences of natural disasters, epidemics, epizootics, industrial accidents and immediately eliminate their consequences; to prevent accidents that endanger or may endanger the lives or normal living conditions of people, death or damage to property. title: Digital inclusive finance and the export duration of small and medium-sized Enterprises: evidence from China
summary: Rising global uncertainty makes the sustainability of small and medium-sized enterprises’ (SMEs) export activities increasingly important. Drawing on firm-level export data from China, this study applies a discrete-time survival model to investigate how digital inclusive finance (DIF) affects SMEs’ export duration. The results show that DIF significantly reduces export hazard rates and prolongs export relationships. Financing constraints, working capital turnover, and digital transformation are potential mechanisms underlying the relationship between DIF and export duration. Heterogeneity analysis reveals significant differences across ownership and trade modes. These findings provide new evidence on how DIF shapes SMEs’ export persistence.

title: Audit Complexity dan Earning Quality: : Peran Sustainabilty Disclosure dan Audit Tenure
summary: This study examines the effect of Sustainability Disclosure and Audit Tenure on Earnings Quality, with Audit Complexity as a moderating variable. The study is motivated by the increasing demand for transparent financial reporting and the need to understand the conditions under which sustainability reporting and audit characteristics contribute to improving earnings quality. The research employs a quantitative approach using panel data from 26 energy sector companies listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange during the 2021–2024 period, resulting in 104 firm-year observations. Data were analyzed using panel data regression with the Random Effect Model selected as the most appropriate estimation model. The findings reveal that Sustainability Disclosure has a positive and significant effect on Earnings Quality, whereas Audit Tenure has no significant effect. Furthermore, Audit Complexity strengthens the positive relationship between Sustainability Disclosure and Earnings Quality, but weakens the relationship between Audit Tenure and Earnings Quality. These findings indicate that the effectiveness of sustainability disclosure in improving earnings quality depends on the level of audit complexity faced by the company. This study contributes to the development of Stakeholder Theory by demonstrating that Audit Complexity acts as a contingency factor influencing the effectiveness of corporate transparency and audit mechanisms in enhancing Earnings Quality. The findings also provide practical implications for management and auditors in improving the credibility of financial reporting, particularly in the energy sector.

title: A FRAMEWORK FOR INTERNET OF THINGS (IOT) ADOPTION AMONG STUDENTS AND STAFF OF HIGHER EDUCATION INSTITUTIONS IN KEBBI STATE, NIGERIA
summary: The Internet of Things (IoT) technologies are emerging that present great potential to transform higher education, including the concept of smart classrooms, intelligent laboratories, automated administration, campus resource management, environmental monitoring, and data-driven operations. Despite these advantages, the adoption of IoT in Nigerian higher education institutions (HEIs) particularly Kebbi State (HEIs) is still limited due to behavioural, technological, organizational and environmental factors. The study proposes the development of a UTAUT and TOE framework for modelling the adoption of IoT in Nigerian HEIs by combining the technology organization environment (TOE) and Unified theory of acceptance and use of technology (UTAUT) framework. A quantitative survey design was used and data collected from 375 respondents, which included students, academicstaff and administrative staff of the HEIs in Kebbi State. The proposed relationships were assessed using statistical analysis. Results show that the factors of Performance Expectancy (β = 0.26), Effort Expectancy (β = 0.14), Facilitating Conditions (β = 0.18), Technological Factors (β = 0.17) and Organizational Factors (β = 0.23) have significant influence on IoT adoption while Social Influence (β = 0.05, p = 0.239) and Environmental Factors (β = 0.06, p = 0.153) are not. The model accounted for 64% (R2=0.64) of the variance in IoT adoption. The results indicate that perceived benefits, ease of use, enabling conditions, technological appropriateness, and organizational capability are key factors in the adoption of IoT in the Nigerian HEIs. The study offers an integrated and parsimonious model that integrates the acceptance of individual IoT devices with the conditions for institutional adoption and offers guidance to the university administrator, ICT manager, policymakers, and other stakeholders interested in supporting sustainable digital transformation using IoT technology.

title: الحوسبة السحابية وسيادة البيانات في البلدان النامية: التحديات والمخاطر واستراتيجيات الحوكمة
summary: This paper examines the question of data sovereignty amid the rapid expansion of cloud computing adoption by developing countries, relying on services provided by major global technology firms. While these services deliver clear gains in cost reduction, accelerated digital transformation, and access to advanced infrastructure for smaller institutions, they simultaneously place the data of citizens, institutions, and governments in developing countries under legal and technical frameworks based outside their national borders. This raises fundamental questions about the actual degree of control such countries retain over their data and their capacity to safeguard strategic, security, and economic interests. The paper reviews the core concepts underlying cloud computing and data sovereignty, analyzes the state of digital adoption in developing countries, and discusses the principal legal, regulatory, technical, and economic challenges, alongside the security and geopolitical risks arising from excessive dependence on foreign providers. It also presents national and regional case studies in building legislative frameworks for data protection and storage regulation, concluding with a set of governance strategies and practical recommendations that policymakers in developing countries can draw upon to strike a balance between benefiting from cloud computing and preserving digital sovereignty.
